dimensions.label: AI data centers
dimensions.question: Should America build AI data centers as fast as possible, or slow down until electric bills, water and communities are protected?

dimensions.label: AI risk and control
dimensions.question: How dangerous is advanced AI, and how hard should the government regulate the companies building it?

dimensions.label: Big Tech regulation
dimensions.question: Should Washington rein in the big technology companies (kids safety, privacy, antitrust, Section 230), or leave them mostly alone?

dimensions.label: State AI laws
dimensions.question: Should states be allowed to pass their own AI laws, or should one national rule block them?

dimensions.label: China and AI chips
dimensions.question: Should the U.S. keep its most advanced AI chips away from China, or sell more of them abroad?

votes.title: Should states keep the right to regulate AI?
votes.plain: The House version of the 2025 Republican tax-and-spending law (H.R. 1) contained a 10-year ban on states enforcing their own AI laws. On July 1, 2025 the Senate voted on Sen. Marsha Blackburn's amendment to strip that ban out. It passed 99 to 1 after a compromise between Blackburn and Sen. Ted Cruz collapsed overnight. Because almost everyone voted yes, including Cruz, this vote alone does not tell you who supports a national rule; the positions on this site come from what members said and sponsored.
votes.yea_means: Strip the ban: states keep their power to regulate AI
votes.nay_means: Keep the 10-year ban on state AI laws

votes.title: House passes the budget bill that carried the 10-year ban on state AI laws
votes.plain: On May 22, 2025 the House passed H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, 215 to 214. Buried inside was a 10-year moratorium on state and local AI laws. This was a vote on a giant bill, so it says little about any one member's AI views. Several Republicans, including Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, later said they did not know the AI provision was in it and would have opposed it. The Senate removed the provision before the bill became law.
votes.yea_means: Pass the budget bill (with the state AI law ban inside)

votes.title: TAKE IT DOWN Act: a federal crime to post AI sexual deepfakes without consent
votes.plain: The TAKE IT DOWN Act makes it a federal crime to publish real or AI-generated sexual images of a person without consent and forces platforms to remove them within 48 hours of a request. The House passed it 409 to 2 on April 28, 2025 and President Trump signed it in May 2025. The two no votes were Reps. Thomas Massie and Eric Burlison, who cited free speech and government overreach concerns.

votes.title: KIDS Act: the Republican kids-online-safety package, with AI chatbot rules
votes.plain: On June 29, 2026 the House passed the KIDS Act 267 to 117. The Republican-led package bundled kids' online safety rules, app store age checks and new rules for AI chatbots that talk to minors. Most Democrats voted no, arguing it was a weaker substitute for the Senate's Kids Online Safety Act and gave tech companies too much cover; a yes vote here reads as support for the GOP approach, not necessarily as pro or anti regulation.
votes.yea_means: Pass the House GOP kids-safety and chatbot package
votes.nay_means: Reject it (most Democrats wanted the stronger Senate KOSA)

votes.title: Remote Access Security Act: close the cloud loophole in AI chip export controls
votes.plain: Export controls stop China from buying America's most advanced AI chips, but Chinese firms could still rent the same chips remotely through the cloud. This bill lets the Commerce Department control that remote access too. The House passed it 369 to 22 on January 12, 2026.
votes.yea_means: Tighten controls on Chinese access to U.S. AI chips

votes.title: Repeal the consumer watchdog's oversight of Big Tech payment apps
votes.plain: In late 2024 the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau finalized a rule letting it supervise large digital payment apps (Apple Pay, Google Pay, Venmo, Cash App) the way it supervises banks. On March 5, 2025 the Senate voted 51 to 47, along party lines, to repeal that rule; the House agreed 219 to 211 in April and the repeal became law. A yes vote was a vote for lighter oversight of Big Tech's financial products.
votes.yea_means: Repeal the oversight rule (lighter touch on Big Tech)
votes.nay_means: Keep the watchdog's oversight of payment apps

votes.title: House vote to repeal the consumer watchdog's oversight of Big Tech payment apps
votes.plain: The House companion vote on April 9, 2025 (219 to 211) to the Senate repeal of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's rule supervising large digital payment apps. See the Senate vote above for the background.
votes.yea_means: Repeal the oversight rule (lighter touch on Big Tech)
votes.nay_means: Keep the watchdog's oversight of payment apps

votes.title: Kids Online Safety Act passes the Senate (2024)
votes.plain: The Kids Online Safety Act would give social media companies a legal duty of care to protect children from bullying, sexual exploitation and content that promotes self-harm, and let parents turn off addictive features. The Senate passed it 91 to 3 on July 30, 2024 (Sens. Wyden, Paul and Lee voted no, citing free-speech and censorship concerns). The House never took it up that year, and the fight over a House version continued into 2026.
votes.yea_means: Pass kids' online safety rules for social media

votes.title: Force TikTok's Chinese owner to sell or face a U.S. ban
votes.plain: On March 13, 2024 the House voted 352 to 65 to require ByteDance to sell TikTok or see the app banned in the United States. A version of the measure became law the following month. The no votes came from both parties: progressives worried about free speech and some Republicans who opposed the precedent of banning an app.
votes.yea_means: Force a sale or ban of TikTok
votes.nay_means: Oppose the forced sale or ban

votes.title: Stop the government from buying Americans' data from brokers
votes.plain: The Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act would stop law enforcement and intelligence agencies from buying Americans' location and browsing data from data brokers without a warrant. The House passed it 219 to 199 on April 17, 2024 with an unusual coalition of privacy-minded Republicans and Democrats; the Senate never voted on it.
votes.yea_means: Ban warrantless government purchases of personal data

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: As the DFL nominee for governor she says data centers raise electric rates and hurt the environment, wants local control, strong state standards, full cost recovery from developers and an end to secret NDAs. She has not endorsed a moratorium and did not answer directly when asked about local moratoria.

evidence.title: KFGO radio interview: Klobuchar on data centers as candidate for governor
evidence.quote: Cause people's rates to go up, they have hurt the environment, and that just can't keep happening. So my answer to this is number one, local control.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own words: data centers are a rate and environmental problem, and locals should decide; she also said NDAs with officials should not be happening.

evidence.title: West Central Tribune candidate survey on data centers
evidence.quote: If Minnesotans don't want a data center in their community, I don't want it there either.
evidence.what_it_shows: She would require projects to cover 100 percent of energy and grid costs, disclose power and water demand before local approval, and report annually; she attacked her opponent for blocking an NDA ban.

evidence.title: Minnesota Reformer questionnaire: spokesman on Klobuchar's data center position
evidence.quote: The Senator supports robust environmental standards for any proposed data centers as well as greater transparency and local control over decisions to build
evidence.what_it_shows: Her campaign backs the 2025 state law making data centers pay full energy costs but did not answer the paper's direct questions about local moratoria or NDAs.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: She has pushed specific AI rules for years (deepfakes, election ads, whistleblowers, chatbots and toys, AI scams, gene synthesis screening) and is now the lead Democrat on a Senate bill for government oversight of the most dangerous frontier models. Safety advocates and Sen. Cantwell say her draft leans on company self-testing, so she sits between targeted guardrails and strict rules.

evidence.title: Nextgov: Klobuchar statement on the Cruz-Thune-Klobuchar frontier AI bill
evidence.quote: That includes requiring developers to work with government experts to verify and test models to make sure AI is safe. We cannot allow the release of dangerous models, including those that evade the control of their developers.
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants binding government oversight of the riskiest models, but a Democratic committee aide called the draft 'primarily a voluntary standard type situation' and Cantwell is demanding mandatory national lab testing.

evidence.title: Press release: Klobuchar questions Sam Altman and Brad Smith at Senate Commerce AI hearing
evidence.quote: We want it to lead us to heaven, and I think we do that by making sure we have some rules of the road in place
evidence.what_it_shows: She framed her Thune bill as risk-based 'basic guardrails for the riskiest non-defense applications of AI' and got Altman to agree a risk-based approach is right.

evidence.title: Letter: Cantwell, Klobuchar, Markey ask CPSC to address AI chatbots in children's toys
evidence.quote: It is imperative that the manufacturers of these technologies be required to mitigate these risks before marketing toys to young children.
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants mandatory risk mitigation before AI toys reach kids, a targeted binding rule.

evidence.title: Transcript: Senate Judiciary hearing 'Examining the Harm of AI Chatbots'
evidence.quote: One of the things that we know about these AI chatbots is that they are frequently designed to tell users what they want to hear
evidence.what_it_shows: She pressed grieving parents and experts on addictive companion bot design and whether parents should have a right to see their children's chatbot conversations.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1792 AI Whistleblower Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs protecting AI company workers who report safety problems to the government.

evidence.title: ARI release: Cotton and Klobuchar introduce Biosecurity Modernization and Innovation Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Her bipartisan bill would make mandatory the screening of synthetic DNA orders, aimed at AI lowering the barrier to designing dangerous pathogens.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.1213 Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would ban AI deepfakes of candidates meant to deceive voters, one of several election AI bills she leads.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4591 NO FAKES Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a federal right to stop unauthorized AI copies of a person's voice and face; Roll Call named her a particular proponent when Judiciary advanced it in June 2026.

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on AI chatbot policies permitting 'romantic or sensual' conversations with children
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators demanded details on how Meta's chatbot safety policies for minors were developed, asked for more visible disclosures and a ban on targeted ads to under-18 users, writing that 'the wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.'

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: A long-time Big Tech antitrust hawk who sponsors the main Senate antitrust reform bill, backs sunsetting Section 230, and cosponsors KOSA, COPPA 2.0 and the STOP CSAM Act. She says courts and current law are not enough and Congress must write new rules for dominant platforms.

evidence.title: Press release: Klobuchar statement on the Google antitrust remedy decision
evidence.quote: Today's ruling is a reminder of Google's sweeping power over the online economy, but the limited remedies ordered by the court demonstrate why we need additional rules of the road for Big Tech.
evidence.what_it_shows: She used the Google ruling to push her American Innovation and Choice Online Act against self-preferencing by dominant platforms.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.130 Competition and Antitrust Law Enforcement Reform Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Her flagship bill would make big mergers harder and shift the burden to the largest companies.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3546 Sunset Section 230 Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would end platforms' liability shield in two years to force Congress to write new rules.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care for platforms toward minors.

evidence.title: Opening remarks at Judiciary subcommittee hearing on Meta whistleblowers and child safety
evidence.quote: Well, sorry is not enough anymore, and we need to put in some rules of the road to stop this from happening.
evidence.what_it_shows: As subcommittee ranking member she accused Meta of hiding child safety research and called for bipartisan rules.

evidence.title: Letter to DOJ and FTC urging antitrust probe of generative AI features on dominant platforms
evidence.quote: we urge the Department of Justice Antitrust Division and the Federal Trade Commission to investigate whether the design of some generative AI features, introduced by already dominant platforms, are a form of exclusionary conduct
evidence.what_it_shows: She led seven Democrats asking enforcers to treat AI summaries that keep users on Google and Meta as possible antitrust violations harming journalists.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.146 TAKE IT DOWN Act (now law)
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-authored with Sen. Cruz the law forcing platforms to remove nonconsensual intimate images and deepfakes within 48 hours.

evidence.title: Schatz-led bipartisan letter of 10 senators to Zuckerberg on safeguards for children using Meta AI chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators told Meta they were 'alarmed' by its chatbot policies, asked how its minor-safety rules were developed, and demanded Meta ban targeted ads to under-18s, improve disclosures and add mental-health referrals.

evidence.title: Cruz and Klobuchar statements marking one year of the TAKE IT DOWN Act as FTC enforcement begins
evidence.what_it_shows: The law's authors said platforms must now remove nonconsensual intimate images and deepfakes within 48 hours, with Cruz saying 'Big Tech can no longer look the other way' and Klobuchar noting platforms can no longer 'turn a blind eye.'

preemption.label: Leans states
preemption.summary: She cosponsored the States' Right to Regulate AI Act and wrote a New York Times op-ed arguing state AI laws keep people safe against Trump's preemption push. At the same time she is negotiating a national AI framework with Sens. Cruz and Thune that Sen. Cantwell warns would set a weak federal standard undermining state laws, so her final line on preemption depends on that bill.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3557 States' Right to Regulate AI Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Original cosponsor of Sen. Markey's bill saying the federal government cannot wipe out state AI rules; joined a week after the Dec. 11 executive order.

evidence.title: New York Times op-ed: 'State A.I. Laws Keep Us Safe. Trump's Next Move Could Upend That.'
evidence.what_it_shows: Headline seen via Google News; the page itself was blocked, so no verbatim text. The op-ed argued against Trump's planned executive order overriding state AI laws.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium from H.R. 1
evidence.what_it_shows: Joined the 99-1 vote to remove the moratorium; nearly every senator voted the same way, so the vote alone says little. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: Nextgov: Klobuchar co-leading Cruz-Thune-Klobuchar national AI bill; Cantwell objects
evidence.quote: I'm continuing to work toward a bipartisan agreement on legislation for government oversight of the greatest risks posed by AI models
evidence.what_it_shows: Contradictory signal: she is drafting the national framework Republicans want; Cantwell posted that she opposes a 'weak federal standard' that undermines existing state AI legislation, so preemption terms remain the fight.

evidence.title: Cantwell and Senate Commerce Committee Democrats letter to Chairman Cruz demanding a markup of the reconciliation Commerce title, flagging the AI moratorium
evidence.what_it_shows: Twelve Commerce Committee Democrats told Cruz the AI moratorium 'tramples states' rights and holds the $42 billion BEAD program hostage' and asked for regular committee consideration instead of a fast-tracked floor vote.

china_chips.label: No public position found
china_chips.summary: No public position found on chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China as of Sept 2026. Searches for Nvidia, H20/H200, export controls, Chip Security Act and GAIN AI returned only news of her support for CHIPS Act grants to Minnesota chip factories, which is about domestic manufacturing, not export policy.

data_centers.label: Pause or block
data_centers.summary: Sanders wants a federal moratorium on new AI data centers and wrote the Senate bill to impose one. He says data centers raise electricity prices, strain water supplies and harm the environment, and that democracy needs time to catch up with the technology.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.4214, Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He is the Senate author of the bill to halt new AI data centers until national safeguards on safety, jobs and utility prices are in place; it had no Senate cosponsors as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Press release: Sanders, Ocasio-Cortez announce AI Data Center Moratorium Act
evidence.quote: We need serious public debate and democratic oversight over this enormously consequential issue. The time for action is now. We need a federal moratorium on AI data centers.
evidence.what_it_shows: His own words announcing the bill; the release says the moratorium should last until safeguards ensure AI does not raise electricity or utility prices or harm communities.

evidence.title: Press release: Sanders: Yes. We Need a Moratorium On Data Center Construction.
evidence.quote: The local officials who are supporting a moratorium are right: data centers will have a profound impact on land and water use, and will drive up electricity costs.
evidence.what_it_shows: He applauded Denver's local data center moratorium and repeated his call for a federal one, citing land, water and electricity costs.

evidence.title: Fox News op-ed: Yes, we must hit the pause button on AI before it is too late
evidence.quote: AI data centers are raising electricity prices, straining water systems and harming the environment. That is why 75% of Americans oppose data centers near where they live
evidence.what_it_shows: He ties data centers to household power bills and local opposition, and frames them as part of the case for pausing AI.

evidence.title: Video on social media endorsing a national data center moratorium, as reported by E&E News
evidence.quote: This moratorium will give democracy a chance to catch up, and ensure that the benefits of these technologies work for all of us, not just the wealthiest people on Earth
evidence.what_it_shows: E&E News reported he was likely the first member of Congress to endorse a national halt on data center construction.

evidence.title: HuffPost Q&A with Sanders on responding to the threat of AI
evidence.quote: Six months ago, [Rep.] Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and I introduced legislation calling for a moratorium on data center construction, and we were thought crazy, radical.
evidence.what_it_shows: He argues the moratorium idea has moved from the fringe to the mainstream as communities and governors turn against data centers.

evidence.title: Markey-McClellan bicameral letter to EPA urging withdrawal of proposed rule letting data centers and power plants begin construction before air permits
evidence.what_it_shows: Sixteen lawmakers told EPA to withdraw its May 2026 proposal redefining 'begin actual construction' so data centers and fossil plants can pour foundations and install wiring before New Source Review permits, saying it turns the Clean Air Act's preconstruction safeguards 'on its head.'

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Sanders treats advanced AI as a possible existential threat. He wants an immediate pause on frontier AI development, a permanent ban on superintelligence enforced by a new cabinet-level agency with prison terms for violators, and he has told AI CEOs the Senate will act if they do not pause on their own.

evidence.title: Press release: Sanders, Casar to introduce legislation to ban artificial superintelligence and temporarily pause advanced AI development
evidence.quote: It is irresponsible for society to allow them to move forward and make these products even more advanced. That’s why I am introducing legislation to immediately pause the development of increasingly powerful AI
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would permanently ban superintelligent AI, pause advanced AI development until a new federal regulator sets rules, and set penalties of up to 20 years in prison.

evidence.title: Press release: Sanders calls on tech giants to pause development of out-of-control AI (letter to Anthropic, Meta and OpenAI)
evidence.quote: In the interest of humanity, stand by your words. Pause AI development. It is not too late to avoid disaster. Stop building machines that humans cannot control.
evidence.what_it_shows: He demanded a voluntary pause after reports of AI systems escaping human control and warned that if the companies do not act, the Senate will.

evidence.title: Op-ed in The Guardian: AI poses unprecedented threats. Congress must act now
evidence.quote: there is a very real fear that, in the not-so-distant future, a super-intelligent AI could replace humans in controlling the planet.
evidence.what_it_shows: As HELP ranking member he launched an investigation into AI and said loss of human control is a real danger that Congress must address.

evidence.title: Fox News op-ed: Yes, we must hit the pause button on AI before it is too late
evidence.quote: These CEOs must immediately pause the development of increasingly powerful AI. And that pause must be international in scope.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants a pause that covers other countries too, comparing the moment to Reagan and Gorbachev on nuclear arms control.

evidence.title: HuffPost Q&A with Sanders on responding to the threat of AI
evidence.quote: How in God’s name can you keep going forward in the direction of superintelligence when you don’t know what that means?
evidence.what_it_shows: He says the pause idea is gaining support and that he is hosting a closed-door Senate briefing on Sept 16, 2026 with leading AI scientists on runaway AI.

evidence.title: Post responding to Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon's resignation warning, as reported by The Hill
evidence.quote: The very people building this technology admit that it could threaten the future of humanity. That is why I will soon be introducing legislation to ban superintelligence and pause AI development.
evidence.what_it_shows: He used a viral extinction warning from an AI researcher to push his superintelligence ban.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1394 (118th), Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for a hard rule keeping humans in control of nuclear launch decisions.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.681 (118th), Facial Recognition and Biometric Technology Moratorium Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed a moratorium on federal use of face recognition until Congress sets rules.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: Sanders casts Big Tech leaders as oligarchs and wants structural change: a 50% public ownership stake in the largest AI companies with forced break-ups of their AI and non-AI businesses, plus curbs on robocalls, worker surveillance and rent-setting algorithms. He has said less about Section 230 or specific antitrust cases.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.4825, American A.I. Sovereign Wealth Fund Act
evidence.what_it_shows: A one-time 50% tax on the stock of the biggest AI companies would go into a public fund with voting shares, and companies mixing AI and non-AI lines would have to split them.

evidence.title: Press release: Sanders introduces legislation to create $7 trillion AI sovereign wealth fund
evidence.quote: As a society, we can no longer sit back and allow a handful of Big Tech oligarchs to determine the future of this revolutionary technology with no democratic input.
evidence.what_it_shows: His own framing of the bill: public control over Big Tech's AI decisions, including a requirement to break up combined AI and non-AI businesses.

evidence.title: Press release: Sanders releases report on Big Tech oligarchs' war against workers
evidence.quote: But it will not happen if decisions are made in boardrooms by billionaires who only care about short-term profits. Congress must ensure that AI and automation benefit workers, not just corporate CEOs and Wall Street.
evidence.what_it_shows: His HELP Committee report proposes a robot tax, profit sharing, a 32-hour week and other mandates on corporations deploying AI.

evidence.title: HuffPost Q&A with Sanders on responding to the threat of AI
evidence.quote: The AI industry is owned by the wealthiest people in the world, they are prepared this election to spend hundreds of millions of dollars to make sure that Congress does not do the right thing
evidence.what_it_shows: He blames AI industry campaign spending for Congress's reluctance to regulate.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4307, Protecting American Consumers from Robocalls Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports tougher rules and penalties on spam robocalls.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.262 (118th), Stop Spying Bosses Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would limit secret electronic monitoring of workers and require disclosure of data collected.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3692 (118th), Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Treats shared rent-setting software as illegal price fixing.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Sanders wants states free to regulate AI. He cosponsored the States' Right to Regulate AI Act to block Trump's December 2025 executive order and attacked the order as a favor to Big Tech oligarchs. His Yea on the July 2025 vote to strip the state-law moratorium matched 98 other senators and is weak evidence on its own.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3557, States' Right to Regulate AI Act
evidence.what_it_shows: The bill says states keep their power to pass AI rules and would stop the administration from carrying out the preemption executive order.

evidence.title: Op-ed in The Guardian: AI poses unprecedented threats. Congress must act now
evidence.quote: Why does Donald Trump, who is strongly supporting the big tech oligarchs, want to impose an executive order blocking states from regulating artificial intelligence?
evidence.what_it_shows: He criticized the planned executive order to override state AI laws days before it was signed.

evidence.title: Press release (Sen. Welch): Welch joins legislation to block Trump's illegal executive order undermining AI state safeguards, listing Sanders as cosponsor
evidence.what_it_shows: Confirms Sanders joined the Markey bill filed as an appropriations amendment to prohibit implementation of the preemption executive order.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on Senate roll call 363, Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted with the 99-1 majority to remove the state AI-law moratorium; nearly every senator did, so this alone is not strong evidence. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Sanders has not taken a position on Nvidia chip sales to China. His data center bill would ban exports of AI computing gear to any country lacking safety and labor safeguards, and his superintelligence ban lists export controls as a tool to stop superintelligence anywhere. At the same time he wants Washington and Beijing to negotiate an AI safety treaty rather than race each other.

evidence.title: Press release: Sanders, Ocasio-Cortez announce AI Data Center Moratorium Act
evidence.quote: It accomplishes this by banning U.S. exports of AI computing infrastructure to countries that do not have safeguards in place to guarantee AI is safe and effective, workers are protected and AI does not harm the environment.
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would restrict AI hardware exports on safety grounds, which would cover China, but it is not framed around the chip race.

evidence.title: Press release: Sanders, Casar to introduce legislation to ban artificial superintelligence
evidence.quote: pursue international agreements, allied coordination, and policies such as export controls to prevent the development of artificial superintelligence anywhere in the world.
evidence.what_it_shows: He sees export controls as one lever to stop dangerous AI abroad, again on safety rather than competition grounds.

evidence.title: Press release: Sanders statement on upcoming U.S.-China AI talks
evidence.quote: Trump and Xi must seize this moment to make clear that humans, not machines, come first.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Whitehouse is the Senate's leading voice for making AI data centers pay their own way. He wrote the Clean Cloud Act to charge big data centers for dirty power, led letters to protect New England electric customers, and is pressing EPA to act on xAI's unpermitted gas turbines. He says the U.S. can lead on AI and climate at the same time, and he was open to a permitting deal to speed grid upgrades.

evidence.title: S.1475 Clean Cloud Act of 2025 (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill would have EPA set an emissions standard for data centers and crypto mines and charge them a rising fee when their power is too dirty, with a quarter of the money going to low-income ratepayers.

evidence.title: Press release: Whitehouse, Fetterman introduce Clean Cloud Act
evidence.quote: The good news is that we don't have to choose between leading the world on AI and leading the world on climate safety: big technology and AI companies have all the money in the world to pay for developing new sources of clean energy, rather than overloading local grids and firing up fossil fuel pollution.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he blames data centers for higher electric bills and more pollution, and wants tech companies to pay for new clean power.

evidence.title: Letter: Reed and Whitehouse lead six New England senators asking ISO New England how it will protect ratepayers from data center costs
evidence.quote: We believe it is necessary to require tech companies, not American families, to foot the bill for their load.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants the grid operator to make data center owners, not households, pay for the power demand they add.

evidence.title: Letter: Whitehouse and colleagues urge Biden White House to reconsider fast-tracking AI data centers
evidence.quote: we urge you to uphold critical clean air and water standards and ensure that the energy needs of technology companies are not prioritized over the needs of households
evidence.what_it_shows: Even under a Democratic president he opposed speeding up data center construction if it meant weaker pollution rules or higher household bills.

evidence.title: Letter: Whitehouse, Heinrich and Van Hollen probe nine companies over gas-powered AI data centers (Latitude Media)
evidence.quote: Gas turbines are not the only option for data center developers looking to meet booming demand
evidence.what_it_shows: He is investigating Meta, OpenAI, xAI and others over plans to run AI data centers on gas plants, pushing them toward cleaner power.

evidence.title: Letter: Whitehouse asks EPA to take enforcement action against xAI's Memphis-area data center (E&E News)
evidence.quote: xAI's strategy of installing turbines first and seeking permits after the fact is clearly illegal
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants federal regulators to crack down on an AI company that ran gas turbines without air permits.

evidence.title: Politico: Whitehouse and Heinrich joint statement as Senate Democrats end permitting reform talks
evidence.quote: There was a deal to be had that would have taken politics out of permitting, made the process faster and more efficient, and streamlined grid infrastructure improvements nationwide
evidence.what_it_shows: He was willing to speed up permitting for grid projects, so he is not against building, but walked away after the administration attacked offshore wind.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Whitehouse backs targeted AI rules: keeping kids away from AI companion chatbots, banning AI fakes that trick voters, and bias testing for automated decision systems. No statement was found calling advanced AI an existential danger or seeking licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: S.3062 GUARD Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring AI chatbot companies to verify ages and keep minors away from AI companion bots.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Senate Judiciary advances GUARD Act; Whitehouse ties kids' chatbot safety to repealing Section 230
evidence.what_it_shows: During the committee markup of the chatbot bill he argued Congress should also protect kids on other online platforms by repealing the Section 230 liability shield.

evidence.title: S.4774 Fraudulent Artificial Intelligence Regulations (FAIR) Elections Act of 2026 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports rules against using AI-made fake video and audio to deceive voters.

evidence.title: S.2892 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed making big companies test automated decision systems for bias and harm and report results to the FTC.

evidence.title: S.2325 Algorithmic Justice and Online Platform Transparency Act (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed transparency rules for the algorithms that pick what people see online and a ban on discriminatory algorithms.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: Whitehouse wants to rein in Big Tech. He is a lead cosponsor of the bipartisan bill to repeal Section 230, backs tougher antitrust law against giant mergers, and supports the Kids Online Safety Act and the EARN IT Act.

evidence.title: S.3546 Sunset Section 230 Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports ending the law that shields online platforms from lawsuits over user content.

evidence.title: Uprise RI: Whitehouse announces he is filing a bipartisan Section 230 repeal with Sen. Graham
evidence.quote: At long last, we are proceeding to file a bipartisan Section 230 repeal
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he has pushed for years to strip platforms of their legal immunity.

evidence.title: S.130 Competition and Antitrust Law Enforcement Reform Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making it harder for giant companies, including Big Tech, to merge.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care requiring apps and platforms to protect minors.

evidence.title: S.1207 EARN IT Act of 2023 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed removing platforms' legal shield when they allow child sexual abuse material to spread.

evidence.title: S.1094 Journalism Competition and Preservation Act of 2023 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed letting news outlets bargain together to make Google and Facebook pay for their stories.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Barrasso wants data centers and the power plants behind them built fast: he praised Trump's AI Action Plan for tearing down barriers to new data centers and is pushing a bill to break federal permitting bottlenecks. His one caveat is that data centers on federal land should get state and local input.

evidence.title: Senate floor speech: Barrasso: Whoever Powers the AI Revolution Will Win the AI Arms Race
evidence.quote: It tears down barriers to building new data centers. It encourages more private investment. Most importantly, it recognizes that America's AI future depends on America's energy future.
evidence.what_it_shows: He celebrates the White House plan for removing obstacles to data center construction and ties it to Wyoming coal, gas and uranium.

evidence.title: Senate floor speech: Barrasso Calls on Senate to Fix America's Costly, Complex, and Cumbersome Permitting Process
evidence.quote: I will soon introduce legislation to break the bottlenecks in federal permitting. That is the number one way to boost American energy and mineral dominance.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants NEPA deadlines and limits on lawsuits so energy projects for the AI demand surge get built faster.

evidence.title: Cowboy State Daily: Developers Now Targeting Public Lands To Build Huge AI Data Centers (Barrasso comment)
evidence.quote: Development of federal land, including the construction of new data centers, deserves meaningful input from state and local governments and the public
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports the AI buildout but attaches a condition of local input when data centers go on federal land.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Barrasso treats AI as an arms race with China and applauds cutting regulations on AI developers. His stated AI worries are political bias in chatbots and Chinese theft of research, not safety rules on advanced models, though he did cosponsor the TAKE IT DOWN Act against AI sexual deepfakes.

evidence.title: Senate floor speech: Barrasso: Whoever Powers the AI Revolution Will Win the AI Arms Race
evidence.quote: President Trump recently announced an AI Action Plan. It releases American innovators from painful, punishing regulations.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI regulation as a burden to be lifted and puts winning the race with China first.

evidence.title: Senate Energy Committee hearing remarks: Barrasso: With Growth of AI and Other Critical Technologies, Labs Must Take China Threat Seriously
evidence.quote: We can't let political bias infiltrate development of AI. This is particularly true when taxpayer dollars are helping fund the technology's development.
evidence.what_it_shows: His AI concern is left-wing bias in chatbots like ChatGPT and security of taxpayer-funded research, not existential risk.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.146 TAKE IT DOWN Act (now law)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed a targeted guardrail making AI-faked intimate images a crime, a narrow exception to his hands-off tone.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Barrasso backs targeted rules on tech companies, especially for kids: he cosponsored the Kids Online Safety Act, the Digital Age Assurance Act, the TAKE IT DOWN Act and a ban on Chinese-linked connected cars. He has not called for breaking up Big Tech or repealing Section 230.

evidence.what_it_shows: He joined the major bipartisan bill requiring platforms to protect minors.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.5090 Digital Age Assurance Act of 2026

evidence.what_it_shows: Trade press confirms Barrasso as a sponsor of a new federal kids online safety mandate.

evidence.what_it_shows: He backed platform transparency rules on content moderation, a targeted Section 230 fix rather than repeal.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1094 Journalism Competition and Preservation Act (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported letting news outlets bargain collectively with Google and Facebook.

members.signature: Senate Majority Whip who frames AI as an arms race with China that Wyoming coal, gas and uranium should power; pushes permitting reform and praised Trump's AI Action Plan for cutting rules on data centers.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: McConnell cheered the Trump administration's choice of the DOE Paducah site for a giant AI data center and power campus, and had pushed the Energy Department on the site for years. He has not publicly raised electric-bill, water or local-control conditions as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Press release: McConnell praises Trump's selection of Paducah DOE site as future home of AI infrastructure
evidence.quote: This is great news for the Paducah community, and I want to thank President Trump for selecting the Paducah site to host new AI infrastructure
evidence.what_it_shows: He celebrated a hyperscale AI campus coming to Kentucky and thanked the president for it, with no mention of ratepayer or community conditions.

evidence.title: Press release: McConnell statement on confirmation of Energy Secretary Chris Wright
evidence.quote: I look forward to working with Secretary Wright to move our country toward greater energy dominance and to support the agency’s job-creating policies, like their work at the Department of Energy site in Paducah, Kentucky.
evidence.what_it_shows: Months before the AI site selection he was already lobbying the new Energy Secretary to develop the Paducah DOE site, the project that became the $100B AI hub.

ai_risk.label: No public position found
ai_risk.summary: No public statements found on AI safety rules, chatbots, deepfakes or AI regulation as of Sept 2026. Searches of his press releases, floor remarks and Kentucky press turned up only coverage of a disputed July 2026 hospital photo that critics claimed was AI-generated, which is not a policy position.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: McConnell backed the 2024 law forcing TikTok's Chinese owner to sell or face a ban and filed a Supreme Court brief defending it, framing it as a national-security rule on conduct, not speech. Beyond that one China-focused fix, no positions found on Section 230, antitrust or kids' online safety in this period.

evidence.title: Senate floor speech: McConnell endorses TikTok divest-or-ban bill
evidence.quote: This is a matter that deserves Congress’ urgent attention. And I’ll support commonsense, bipartisan steps to take one of Beijing’s favorite tools of coercion and espionage off the table.
evidence.what_it_shows: As Senate Republican leader he threw his weight behind forcing a Chinese-owned platform to divest, a targeted rule on one company rather than broad Big Tech regulation.

evidence.title: Amicus brief: McConnell urged the Supreme Court to uphold the TikTok ban-or-divest law
evidence.quote: The right to free speech enshrined in the First Amendment does not apply to a corporate agent of the Chinese Communist Party.
evidence.what_it_shows: He kept pushing the TikTok law through the courts and argued it does not violate the First Amendment.

preemption.label: No public position found

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Merkley wants data centers to grow only with protections for electric bills, water, farmland, tribal rights and public transparency. He acknowledges their national security and union-job value but his one major action is a joint letter with Wyden urging Oregon's advisory committee to protect ratepayers and communities.

evidence.title: Letter: Wyden and Merkley to Gov. Kotek's Data Center Advisory Committee
evidence.quote: your work to strike a balance between pursuing economic development opportunities in alignment with sustainable utility costs and environmental impacts is critical for Oregon and the Northwest
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked the state panel to address rising electricity costs for consumers, water use, farmland rezoning, tribal rights and transparency, while calling data centers critical to national security and union jobs.

evidence.title: Same letter: list of concerns the senators asked the committee to weigh
evidence.quote: Increasing electricity costs for consumers because of increased demand.
evidence.what_it_shows: Ratepayer costs were listed first among the concerns he wants the state to solve before data centers expand.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Merkley is one of the Senate's most persistent critics of government facial recognition and AI surveillance, and he wants binding rules against AI misuse in elections. His focus is targeted guardrails on specific harms, not frontier AI licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: KATU: Wyden, Merkley introduce ICE Out of Our Faces Act to bar ICE and CBP facial recognition
evidence.quote: Without oversight, this technology is dangerous in the hands of any government, and the Trump Administration is abusing it to trample on privacy, freedom of speech, and civil liberties.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants a statutory ban on federal immigration agencies using face recognition and other biometric AI.

evidence.title: Democracy Docket: Merkley introduces the FAIR Elections Act on AI and voter suppression
evidence.quote: The ballot box is the beating heart of democracy, and we must use every tool at our disposal to protect it
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would prohibit AI-generated content used to intimidate election officials or spread false voting information.

evidence.title: S.4774 Fraudulent Artificial Intelligence Regulations (FAIR) Elections Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: He sponsors a bill setting binding rules against AI deepfakes and AI-driven disinformation in federal elections.

evidence.title: FedScoop: Senators want TSA to scale back facial recognition at airports (Traveler Privacy Protection Act)
evidence.quote: Folks don’t want a national surveillance state, but that’s exactly what the TSA’s unchecked expansion of facial recognition technology is leading us to
evidence.what_it_shows: He leads the bipartisan bill to make TSA face scans opt-in and has pushed a watchdog audit of the program.

evidence.title: S.1691 Traveler Privacy Protection Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill requires airport security to get consent before scanning travelers' faces.

evidence.title: S.2164 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs mandatory bias and harm testing of automated decision systems by large companies.

evidence.title: S.3308 Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports banning discriminatory uses of AI and requiring bias testing.

evidence.title: S.1394 Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants a legal guarantee that only humans, never AI, can order a nuclear launch.

evidence.title: S.681 Facial Recognition and Biometric Technology Moratorium Act of 2023 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He has long backed pausing federal use of face recognition until Congress writes rules.

evidence.title: Press release (Quiver copy): Wyden and Merkley request transparency from Meta on facial recognition in smart glasses
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed Meta on plans to add face recognition to consumer glasses, warning it could normalize mass surveillance; answers were due April 6, 2026.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Merkley backs specific rules on Big Tech: kids' online safety and privacy laws, takedowns of voting lies, liability for fake goods on marketplaces, and limits on health data collection. He has not called for break-ups or repeal of Section 230.

evidence.title: S.836 Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA 2.0)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports requiring consent before companies collect data on kids and teens and banning targeted ads to them.

evidence.title: S.1409 Kids Online Safety Act (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He cosponsored the main bill imposing a duty of care on platforms toward minors.

evidence.title: S.840 Digital Integrity in Democracy Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants large platforms required to quickly remove false information about how to vote.

evidence.title: S.2934 SHOP SAFE Act of 2023 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He would make online marketplaces liable for counterfeit goods unless they vet sellers.

evidence.title: S.1656 My Body, My Data Act of 2023 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports limits on collecting and selling reproductive health data.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No public position found. I searched for Merkley statements on the 10-year state AI law moratorium, the Dec 2025 executive order, the March 2026 White House framework and the States' Right to Regulate AI Act, and found none; he did not cosponsor S.3557. His Yea on the 99-1 strike vote matched nearly the whole Senate and is not evidence on its own.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted with 98 other senators to remove the moratorium after the deal collapsed; the vote alone does not show a settled view on preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Merkley signed a November 2025 letter urging the Trump administration to restore export controls on advanced AI chips that were suspended in trade talks with China. That is his only located action on chip export policy.

evidence.title: Press release: Wyden, Schumer, Warren, Cortez Masto press Trump to restore export controls after trade talks (Merkley a signer)
evidence.quote: Trump struck a deal that suspended the ability of the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) to enforce export controls on key technologies, including American-made advanced AI chips.
evidence.what_it_shows: The release names Merkley as a signer of the letter demanding the administration reverse the suspension of chip export controls; the quoted line is the release's description, not Merkley's own words.

members.signature: Longtime critic of facial recognition and government surveillance who now pushes bans on TSA and ICE face scanning, an AI-in-elections bill, and data center guardrails with Wyden.

quote.text: For years, I’ve been ringing the alarm bells about the dangers of a national surveillance state built on facial recognition technology.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Reed led a letter from six New England senators asking the regional grid operator how it will keep AI data centers from raising household electric bills, saying the AI industry should pay those costs. He also wants the AI buildout to happen in America rather than the Middle East, so he is not against building data centers.

evidence.title: Letter: Reed and Whitehouse lead six New England senators asking ISO New England how it will protect ratepayers from data center costs
evidence.quote: As the ones who stand to benefit most, the multi-billion-dollar AI industry should be responsible for these costs.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants tech companies, not families, to pay for the grid costs data centers create.

evidence.title: Joint statement of Reed, Coons, Shaheen, Warner, Kelly, Himes and Krishnamoorthi on Trump's UAE and Saudi AI chip deals
evidence.quote: Under this deal, data centers and AI systems that would otherwise be built in America will be built in the Middle East
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats data centers as valuable infrastructure that should be built in the U.S., which tempers his ratepayer concerns.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Reed has said since 2023 that AI needs federal regulation done quickly but carefully. His main work is on military AI: he co-wrote a bill requiring human oversight and a manual override for AI weapons and barring AI from nuclear launch decisions, much of which the Senate Armed Services Committee folded into its 2027 defense bill. He also backed an office to check the most powerful AI models for serious dangers.

evidence.title: S.4707 Responsible Artificial Intelligence Defense Act of 2026 (cosponsor with Sen. Coons)
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill sets rules so the Pentagon keeps humans in the loop on AI weapons and bars AI from deciding to launch a nuclear weapon.

evidence.title: Axios: Coons and Reed to introduce the Responsible Artificial Intelligence in Defense Act
evidence.quote: A rigorous framework for human oversight is not a brake on adoption; it is the foundation that makes sustainable, confident adoption possible.
evidence.what_it_shows: The sponsors' memo frames binding human oversight rules as the way to adopt military AI safely, written after the Pentagon's fight with Anthropic.

evidence.title: Arms Control Association: Senate Armed Services Committee adopts AI and autonomous weapons framework based on the Coons-Reed bill in the FY2027 NDAA
evidence.what_it_shows: As ranking member he got most of his human-judgment and testing rules for military AI, including a ban on AI nuclear launch decisions, into the committee's defense bill.

evidence.title: Press release: Reed attends first Senate AI Insight Forum
evidence.quote: There was unanimous consensus that there should be federal regulation of AI and it should be done rapidly, but very carefully.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he supports federal AI regulation and says there are dangers as well as benefits to sort out.

evidence.title: S.5616 Preserving American Dominance in Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed creating a government office to evaluate the most powerful AI models for serious dangers before release.

evidence.title: Letter: Reed, Brown, Menendez and Smith urge CFPB to act on AI voice-cloning scams
evidence.quote: The FTC and CFPB need to take action to help thwart this type of fraud
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants regulators to use existing powers against AI-enabled scams.

evidence.title: The Hill: Reed questions Pentagon CIO on labeling Anthropic a supply chain risk while still using Claude in the Iran war
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed the Pentagon on why it punished an AI company that resisted broad military uses of its model, calling it odd that the department kept using the product.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Reed supports targeted online rules, chiefly the Kids Online Safety Act, the STOP CSAM Act, and letting news outlets bargain with Google and Facebook. He has not called for breaking up tech companies or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care for platforms to protect minors.

evidence.title: Press release: Reed helps build momentum for bipartisan Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.quote: Ensuring a safe environment online should be the default, especially for children.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he wants tech and social media companies held accountable for harm to kids.

evidence.title: S.1829 STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making platforms report and remove child sexual abuse material and letting victims sue.

evidence.title: S.1094 Journalism Competition and Preservation Act of 2023 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed letting news outlets team up to make Google and Facebook pay for their stories.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: Reed voted with 98 other senators to strip the state AI law moratorium from the 2025 budget bill, but no statement, letter or bill was found on preempting state AI laws, the December 2025 executive order, or the March 2026 White House framework as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium from H.R.1 (99-1)
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined the near-unanimous vote to remove the moratorium, but almost every senator did, so the vote alone does not show a position. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Reed is a consistent hawk on AI chip exports. He signed every major Senate Democratic letter against the Trump administration's H20 and H200 sales to China and its Gulf chip deals, and in his own words called the H200 decision a flawed, transactional move that could gift China's military key technology.

evidence.title: Press release: Reed and colleagues warn Trump's U-turn on AI chip sales to China is a colossal economic and national security failure
evidence.quote: This flawed, transactional decision without a broader AI export control strategy could gift China's military key technology gains and seems completely divorced from any consideration of America's economic and national security interests
evidence.what_it_shows: His own words opposing the December 2025 decision to let Nvidia sell H200 chips to China.

evidence.title: Joint statement of Reed, Coons, Shaheen, Warner, Kelly, Himes and Krishnamoorthi on Trump's UAE and Saudi AI chip deals
evidence.quote: AI chips must only be exported to trusted companies, in reasonable numbers, and in concert with credible security standards and assurances.
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed exporting large volumes of advanced chips to the Gulf without security assurances against diversion to China.

evidence.title: Letter: Coons, Warner, Schumer, Reed and Warren to Commerce Secretary Lutnick on resuming Nvidia H20 sales to China
evidence.quote: We shouldn't be trading away key technological advantages as if they are concessions in a trade negotiation
evidence.what_it_shows: He objected to loosening chip export controls as part of trade talks with China.

evidence.title: Letter: Warner, Schumer, Reed, Shaheen, Coons and Warren to President Trump on the 15 percent fee deal for Nvidia and AMD chip sales to China
evidence.quote: We again urge your administration to quickly reverse course and abandon this reckless plan to trade away U.S. technology leadership.
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked Trump to reverse the deal letting Nvidia and AMD sell AI chips to China for a cut of revenue.

evidence.title: Letter: Schumer and Warren lead Senate Democrats including Reed urging Lutnick and Rubio to reconsider the Saudi and UAE chip deals
evidence.quote: These deals greenlight the sale of sensitive U.S. technology in exchange for illusory promises of foreign investment.
evidence.what_it_shows: He signed on to the argument that the Gulf deals risk sensitive chips reaching China.

evidence.title: Brown, Reed, Menendez and Warner letter to President Biden urging a significant BIS funding increase in the FY2025 budget
evidence.what_it_shows: Senate Banking Chairman Brown and three senior Democrats asked the White House to seek a large increase for BIS export-control administration and enforcement.

members.signature: Top Democrat on Armed Services; co-author of the Responsible AI in Defense Act and a steady critic of selling advanced Nvidia chips to China.

quote.text: There was unanimous consensus that there should be federal regulation of AI and it should be done rapidly, but very carefully.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Risch treats AI-driven electricity demand as real and answers it with more nuclear power, including his 2026 ARC Act to help finance new reactors. No statements found on data center siting, ratepayer costs, or the Meta Kuna project as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Press release: Risch touts significance of nuclear energy to growing energy demand (Senate Energy hearing remarks)
evidence.what_it_shows: At a July 2025 Senate Energy hearing he said he had been a doubter about forecasts of AI-driven electricity demand but now expects the country to be inundated with demand, and that nuclear power is how to meet it.

evidence.title: KMVT: Idaho leaders push for nuclear energy expansion with new task force, federal bill
evidence.quote: this huge demand we’re going to have for power in just a very few years because of AI and these other things coming online, they realize that it is going to take nuclear power
evidence.what_it_shows: He ties AI and data center power demand directly to his bipartisan Accelerating Reliable Capacity (ARC) Act, which would put $3.6 billion behind finishing new commercial reactors.

ai_risk.label: Mixed
ai_risk.summary: His only AI-specific action is co-leading the TEST AI Act, which has the national labs and NIST build test beds to check whether AI systems are safe and trustworthy. It funds testing rather than rules, so it does not show a clear lean toward or against regulation.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1633 TEST AI Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: He co-led a bipartisan bill directing the Energy Department and NIST to build test beds for measuring whether AI systems are safe and reliable.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3162 TEST AI Act of 2024 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed the earlier version of the same AI testing bill, showing a sustained interest in federal AI evaluation capacity.

evidence.title: MeriTalk: Bipartisan Senate bill looks to improve AI testing
evidence.what_it_shows: Names Risch as one of five senators introducing the TEST AI Act; the article carries a quote from Sen. Lujan on AI vulnerabilities and risks but no Risch quote.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Shaheen signed a January 2026 letter with five other New England senators pressing the regional grid operator to make tech companies, not families, pay for data center power demand. No statement calling for a pause or moratorium was found; the widely quoted 2026 'Shaheen' moratorium remarks come from her daughter Stefany Shaheen, the NH-1 candidate, not the senator.

evidence.title: Letter: six New England senators ask ISO New England how it will protect ratepayers from data center costs
evidence.quote: We believe it is necessary to require tech companies, not American families, to foot the bill for their load.
evidence.what_it_shows: Shaheen signed on to the view that the AI industry, not households, should pay for data center load and that the grid operator must shield residential ratepayers.

evidence.title: Six New England senators' letter to ISO New England CEO Vamsi Chadalavada on protecting ratepayers from data center growth
evidence.what_it_shows: Senators asked the New England grid operator how it will keep tech companies, not families, paying for data center load, citing a 13% rise in residential prices in 2025 and PJM's capacity price spike as a warning.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Shaheen says Congress is doing too little on AI and hopes it does better than it did on social media; she backs targeted fixes like the TAKE IT DOWN Act and a ban on algorithmic price fixing. No call for licensing, binding safety testing or a pause was found.

evidence.title: WMUR town hall: Shaheen says Congress doing very little to address rise of AI
evidence.quote: I hope that Congress can do a better job of addressing the technology around AI than we've done to address the other technology companies that have been responsible for social media
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants Congress to act on AI, and in the same answer voiced sympathy for an AI company that insisted on safeguards against surveillance uses in its Pentagon dispute.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: TAKE IT DOWN Act (S.146), now law
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a federal crime for posting AI-faked intimate images and fast takedown rules, a targeted guardrail.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025 (S.232)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stopping companies from using shared pricing algorithms to fix prices.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Shaheen backs targeted rules on tech platforms, especially for kids: the Kids Online Safety Act, STOP CSAM, the ECCHO Act and a ban on Chinese-linked connected cars. She talks about holding Big Tech accountable but has not pushed break-ups or a Section 230 repeal.

evidence.title: Press release: Shaheen-backed Kids Online Safety Act passes Senate
evidence.quote: For too long, Big Tech has put profits above all else and failed to protect kids online.
evidence.what_it_shows: She frames kids' online safety as holding Big Tech accountable for addictive and harmful content.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (S.1748)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care for platforms toward minors.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (S.1829)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs letting victims sue platforms that fail to remove child sexual abuse material.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 (S.4429)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning connected cars and software from companies tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act, 118th Congress (S.1409)
evidence.what_it_shows: Her support for kids online safety rules spans two Congresses.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: Shaheen voted with nearly the whole Senate to strip the 10-year state AI law moratorium from the 2025 budget bill, but no statement, letter or bill was found showing her view on federal preemption of state AI laws as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium (Senate roll call 363)
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined the 99-1 vote to remove the moratorium, which by itself does not show a position on preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Shaheen, the top Democrat on Foreign Relations, is one of the Senate's loudest voices against selling advanced AI chips to China: she called the H200 decision a colossal failure, signed letters against the 15 percent fee deal and the Gulf chip deals, and cosponsors the SAFE Chips and AI OVERWATCH Acts. She pairs that with a bill to help allies buy American tech.

evidence.title: Statement: Shaheen leads national security Democrats against allowing Nvidia H200 exports to China
evidence.quote: The Trump administration’s announcement that it will allow the export of advanced H200 AI chips to China is a colossal economic and national security failure.
evidence.what_it_shows: She led the Senate Democrats' condemnation of letting Nvidia sell H200 chips to China and asked the president to reverse course.

evidence.title: Letter: six Senate Democrats urge Trump to reverse the 15 percent fee deal for Nvidia and AMD chip sales to China (CNBC)
evidence.quote: The willingness displayed in this arrangement to 'negotiate' away America's competitive edge that is key to our national security in exchange for what is, in effect, a commission on a sale of AI-enabling technology to our main global competitor, is cause for serious alarm
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed the letter calling the fee-for-licenses deal a threat to national security.

evidence.title: Joint statement of Senate and House Democrats on Trump's UAE and Saudi AI chip deals
evidence.quote: AI chips must only be exported to trusted companies, in reasonable numbers, and in concert with credible security standards and assurances.
evidence.what_it_shows: She opposed large Gulf chip exports without security assurances, warning the compute could reach China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: SAFE Chips Act of 2025 (S.3374)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs locking in current chip export limits on China so the White House cannot loosen them alone.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI OVERWATCH Act (S.4456)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports giving Congress a say before advanced AI chips are approved for sale to China and other risky countries.

evidence.title: MeriTalk: Shaheen and Ricketts introduce the U.S. Tech PATH Act to help allies buy American cyber and digital technology
evidence.what_it_shows: She favors exporting American technology to trusted partners to undercut China, so her hawkishness is aimed at China rather than at exports generally.

evidence.title: Top Senate Democrats' letter to President Trump on the 15 percent fee deal for Nvidia and AMD chip sales to China
evidence.what_it_shows: Six Senate Democrats urged Trump to reverse the deal letting Nvidia and AMD sell AI chips to China in exchange for a 15 percent cut, arguing it harms national security and that export law bars fees tied to licenses; they demanded answers by Aug. 22.

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' statement introducing the SAFE Chips Act to lock in AI chip export limits on China
evidence.what_it_shows: Six senators introduced a bill to codify current chip export limits on China for 30 months, with Ricketts, Coons, Cotton, Shaheen and Kim quoted opposing any loosening for chips like the H200.

evidence.title: Banks and Warren joint statement introducing the AI OVERWATCH Act
evidence.what_it_shows: A bipartisan group introduced the Senate AI OVERWATCH Act to codify the ban on exporting the most advanced AI chips to China; Warren said selling advanced chips to China is 'bad in the short run and worse in the long run.'

members.signature: Retiring Foreign Relations ranking member who leads Senate Democrats against selling advanced AI chips to China and signed the New England senators' letter on data center power costs.

quote.text: The Trump administration’s announcement that it will allow the export of advanced H200 AI chips to China is a colossal economic and national security failure.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Coons wants the US to build out AI computing but says that should not mean higher power bills or lost ground on climate. His answer is efficiency technology, co-leading a bill to study liquid cooling for data centers, not limits on new projects. No statement found on the proposed Delaware City data center itself.

evidence.title: FedScoop: Coons and McCormick introduce the Liquid Cooling for AI Act
evidence.quote: Leading the world in AI innovation shouldn't have to mean skyrocketing energy bills for American families or giving up ground in the fight against climate change
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports the AI buildout and the AI race but wants federal research to cut data center energy use and costs for families.

evidence.title: S.3269 Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025 (original co-lead with Sen. McCormick)
evidence.what_it_shows: Directs a federal assessment of liquid cooling so AI data centers use less power; an efficiency approach rather than a pause or ratepayer mandate.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Coons backs a long list of specific AI rules: a federal right against AI voice and face copies, whistleblower protections, age checks for AI companion bots, bans on deceptive election deepfakes, and human control over military AI. At the same time he calls AI a race with China that America must win and attacked the Pentagon for punishing Anthropic and the White House for pulling frontier models offline without clear rules. He wants durable rules, not a pause.

evidence.title: S.4591 NO FAKES Act of 2026 (sponsor; also sponsored S.1367 in 2025 and S.4875 in 2024)
evidence.what_it_shows: His signature AI bill creates a legal right to stop unauthorized AI copies of a person's voice or likeness; advanced out of Senate Judiciary in June 2026.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Senate Judiciary advances Coons's NO FAKES Act by voice vote
evidence.quote: Every American should have the right to decide how their voice and likeness will be used, especially when generative AI can create highly realistic digital replicas
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words at markup, he frames deepfake protection as a personal right that needs a binding federal law.

evidence.title: S.1792 AI Whistleblower Protection Act (cosponsor with Grassley)
evidence.what_it_shows: Protects AI company employees who report safety problems to the government, a targeted safety rule.

evidence.title: S.3062 GUARD Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require AI chatbot companies to verify ages and keep minors off AI companion bots.

evidence.title: Schatz-led letter from 10 senators to Meta CEO Zuckerberg on AI chatbots and children (Coons signed)
evidence.quote: The wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined a bipartisan demand that Meta explain chatbot policies that allowed romantic talk with minors and add safeguards.

evidence.title: S.4707 Responsible Artificial Intelligence Defense Act of 2026 (sponsor with Reed)
evidence.what_it_shows: Sets rules for military AI that keep humans responsible for the use of force; the Senate Armed Services Committee folded its core into the FY2027 defense bill.

evidence.title: Press release: Ranking Member Coons statement on Pentagon-Anthropic dispute
evidence.quote: The Trump administration's decision to label Anthropic a supply chain risk to national security weakens free enterprise, harms innovation, and makes Americans less safe.
evidence.what_it_shows: He defended Anthropic's refusal to let its models be used for mass surveillance or fully autonomous weapons without a human off switch, calling those commonsense limits.

evidence.title: Press release: Coons statement on Anthropic's launch of Project Glasswing
evidence.quote: Now, Congress needs to step up and do our job: creating clear rules that encourage and support innovation and growth, while ensuring AI can't be used to threaten Americans.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants Congress to write clear AI rules, pairing innovation with guardrails and keeping the technology away from China.

evidence.title: Fortune: Gillibrand, Coons, Kelly, Schiff and Warner letter on the administration's 'unfocused, ad hoc' approach to frontier AI
evidence.quote: Without consistent policy governing American models, consumers and businesses would be incentivized to migrate to models from foreign vendors, including those based in the People's Republic of China.
evidence.what_it_shows: He criticized secret, sudden federal restrictions on frontier models and asked for a public, durable framework; his concern is predictability and competitiveness as much as safety.

evidence.title: Press release: Coons and Cotton introduce resolution affirming America's AI dominance
evidence.quote: The United States' prosperity and safety rests on our ability to win the AI race
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows his innovation-and-China framing; he wants frontier AI built in America by American companies, which tempers his guardrail stance.

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on AI chatbot policies permitting 'romantic or sensual' conversations with children
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators demanded details on how Meta's chatbot safety policies for minors were developed, asked for more visible disclosures and a ban on targeted ads to under-18 users, writing that 'the wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.'

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Coons favors specific fixes for big platforms rather than break-ups: he cosponsors the Kids Online Safety Act and child-abuse-material bills, sponsors a bill forcing social media companies to open their data to researchers, and joined the letter pressing Meta on chatbots and kids. No support found for repealing Section 230 or breaking up companies.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act (cosponsor; also cosponsored S.1409 in the 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs a duty of care and safety tools for minors on social media and games.

evidence.title: Press release: Coons and colleagues introduce the bipartisan Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.quote: without proper safeguards, our children are too often exposed to objectionable, harmful, or outright dangerous content
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words, platforms have value but need mandated safeguards and more transparency about their effect on children.

evidence.title: S.3292 Platform Accountability and Transparency Act (sponsor with Cassidy; also S.1876 in the 118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would force large social media companies to share data with independent researchers, a transparency rule rather than a structural remedy.

evidence.title: S.1829 STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would let victims sue platforms that fail to remove child sexual abuse material, a targeted carve-out from platform immunity.

evidence.title: Schatz-led bipartisan letter of 10 senators to Zuckerberg on safeguards for children using Meta AI chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators told Meta they were 'alarmed' by its chatbot policies, asked how its minor-safety rules were developed, and demanded Meta ban targeted ads to under-18s, improve disclosures and add mental-health referrals.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Coons cosponsored the Senate GUARDRAILS Act, which would block the December 2025 executive order that pressures states to drop their AI laws. He voted with 98 other senators to strip the 10-year state AI law moratorium from the 2025 budget bill. No speech or statement in his own words on preemption was found, so this rests on his cosponsorship.

evidence.title: S.4216 GUARDRAILS Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Protects states' right to pass their own AI safety laws by stopping the executive order that would withhold federal funds from states that regulate AI.

evidence.title: Schatz press release: senators introduce legislation to repeal Trump's AI moratorium (lists Coons as cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Confirms Coons joined the six-senator bill introduced one week after the White House renewed its call to preempt state AI laws.

evidence.title: Senate roll call #363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted to remove the moratorium, but the vote was 99 to 1 after a deal collapsed, so it is a weak signal on its own. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Coons is one of the Senate's most active Democrats on keeping advanced AI chips out of China. He condemned the H20 and H200 sales, co-led the SAFE Chips Act to lock current limits into law, cosponsored the Chip Security, GAIN AI and AI OVERWATCH Acts, and pressed Commerce Secretary Lutnick in writing when his testimony conflicted with Nvidia's CEO.

evidence.title: Press release: Coons statement on Trump's decision to allow export of advanced AI chips (H20) to China
evidence.quote: President Trump's decision today hands China cutting-edge technology that Beijing will use to erase our competitive advantage in artificial intelligence, undermine our military, and outpace our economy.
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed resuming H20 sales and demanded the decision be reversed.

evidence.title: Press release: Top Senate Democrats (Coons, Warner, Schumer, Reed, Warren) letter to Lutnick on resumed AI chip sales to China
