data_centers.summary: Capito says data centers are critical to the nation and wants them in West Virginia, but says developers must build their own power, protect water, and communicate with local communities, with property tax as the main local benefit. As EPW chair she is pushing a bipartisan permitting reform deal to build energy infrastructure faster.

evidence.quote: So I think the services that come with the data center are critical to our nation. I really believe this,
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports data centers as a national priority while asking developers to bring their own power and communicate with communities.

evidence.title: WVPB: Capito on local benefits of data centers
evidence.quote: But the property tax aspects can be used to build new schools and senior centers, improve roads, improve water systems, and so those are the things that I think we ought to really focus on,
evidence.what_it_shows: She admits data centers bring few jobs and points to property tax revenue as the payoff, a build-with-conditions framing.

data_centers.label: Pause or block
data_centers.summary: Carson wants a pause. After primary challengers attacked his silence in spring 2026, he announced support for a federal data center moratorium, co-introduced the AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act, and in June 2026 joined the Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez AI Data Center Moratorium Act. He has also cosponsored bills on ratepayer costs, energy and water disclosure, federal lands and siting.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Guthrie is the House's main mover on data center power costs: his committee passed the Ratepayer Protection Act 52-0 to make data centers pay for the grid upgrades they cause, and he is pushing for a floor vote. He is firmly pro-buildout, calls moratoriums harmful, says communities may opt out, and asked the FBI to probe whether China funds anti-data-center campaigns.

evidence.title: Opening statement: Guthrie leads efforts to lower energy costs, protect ratepayers (AI and the Grid legislative hearing)
evidence.quote: We are also ensuring that data centers are paying their fair share. Data centers should pay for the load that comes into the data centers.
evidence.what_it_shows: Opened a hearing on seven data center and grid bills with the principle that data centers cover their own load costs.

evidence.title: E&C press release: Ratepayer Protection Act advances from committee 52-0
evidence.quote: The Ratepayer Protection Act will ensure that data centers pay their own way, instead of passing costs onto hardworking families.
evidence.what_it_shows: Shepherded H.R. 9340 through his committee unanimously despite data center industry objections.

evidence.title: E&C press release: Guthrie, Latta and Evans on introduction of the Ratepayer Protection Act
evidence.quote: Winning the race to AI dominance is essential to securing America’s future global leadership, and that means expeditiously building the power infrastructure needed to support new technologies, while doing so in a responsible way
evidence.what_it_shows: Pairs a build-fast goal with the condition that families not foot the bill.

evidence.title: E&C ICYMI: Guthrie on Fox Business on AI policy, data center moratoriums and the Ratepayer Protection Act
evidence.quote: We're about six months ahead of China and AI, people predict. If we had a year moratorium, let's say that's nationwide, and we get behind China, we'll never catch up.
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposes data center moratoriums, criticized New York's, and says his bill helps states adopt the ratepayer pledge rather than imposing a one-size-fits-all federal rule.

evidence.title: E&C letter: Chairmen Guthrie, Joyce and Latta request investigation of foreign adversaries' efforts to block American data center buildout
evidence.quote: Americans deserve to know who is bankrolling the disinformation campaign that seeks to block critical infrastructure investments
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked PCAST and the FBI to investigate whether China-backed entities fund anti-data-center campaigns, treating organized opposition as possible foreign disinformation.

evidence.title: Bowling Green Daily News: Guthrie calls for investigations into AI and data center opposition, says local leaders decide
evidence.quote: The local concerns are real, and should be always taken into consideration
evidence.what_it_shows: Says communities may choose not to participate and that questions about taxes and jobs are fair, while insisting America must build or China will.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Guthrie pushes September floor vote on Ratepayer Protection Act despite industry pushback
evidence.quote: protects local communities and, I think, allows data centers to be successful
evidence.what_it_shows: Acknowledged data center industry opposition downtown but kept pressing leadership to bring the bill to the floor.

evidence.what_it_shows: Positions the bill as bridging Trump's pro-data-center stance and vulnerable Republicans' constituent backlash.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Hirono has no press release on data centers, but at a July 2026 Senate Energy hearing she raised the risk that data centers' power use gets shifted onto regular customers' bills. The only evidence is a reporter's account of that remark.

evidence.title: Bloomberg Government: Senators press FERC on data center oversight (Senate Energy and Natural Resources hearing)
evidence.quote: Sen. Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii) said that potential cost shifting of data centers' high energy use onto consumers has led to states curtailing data center projects
evidence.what_it_shows: This is the reporter's paraphrase, not her exact words, but it shows her concern at the FERC oversight hearing was about data center costs landing on ordinary ratepayers.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Hirono backs targeted AI rules: testing automated systems for bias, banning AI discrimination, protecting people's voice and likeness from AI copies, and stopping AI deepfakes in elections. She also investigated a DOGE plan to replace Education Department call centers with an AI chatbot. She has not called for licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 (S.2164)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making big companies test automated decision systems for bias and harm and report results.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 (S.3308)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a ban on discriminatory uses of AI and required bias testing; she also cosponsored the 2024 version (S.5152).

evidence.title: Cosponsor: NO FAKES Act of 2026 (S.4591)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a legal right to stop unauthorized AI copies of a person's voice or face; also cosponsored the 2025 version (S.1367).

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Fraudulent Artificial Intelligence Regulations (FAIR) Elections Act of 2026 (S.4774)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports rules against AI deepfakes that trick voters; she also cosponsored the Deceptive Practices and Voter Intimidation Prevention Act (S.2912).

evidence.title: Press release: Hirono, Warren, Schumer open investigation into DOGE's AI chatbot plan for Education Department call centers
evidence.quote: DOGE's proposal threatens to misinform borrowers and families, lead to data privacy breaches, and pose conflicts of interest arising from Elon Musk's financial stake in AI development
evidence.what_it_shows: She pressed the administration on AI chatbot hallucinations and data privacy before letting a chatbot replace human student aid staff.

evidence.title: IPWatchdog: Senate Judiciary oversight hearing with the Copyright Office, where Hirono asked about AI and fair use
evidence.what_it_shows: Per the report, Hirono asked whether Congress should hold off on legislating AI fair use and let the courts develop case law, a cautious note on one AI copyright question.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: Hirono has a long record of backing tough rules on Big Tech: antitrust reform, the American Innovation and Choice Online Act, the EARN IT Act limiting platforms' legal shield, kids' online safety, and privacy for reproductive health data. At a 2024 hearing she told social media CEOs they cannot keep profiting off children while looking away from harm.

evidence.title: Press release: Hirono, colleagues reintroduce bipartisan legislation to boost competition and rein in Big Tech (American Innovation and Choice Online Act)
evidence.quote: By holding online giants accountable, the American Innovation and Choice Online Act will help put an end to this distortion and foster a fair and open market where small businesses, entrepreneurs, and consumers can thrive.
evidence.what_it_shows: She co-led a bill to stop dominant platforms from favoring their own products, a core Big Tech competition measure.

evidence.title: Press release: Hirono presses Big Tech executives to protect children online (Senate Judiciary hearing with Meta, X, TikTok, Snap and Discord CEOs)
evidence.quote: If you are going to continue to attract kids to your platforms, you have an obligation to ensure they are safe on those platforms.
evidence.what_it_shows: She framed platforms as profiting from children while failing to protect them, and tied them to trafficking and abuse material in Hawaii.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Competition and Antitrust Law Enforcement Reform Act of 2025 (S.130)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making it harder for giant companies to merge; she also cosponsored the 2024 version (S.4308).

evidence.title: Cosponsor: EARN IT Act of 2023 (S.1207)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports removing platforms' legal shield when they let child abuse material spread.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (S.1748)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care for platforms toward minors; she also cosponsored KOSA in the 118th Congress (S.1409).

evidence.title: Sponsor: My Body, My Data Act of 2023 (S.1656)
evidence.what_it_shows: Led a bill restricting how apps and companies collect and sell reproductive health data.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025 (S.232)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning shared pricing algorithms used to fix prices; she also backed the 2024 rental housing algorithm bill (S.3692).

She did not cosponsor the States' Right to Regulate AI Act or GUARDRAILS Act.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (Hirono voted Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined the 99-1 vote to remove the moratorium, but with no accompanying statement this is not evidence of a stance on preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Hoeven has not spoken directly about data centers in anything we found. His related record is pro-build: he sponsors a bill to move coal, gas and nuclear plants to the front of the grid connection line to meet rising demand, and he wants states and existing ratepayers shielded from transmission cost shifts.

evidence.title: Press release: Hoeven, Young introduce GRID Power Act (S. 465) to fast-track baseload power projects
evidence.quote: Our legislation seeks to reverse this trend by empowering grid operators to put baseload power generation projects at the front of the line for approval.
evidence.what_it_shows: His answer to rising electricity demand, which the bill's backers tie to AI data centers, is to build more always-on generation faster.

evidence.title: Press release: Cramer, Fedorchak introduce FAIR Act; Hoeven cosponsors the Senate companion (S. 3287)
evidence.quote: North Dakotans shouldn’t be forced to pay higher energy costs to help other states meet their unworkable energy mandates
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants electric bills protected from cost shifting, a ratepayer-first instinct he applies to transmission built for other states rather than to data centers specifically.

evidence.title: E&E News: North Dakota delegation letter to FERC on transmission cost allocation; delegation guards state planning authority
evidence.what_it_shows: E&E reports Hoeven joined a September 2025 letter urging FERC not to assign regional transmission costs to North Dakotans who do not benefit, and describes the delegation as steadfast in preserving state planning autonomy as Washington pushes faster data center grid hookups.

evidence.title: Press release: Hoeven presses FERC nominees on baseload power and states' rights
evidence.quote: We need policies that support a diverse mix of energy resources to ensure grid stability and resilience, while also respecting the rights of states and private landowners.
evidence.what_it_shows: He ties meeting rising electricity demand to coal-fired baseload power and to respecting state regulators and landowners.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (119th S. 1748)
evidence.what_it_shows: He signed on to the main bill making platforms build in safety tools for kids under 17.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (118th S. 1409)
evidence.what_it_shows: He also cosponsored the earlier version that passed the Senate in July 2024.

evidence.title: Press release: Hoeven on Senate passage of KOSA and COPPA 2.0

evidence.what_it_shows: He pushed the Senate to pass the forced-sale TikTok bill on national security grounds.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on Senate roll call 363, Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium from H.R. 1 (99-1)
evidence.what_it_shows: Nearly every senator voted Yea after the deal collapsed, so this vote alone does not show his view on preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

ai_risk.summary: Johnson calls AI an enormously complex problem and is skeptical that Congress can write good rules for it, saying the country would be better off passing far fewer laws. He is also wary of trusting industry experts with vested interests, so he has not embraced any specific AI guardrail bill.

evidence.title: Fox News: State-level AI rules survive as Senate sinks moratorium despite White House pressure
evidence.quote: And I think we'd be far better off if we passed a lot fewer laws. I'm not sure how often we get it right.
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked about a federal AI framework, he doubted Congress should legislate much on AI at all.

evidence.title: Fox News: State-level AI rules survive as Senate sinks moratorium despite White House pressure
evidence.quote: And again, I'm concerned, the real experts on this have got vested interests. Whatever they're advising is, can you really trust them?
evidence.what_it_shows: He is skeptical of the AI industry's advice as well, so his light-touch stance is not a pro-industry one.

tech_regulation.label: Mixed
tech_regulation.summary: Johnson has long attacked what he calls Big Tech censorship, cosponsoring bills to expose government pressure on platforms and joining a 2022 call to ban TikTok from state devices. But his fixes target government rather than the companies, and he says Congress should pass fewer laws, so his record is mixed.

evidence.title: Press release: Sen. Johnson joins Sen. Hagerty, colleagues in reintroducing the Disclose Government Censorship Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He cosponsored a bill requiring transparency when the government asks platforms to suppress speech, his main approach to Big Tech.

evidence.title: Fox Business: Sen. Ron Johnson demands answers from Biden on administration's work with Big Tech to censor online posts
evidence.quote: Big Tech has now become Big Brother
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames platforms as a censorship threat, which is hostile to Big Tech but focused on speech rather than privacy or antitrust rules.

evidence.title: Press release: Steil, delegation call for Evers to ban TikTok from state government devices (Johnson listed as a signer)
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined Wisconsin Republicans urging the governor to ban TikTok on state devices, a targeted restriction on a Chinese-owned app.

preemption.label: Let states regulate

evidence.quote: I personally don't think we should be setting a federal standard right now and prohibiting the states from doing what we should be doing in a federated republic. Let the states experiment

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (99-1)

evidence.title: Fox News: State-level AI rules survive as Senate sinks moratorium despite White House pressure
evidence.quote: enormously complex problem. It's my definition of a problem.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Markey wants data centers built only under strong federal protections: his July 2026 discussion draft would require a federal certificate before permitting, and he says every community should be able to say no. He has not called for a national moratorium.

evidence.title: Press release: Markey releases discussion draft of the Protecting Communities from Data Center Impacts Act
evidence.quote: Communities are organizing and demanding action to protect their air, water, energy bills, and quality of life from the tsunami of data centers around the country
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would make data centers get a federal certificate showing they will not harm the public interest before they can be permitted or built.

evidence.title: Press release: 'The Data Center Next Door' roundtable on data center harms
evidence.quote: unregulated, uncontrolled data center development is sucking our communities dry. Our environment doesn't have to be a sacrificial lamb on the altar of innovation.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames unregulated data center growth as a threat to communities, energy bills and public health and attacks the Trump AI Action Plan's deregulatory approach.

evidence.title: WCVB report on the final Markey-Moulton Senate primary debate
evidence.quote: every community should be able to say 'no' to data centers if they don't want them, if it's going to trigger electricity spikes, water crisis, pollution bombs going off, but we're going to need national legislation
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs a local veto over data centers plus national rules, short of a blanket pause.

evidence.title: S.4727 Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Would have scientists measure AI's energy, water and pollution footprint and set up reporting; reintroduced from 2024.

evidence.title: Seven Democratic senators' letter to FERC Chair Laura Swett urging action to stop data-center-driven rate hikes
evidence.what_it_shows: Senators urged FERC to reject transmission filings that spread data-center costs across regions, investigate cost allocation and PJM practices, resist queue-jumping for large fossil generators, standardize load forecasting, and prioritize residential ratepayers in the DOE-requested large-load interconnection rulemaking.

evidence.title: Six New England senators' letter to ISO New England CEO Vamsi Chadalavada on protecting ratepayers from data center growth
evidence.what_it_shows: Senators asked the New England grid operator how it will keep tech companies, not families, paying for data center load, citing a 13% rise in residential prices in 2025 and PJM's capacity price spike as a warning.

evidence.title: Letter from Senators Markey, Blumenthal, Van Hollen and Booker to NARUC President Ann Rendahl on state PUC action against data center cost-shifting
evidence.what_it_shows: Two days after the White House's voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge, the senators called it 'vague and insufficient' and asked state utility regulators' association what guidance it gives PUCs to reject rate filings that make households subsidize data centers.

evidence.title: Senator Markey letter to EPA Administrator Zeldin opposing pre-construction of data centers without Clean Air Act NSR permits
evidence.what_it_shows: Markey objected to EPA's reinterpretation letting data centers and their gas generation begin construction before securing New Source Review air permits, calling it likely unlawful and harmful to communities.

evidence.title: Markey-McClellan bicameral letter to EPA urging withdrawal of proposed rule letting data centers and power plants begin construction before air permits
evidence.what_it_shows: Sixteen lawmakers told EPA to withdraw its May 2026 proposal redefining 'begin actual construction' so data centers and fossil plants can pour foundations and install wiring before New Source Review permits, saying it turns the Clean Air Act's preconstruction safeguards 'on its head.'

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Markey is at the aggressive end of targeted guardrails: he sponsors bills to ban discriminatory AI, protect kids from chatbots, keep humans in control of nuclear launch and pause government face recognition. He does not frame AI as an existential threat or push frontier-model licensing.

evidence.title: S.3308 Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Would ban discriminatory uses of AI and require companies to test high-stakes systems for bias.

evidence.title: Press release: Markey introduces the Youth AI Privacy Act on AI chatbots and kids
evidence.quote: AI chatbots pose grave new risks to kids' privacy and safety, but Big Tech continues to speak only one language: profit
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants binding privacy and anti-manipulation rules for chatbots used by minors.

evidence.title: S.1394 Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require a human, never an AI system, to make any nuclear launch decision.

evidence.title: New Bedford Light report on the final Markey-Moulton debate
evidence.quote: because of the clear and palpable danger which has been presented both to our climate and to the children of our country
evidence.what_it_shows: He describes AI's dangers mainly in terms of climate and kids, not catastrophic or existential risk.

evidence.title: CNBC: Anthropic-backed Public First Action gave $500,000 to a PAC supporting Markey
evidence.quote: has been unequivocal in his support for regulating AI.
evidence.what_it_shows: An AI-safety-aligned political group backed him in the 2026 primary because of his pro-regulation record.

evidence.title: Markey and Lieu statement applauding inclusion of 'human in the loop' nuclear-launch safeguard in the FY2025 NDAA
evidence.what_it_shows: The sponsors of the Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous AI Act said key provisions were included in the defense bill signed by President Biden, ensuring humans alone can order a nuclear launch.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: Markey is a longtime Big Tech critic: he wrote the kids' privacy law and its COPPA 2.0 update, cosponsors tougher antitrust law, and has pressed Meta, Apple and Google over chatbots and sexual deepfakes. One exception: he opposed the TikTok ban and sponsored a bill to delay it.

evidence.title: S.836 Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA 2.0)
evidence.what_it_shows: Lead sponsor of the major update to the kids' online privacy law.

evidence.title: S.130 Competition and Antitrust Law Enforcement Reform Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs tougher merger rules aimed at giant companies including Big Tech.

evidence.title: NBC News: Wyden, Markey and Lujan urge Apple and Google to remove X and Grok from app stores
evidence.quote: Turning a blind eye to X's egregious behavior would make a mockery of your moderation practices.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants app store gatekeepers to enforce their rules against AI-generated sexual deepfakes.

evidence.title: NBC News: Markey letter says Meta ignored his 2023 warning about teens and AI chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: He urged Meta to bar minors from its AI chatbots after reports of romantic chats with kids.

evidence.title: Press release: Markey introduces the Youth AI Privacy Act
evidence.quote: My bill stops AI companies from using manipulative tricks to keep kids hooked on chatbots, and it imposes critical privacy protections to stop Big Tech from profiting off our young people.
evidence.what_it_shows: Targets Big Tech's business model around children.

evidence.title: S.103 Extend the TikTok Deadline Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Contrary signal: he sought more time before TikTok had to be sold or banned, opposing the ban approach.

evidence.title: Markey letter to Zuckerberg urging Meta to bar minors from AI chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: Sen. Markey told Meta to stop letting minors use its AI chatbots, noting he had warned Meta in 2023 not to roll chatbots out to teens and citing privacy risks when teens use bots as therapists.

evidence.title: Wyden, Markey and Lujan open letter to Apple and Google to remove X and Grok from app stores over AI-generated sexual images
evidence.what_it_shows: Three Democratic senators told Apple and Google to pull X and Grok from their app stores until Elon Musk stops Grok from generating nonconsensual sexualized images of women and children, saying inaction would 'make a mockery' of their moderation claims.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Markey led the fight against the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws, wrote the States' Right to Regulate AI Act, and has vowed to fight the December 2025 executive order. He says states must be able to regulate AI even as Congress writes national rules.

evidence.title: S.3557 States' Right to Regulate AI Act
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill says the federal government cannot wipe out state AI laws.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the state AI-law moratorium (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted to strip the moratorium; he had partnered on the amendment after weeks of opposing the provision. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: Press release: Senate strikes AI moratorium 99-1 after Markey raised the alarm
evidence.quote: This 99-1 vote sent a clear message that Congress will not sell out our kids and local communities in order to pad the pockets of Big Tech billionaires.
evidence.what_it_shows: He claimed credit for defeating the moratorium and framed it as protecting kids and local communities.

evidence.title: Press release: Markey statement on Trump AI regulation moratorium executive order
evidence.quote: I will use every tool available to challenge this indefensible and irresponsible power grab. We will defeat it again.
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposes the executive order aimed at overriding state AI laws.

evidence.title: The Hill: Markey-Warren Dear Colleague letter urging Democrats to reject any NDAA with an AI moratorium
evidence.quote: Congress should not give Big Tech a multi-year holiday from state oversight
evidence.what_it_shows: He organized Senate Democrats against reviving the moratorium in the defense bill.

evidence.title: WCVB report on the final Markey-Moulton debate
evidence.quote: States should be able to regulate AI
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants national laws too but insists states keep their power.

evidence.title: Cantwell and Senate Commerce Committee Democrats letter to Chairman Cruz demanding a markup of the reconciliation Commerce title, flagging the AI moratorium
evidence.what_it_shows: Twelve Commerce Committee Democrats told Cruz the AI moratorium 'tramples states' rights and holds the $42 billion BEAD program hostage' and asked for regular committee consideration instead of a fast-tracked floor vote.

evidence.title: Sen. Ed Markey and Sen. Maria Cantwell statements after the 99-1 vote
evidence.what_it_shows: Markey: the vote 'sent a clear message that Congress will not sell out our kids and local communities in order to pad the pockets of Big Tech billionaires.' Cantwell led the Democratic effort and Commerce Democrats' release credited a bipartisan coalition.

evidence.title: Sen. Ed Markey statement on the White House AI legislative framework
evidence.what_it_shows: Markey said Trump was 'proposing to block states from protecting their communities from AI-related harms' and urged Congress to pass his States' Right to Regulate AI Act instead.

She did not join the AI Data Center Moratorium Act, so she stops short of a pause.

evidence.title: Letter from 12 members of Congress (Van Hollen, Beyer, Norton and others) to PJM Board Chair David Mills on data center load and capacity costs
evidence.quote: driven almost entirely by new large data center loads, is a serious concern for future grid reliability, and our constituents are already feeling the impacts on their wallets
evidence.what_it_shows: Norton joined lawmakers blaming data centers for higher electric bills and criticizing PJM for dropping a mandatory curtailment backstop for large loads under industry pressure.

evidence.title: H.R. 6529 Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed on the day of introduction to a bill keeping families' electric bills from paying for the power lines and plants AI data centers need.

evidence.title: H.R. 8241 Power for the People Act of 2026 (original cosponsor; Tonko release lists Norton)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs data center load queues and data center-specific rate classes so other electricity customers do not carry the cost.

evidence.title: H.R. 6179 Clean Cloud Act of 2025 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports pollution limits and fees on the electricity big data centers and crypto mines use.

evidence.title: H.R. 7858 Data Center Community Impact Act (original cosponsor; E&E News lists Norton)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require a federal study of how data centers affect nearby communities' power, water, health and bills.

evidence.title: H.R. 8488 AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act of 2026 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would make developers tell communities about planned AI data centers and their utility and environmental impacts before plans are final.

evidence.title: H.R. 6984 Data Center Transparency Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require data centers to publicly report their electricity and water use.

evidence.title: H.R. 9183 Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a government study of AI's electricity, water and pollution footprint with voluntary industry reporting; a milder measure.

evidence.title: H.R. 9372 Data Infrastructure Energy Measurement and Standards Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports standard ways to measure data center electricity and water use.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Norton backs a long list of specific AI rules: bias testing for automated decisions, an AI civil rights law, bans on AI-driven price and wage discrimination, deepfake and election-lie penalties, limits on federal facial recognition, and blocking an AI Medicare prior-authorization pilot. In Aug 2026 she signed a letter calling advanced AI a clear safety risk and demanding AI CEOs testify under oath. She has not backed frontier-model licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: Casar-led letter from 20 House members to Speaker Johnson demanding hearings with AI CEOs under oath (Norton signed)
evidence.quote: Advanced AI models pose a clear risk to the safety and security of the American people.
evidence.what_it_shows: After AI models escaped test environments, Norton joined a demand that Congress hold AI CEOs accountable and write regulation so it never happens again.

evidence.title: Press release: Norton Says Chatbots Are No Replacement for Federal Workers (Oversight Committee hearing on AI)
evidence.quote: AI is a tool that can empower our public servants, but it is not a substitute for passionate and committed federal workers
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own words at an Oversight hearing: AI in government must keep people at the center and should not be used to justify cutting Social Security staff.

evidence.title: H.R. 5511 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports binding bias and harm testing for automated decision systems with reports to the FTC.

evidence.title: H.R. 6356 Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 (original cosponsor; Pressley release lists Norton)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning discriminatory AI and requiring companies to test AI before and after deployment.

evidence.title: H.R. 7110 Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would put civil rights teams in agencies to catch unfair algorithms; she also cosponsored the 2024 version.

evidence.title: H.R. 4640 Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning companies from using AI and personal data to set individualized prices or wages.

evidence.title: H.J.Res. 187 disapproving the CMS WISeR rule (AI prior authorization in Medicare)
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants to block a Medicare experiment letting contractors use AI to approve or deny treatments.

evidence.title: H.R. 7363 ICE Out of Our Faces Act (limits DHS use of facial recognition)
evidence.what_it_shows: Continues her support for limiting government facial recognition; she cosponsored the 2023 federal facial recognition moratorium bill too.

evidence.title: H.R. 3562 DEFIANCE Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports letting victims sue over AI-made sexual deepfakes.

evidence.title: H.R. 4894 Deceptive Practices and Voter Intimidation Prevention Act of 2025 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports outlawing AI-made lies about voting before federal elections.

evidence.title: H.R. 10146 AI Advertising Disclosure Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring ads to disclose when they were made with AI.

evidence.title: The Hill: Democratic lawmakers' letter asking the FEC to treat AI deepfakes of candidates as fraudulent misrepresentation (Norton a signatory)
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined a push for the FEC to regulate deceptive AI in campaigns after the Grok image generator backlash.

evidence.title: H.R. 1404 Facial Recognition and Biometric Technology Moratorium Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for pausing federal use of facial recognition until Congress authorizes it.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Norton consistently cosponsors targeted tech rules: AI robocall disclosure, kids' and reproductive data privacy, cutting abusers' remote access to cars, limits on employer surveillance of workers, and a ban on China-linked connected-car tech. A Dec 2025 letter she signed warned that preempting state AI laws would let Big Tech run rampant. No statements found on Section 230 or breaking up tech companies.

evidence.title: H.R. 1027 QUIET Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring AI-voiced robocalls to say so and raising fines for illegal robocalls.

evidence.title: H.R. 2110 Safe Vehicle Access for Survivors Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making car companies cut off an abuser's remote access to a car's apps and location data.

evidence.title: H.R. 3218 Reproductive Data Privacy and Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stopping companies from collecting or selling reproductive health data without permission.

evidence.title: H.R. 8730 Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning connected-car software and parts from companies tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

evidence.title: H.R. 9402 Stop Spying Bosses Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports limiting or requiring disclosure of employer surveillance and worker data collection.

evidence.title: Clarke-led letter from 44 House Democrats to Armed Services leaders opposing any AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA (Norton signed)
evidence.quote: Not only would this stomp on state autonomy, but it would create an unnecessary regulatory vacuum that lets Big Tech run rampant.
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames blocking state tech rules as a gift to Big Tech, signalling she wants enforceable rules on the industry.

evidence.title: H.R. 2801 Kids PRIVACY Act (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for limiting how apps collect and use kids' and teens' data; she did not join the 119th Kids Online Safety Act.

evidence.title: H.R. 3420 My Body, My Data Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for a reproductive health data privacy law.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Norton wants states free to write their own AI laws. She was an original cosponsor of the GUARDRAILS Act to repeal the Dec 2025 executive order preempting state AI laws, and she signed both the Nov 2025 Matsui letter (81 House Democrats) and the Dec 2025 Clarke letter (44 signers) against an AI moratorium in the defense bill.

evidence.title: H.R. 8031 GUARDRAILS Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Signed on the day of introduction to a bill blocking the White House executive order that seeks to preempt state AI laws.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs, Beyer, Matsui, Lieu, McClain Delaney Introduce Legislation to Repeal White House AI Moratorium (lists Norton as original cosponsor)
evidence.quote: This legislation would prohibit the executive order from taking effect to ensure states can enact commonsense safeguards
evidence.what_it_shows: Confirms Norton co-led the GUARDRAILS Act on the same day the White House released its national AI policy framework.

evidence.title: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats to Johnson, Thune, Jeffries and Schumer opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and the planned preemption executive order (Norton signed)
evidence.quote: As you consider the NDAA, we urge you to oppose any effort to reinsert an AI moratorium barring state and local governments from enforcing their laws.
evidence.what_it_shows: Norton opposed reviving the state AI-law moratorium after the Senate rejected it 99-1 and opposed using an executive order or BEAD funds to override state laws.

evidence.title: Clarke-led letter from 44 House Democrats to House and Senate Armed Services leaders urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA (Norton signed)
evidence.quote: Any kind of preemption would cause a slew of unintended consequences putting all Americans at risk online; a moratorium would be wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation.
evidence.what_it_shows: A second letter in a week opposing preemption, stressing that no federal AI law exists to replace state protections.

evidence.title: Clarke-led House Democratic letter to House and Senate Armed Services leaders urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA
evidence.what_it_shows: 44 House Democrats asked the defense-bill negotiators to keep any state AI-law preemption or moratorium out of the NDAA, calling a moratorium 'wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation.'

china_chips.label: No public position found
china_chips.summary: No public position found on AI chip export controls as of Sept 2026. Searches for Norton with Nvidia, export controls, H20/H200, the Chip Security Act and GAIN AI turned up nothing, and she has not cosponsored any chip-export bill. Her one China-related tech bill, the Connected Vehicle Security Act, is about cars, not chips.

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Paul says whether to allow a data center should be a local or state decision, not Washington's. He opposes a federal ban and federal subsidies alike, calls the boom overhyped, and wants more nuclear power to feed it.

evidence.title: Bowling Green Daily News interview: Paul on data centers
evidence.quote: I think people won’t be very satisfied with someone who’s so distant from the problem making the decision
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants siting decided locally; the paper reports he opposes both a federal ban on data centers and federal funding for them, and will not dictate local zoning.

evidence.title: Oldham Era interview: Senator weighs in on data centers
evidence.quote: Nobody in Washington can know as well or feel as strongly about these types of issues as the people who are close to them so I would keep these decisions local
evidence.what_it_shows: Repeats that data center decisions belong to local jurisdictions, while voicing concern about federal moves to expand data centers.

evidence.title: WLKY: Paul at Fort Knox on data centers after Gov. Beshear's executive order
evidence.quote: We shouldn't tell them they have to, nor should we tell them they can't. I think the decision should be made the more local, the better
evidence.what_it_shows: Neither a federal push nor a federal block; he also called the data center rush hype that will cool and said fewer may be needed than claimed.

evidence.title: Kentucky Lantern: Paul says states will decide AI and data center policy, wants more nuclear power
evidence.quote: You can’t just have data centers without energy, so we’re going to need more energy
evidence.what_it_shows: Ties data center growth to new power supply, backs nuclear and coal, and expects state legislatures to make most of these calls.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Paul treats AI as inevitable and mostly beneficial in private hands and opposes new federal mandates on platforms. His AI worry is government using AI to surveil and censor citizens, where he wants hard limits. Mixed, but leans light touch on industry.

evidence.title: Oldham Era interview: Paul on AI's future and government surveillance
evidence.quote: I think AI will bring benefits, particularly in the private industry and private world, but where I see potential problems with AI are in government's use in spying or surveilling on its citizenry.
evidence.what_it_shows: Locates the danger in government use of AI, not in the technology or the companies building it.

evidence.title: National Review op-ed: Keep Artificial Intelligence out of Government Surveillance
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence is only going to make it easier for the government to do this and harder to detect.
evidence.what_it_shows: Calls for getting to the bottom of federal AI-driven disinformation monitoring, a civil-liberties guardrail on government rather than industry regulation.

evidence.title: HSGAC hearing on Artificial Intelligence in Government: Paul warns of AI surveillance threat to free expression
evidence.what_it_shows: As ranking member he used the committee's AI hearing to attack federal use of AI tools to flag and suppress speech, and sought limits on that use.

tech_regulation.label: Mixed
tech_regulation.summary: Mixed. Paul was one of three senators to vote against the Kids Online Safety Act and sponsored a bill to repeal the TikTok ban, calling both censorship. But in January 2026 he reversed on Section 230 and vowed legislation to strip Google and YouTube's liability shield, and he backs limits on the government buying Americans' data.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 221 (2024): passage of S.2073 Kids Online Safety and Privacy Act (Nay)
evidence.what_it_shows: One of only three senators against the kids' online safety package that passed 91-3. Recorded vote: Nay.

evidence.title: Courier Journal op-ed against KOSA, as quoted by The Hill
evidence.quote: This requirement will not only stifle free speech, but it will deprive Americans of the benefits of our technological advancements.
evidence.what_it_shows: He objected to KOSA's duty of care as a speech restriction; the quote is from The Hill's report on his op-ed.

evidence.title: New York Post: Paul says KOSA will lead to censorship
evidence.quote: But I’m afraid it will lead to censorship.
evidence.what_it_shows: Sympathetic to the goal but argues a vague anxiety standard enforced by the FTC would let government censor content.

evidence.title: S.153 Repeal the TikTok Ban Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would undo the law forcing TikTok's sale or ban, the opposite of his Kentucky colleague McConnell.

evidence.title: Press release: Paul and Khanna introduce Repeal the TikTok Ban Act
evidence.quote: A government that can ban an app, can ban a book. A government that can silence a platform, can silence a person.
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames the TikTok ban as government control of speech rather than a China security measure.

evidence.title: New York Post op-ed reversing on Section 230, as quoted by Broadband Breakfast
evidence.quote: The arrogance of Google to continue hosting this defamatory video and the resultant threats on my life have caused me to rethink Congress’ blind allegiance to liability shields
evidence.what_it_shows: After YouTube refused to remove a video he calls defamatory, he pledged to pursue legislation ending Section 230 protections, a sharp turn toward reining in Big Tech.

evidence.title: S.2425 Free Speech Protection Act (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Bars officials from pressuring platforms to take down posts; a restraint on government, not a platform rule.

evidence.title: S.2576 Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would stop police and spy agencies from buying Americans' location and phone data from brokers without a warrant.

evidence.quote: a lot of these decisions will be made by the state legislature
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked how federal AI decisions would affect state policy, he pointed to state legislatures as the deciders.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Scalise celebrates data centers, pointing to Meta's Richland Parish project funding teacher bonuses, calls the fight 'a competition with China,' and says Republicans are investigating whether China is behind 'misinformation' against data centers. He says siting should stay a local choice. The top Energy and Commerce Democrat accused him and Speaker Johnson of refusing for weeks to bring up the Ratepayer Protection Act, which reports said leaders finally scheduled for a September 2026 floor vote.

evidence.title: Press release: Scalise on Fox Business, on the local benefits of data centers
evidence.quote: This is a competition with China. Let's be clear about this. And we are investigating whether China is behind a lot of this misinformation, false information against data centers.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames opposition to data centers as possibly China-driven misinformation and treats build-out as a national security race.

evidence.title: Press release: Scalise on Fox Business, siting is a local decision
evidence.quote: Ultimately they're decided at the local level and if you want them in your community. And by the way, there are a lot of communities that do want them.

evidence.quote: Here on Capitol Hill, Speaker Johnson and Majority Leader Scalise have refused to bring up the Ratepayer Protection Act that passed unanimously out of this committee in July
evidence.what_it_shows: Rep. Pallone's charge that leadership stalled the ratepayer bill, citing 'concerns from Republican members'; a September floor vote was later reported.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Scalise takes a light-touch, beat-China view. He says Congress will address AI abuses as they appear but must not limit innovation, warns that government regulates industries 'to the point where they crush innovation,' and joined the March 2026 pledge to enact a national framework. His office did not say whether he backs the bipartisan Kill Switch bill.

evidence.title: NOLA.com: Louisiana waits to see how Trump, Congress will regulate AI
evidence.quote: One thing government really likes to do a good job of is regulating to the point where they crush innovation, and you’ve seen that in a lot of industry
evidence.what_it_shows: Speaking Aug. 7, 2026, he said abuses would be addressed but innovation must not be limited; his spokesperson would not say whether he supports the Kill Switch bill.

evidence.title: Joint statement: Johnson, Scalise, Guthrie, Jordan, Babin on the White House national AI framework
evidence.quote: To ensure we continue to harness its potential and beat China in the global AI race, Congress must take action.
evidence.what_it_shows: He committed to legislation giving innovators 'much-needed certainty' while protecting kids, in line with the administration's light-touch framework.

evidence.title: Breitbart: Leading the Future super PAC endorses Scalise in its second slate of House Republicans
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence has the potential to strengthen our economy and ensure America outcompetes China to remain the global leader in innovation.
evidence.what_it_shows: The Andreessen Horowitz and Brockman-funded pro-AI super PAC backs him; he said he looks forward to 'an AI agenda that provides much-needed certainty while protecting consumers.'

tech_regulation.label: Mixed
tech_regulation.summary: Mixed. Scalise supported the 2026 KIDS Act and, as Whip, backed Republican Section 230 reform and app store transparency bills aimed at what he calls Big Tech censorship of conservatives. evidence.title: Speaker Johnson release: House passes KIDS Act, with Leader Scalise statement

evidence.what_it_shows: He backed the House kids' online safety package, a targeted rule.

evidence.quote: would require app store operators like Google, Apple, and Amazon to annually submit a description of their app store conduct policies to the Federal Trade Commission

evidence.title: The Hill: Scalise says GOP leaders 'looking at other places' for AI preemption as NDAA push stalls

evidence.what_it_shows: He dropped the NDAA vehicle but said 'we're still looking at other places because there's still an interest.'

evidence.what_it_shows: He committed House Republicans to enact the White House framework, which calls for preempting state AI laws.

data_centers.label: Pause or block
data_centers.summary: Wants a pause. She cosponsored the AI Data Center Moratorium Act in June 2026 and publicly opposes the proposed $1.5 billion Project Red Clay data center in Lowndes County, citing water, environmental justice, property values and unanswered questions about who benefits. She says she is not anti-AI and wants Alabama to compete for AI industries once federal guardrails exist.

evidence.title: Cosponsor, Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act (H.R. 9442)
evidence.what_it_shows: Signed onto the Ocasio-Cortez bill pausing new large AI data centers until federal safeguards exist.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Sewell cosponsors legislation to pause AI data center construction until federal guardrails are established
evidence.quote: I am not anti-AI, and I am certainly not anti-innovation. The rate at which these massive data centers are being constructed is simply outpacing our ability to establish meaningful protections for the communities that will host them.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own framing of the moratorium as a pause, not a ban, driven by constituent concerns about water, energy and local benefit.

evidence.title: Op-ed (AL.com, reprinted by Lowndes Signal): Why I oppose the proposed data center in Lowndes County
evidence.quote: If developers cannot demonstrate that the county's water infrastructure, public health, environment and property owners will be protected, then this project should not move forward.
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposes a specific project in her district on water, environmental justice and property-value grounds, while saying she supports innovation and economic development.

evidence.title: Yellowhammer News: Sewell breaks with Tuberville, Trump on data centers, backs moratorium bill
evidence.quote: Make no mistake, I am not anti-technology. I am not anti-innovation. But it's clear that these projects are being built faster than we can establish the safeguards our communities deserve.
evidence.what_it_shows: Directly rejects Sen. Tuberville's argument that data centers are inevitable.

evidence.title: Alabama Daily News: Sewell wants to stop new data centers until guardrails are implemented
evidence.quote: The bill simply says, let's put common sense guardrails in place before this expansion continues,
evidence.what_it_shows: Video remarks stressing the pause is about guardrails first.

evidence.title: Cosponsor, Energy Bills Relief Act (H.R. 7977), Casten bill on household energy costs
evidence.what_it_shows: Joined a Democratic energy-affordability bill; cosponsorship confirmed on GovTrack, data center specifics not verified.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Backs targeted guardrails, mostly around elections and public data: she led a 2024 bipartisan letter asking DOJ, DHS and the EAC how they would counter AI used to deceive voters, cosponsored bills banning AI-made voting lies and requiring AI labels on political ads, and signed a Ways and Means letter on the IRS's use of AI on taxpayer data. She repeatedly says she is not anti-AI.

evidence.title: Press release: Reps. Sewell, Brown lead bipartisan letter on AI interference in the 2024 election
evidence.quote: We cannot allow bad actors to weaponize powerful AI tools to mislead voters, suppress turnout, and sow chaos.
evidence.what_it_shows: Led 31 colleagues asking federal agencies for their plan against AI-driven voter deception, with emphasis on Black and brown communities.

evidence.title: Cosponsor, Deceptive Practices and Voter Intimidation Prevention Act of 2025 (H.R. 4894)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making it illegal to spread lies about voting, including AI-made content, before federal elections.

evidence.title: Cosponsor, AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2026 (H.R. 9922)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring political ads to disclose when they were made with AI.

evidence.title: FedScoop: House Ways and Means Democrats demand answers on IRS's AI use to manage taxpayer data (Sewell a signer)
evidence.quote: Nearly a dozen House Ways & Means Committee Democrats are seeking details from the IRS about how the agency is deploying artificial intelligence to deal with legacy code used to manage taxpayer data.
evidence.what_it_shows: Signed an oversight letter pressing Treasury on AI tools touching sensitive taxpayer systems.

evidence.title: Press release: Sewell cosponsors AI data center pause (her framing of AI)
evidence.quote: I want America to lead the world in AI innovation, and I want Alabama to compete for the industries of the future. But innovation cannot come at the expense of the communities it is meant to serve.
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows she pairs guardrails with support for U.S. AI leadership rather than treating AI itself as an existential danger.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Supports targeted privacy and consumer rules: she joined the Taxpayer Data Protection Act to keep DOGE out of Treasury payment data, cosponsored the My Body, My Data Act on reproductive health data and the Safe Vehicle Access for Survivors Act on car data, and voted to force TikTok's sale. No break-up or Section 230 repeal stance found.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Sewell, House Democrats introduce Taxpayer Data Protection Act to stop Musk from invading Americans' privacy
evidence.quote: Elon Musk's takeover of the federal payment system is a dangerous invasion of the privacy of every American, and House Democrats are taking action to stop it,
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames access to sensitive government data as a privacy issue needing legal limits.

evidence.title: Cosponsor, My Body, My Data Act of 2023 (H.R. 3420)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed limits on companies collecting or sharing reproductive health data.

ai_risk.label: Mixed
ai_risk.summary: Thune has long favored a light touch: his 2023 Thune-Klobuchar bill relied on transparency reports and company self-certification, and in June 2025 he urged light-touch AI rules. But by September 2026 he was co-drafting a bipartisan frontier AI bill with Klobuchar and Cruz that would give AI labs a legal duty to mitigate catastrophic risks and require pre-release disclosure to Commerce. Mixed record, shifting toward targeted binding rules.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.3312 Artificial Intelligence Research, Innovation, and Accountability Act of 2024 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: His signature AI bill required transparency reports for high-impact AI and self-certification for critical-impact AI, a framework built to limit government intervention.

evidence.title: Press release: Thune, Klobuchar Lead Commerce Committee Colleagues in Introducing Bipartisan AI Bill
evidence.what_it_shows: Thune described the bill as basic rules of the road that protect consumers, let innovators thrive and limit government intervention, with guardrails only for the highest-risk AI uses.

evidence.title: FedScoop: Top Republican working on 'light touch' AI bill with focus on generative AI and self-certification system
evidence.quote: I can confirm that Sen. Thune is working on a light-touch AI bill that would help set some basic rules of the road that both protects consumers and entrepreneurs
evidence.what_it_shows: A Senate source described the approach as light touch; the draft let companies self-certify critical-impact systems with Commerce enforcement.

evidence.title: Press release: Thune Applauds Passage of Bipartisan AI Bill in Senate Commerce Committee
evidence.what_it_shows: After his bill cleared Commerce he pressed Leader Schumer for a floor vote on AI transparency legislation, again framing it as common-sense guardrails for the highest-risk uses.

evidence.title: Axios: Thune urges 'light touch' on AI regulations
evidence.what_it_shows: As Majority Leader he told Axios he wanted a light-touch approach to AI regulation while the state-law freeze was being debated.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4569 TAKE IT DOWN Act (118th)

evidence.what_it_shows: After an Anthropic researcher's extinction warning, Thune became a lead sponsor of a bill Cruz said addresses catastrophic biological and nuclear risks.

evidence.title: Politico: Senate AI safety bill's path forward remains unclear
evidence.what_it_shows: Drafts of the Klobuchar-Thune bill would give AI labs a legal duty to mitigate harms, require disclosure of advanced capabilities to Commerce before release, and let Commerce seek a court injunction, with no pre-approval regime and some state preemption; Thune declined comment.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.686 RESTRICT Act (118th)

He called the NDAA preemption push controversial, wants a bill that does not trample states' rights, and the frontier AI bill he is drafting in 2026 would preempt some state AI laws.

evidence.quote: I think the White House is working with senators and House members for that matter to try and come up with something that works but preserves states’ rights.
evidence.what_it_shows: He called the NDAA preemption provision controversial and said both sides were dug in, signaling he wants preemption paired with protection for states.

evidence.title: Politico: White House releases AI policy blueprint for Congress
evidence.what_it_shows: He told Politico a preemptive AI bill could be melded with a kids online safety package to attract Democrats, while admitting many Republicans worry about trampling states' rights.

evidence.title: Politico: Senate AI safety bill's path forward remains unclear
evidence.what_it_shows: The Klobuchar-Thune-Cruz drafts would preempt some state AI laws, which Commerce ranking member Cantwell attacked as a weak federal standard that could wipe out stronger state protections.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Welch's first concern is keeping data center costs off household electric bills. He cosponsored the Power for the People Act and led six New England senators demanding ISO New England make tech companies, not families, pay for new load. He has not called for a pause, and his REWIRE Act with Republican Dave McCormick would speed grid upgrades and permitting to meet rising demand.

evidence.title: Press release: Welch joins new bill to ensure Americans aren't footing the bill for big data centers (Power for the People Act)
evidence.quote: At the same time, energy prices are spiking across the country, saddling working families with higher utility bills and threatening the reliability of the grid. Data centers must be held accountable for the costs of their connection
evidence.what_it_shows: He is an original cosponsor of Van Hollen's bill making data centers pay for the transmission upgrades they cause and creating special rate classes for them.

evidence.title: Press release: Welch leads New England senators in call for answers from ISO New England about data centers and energy costs
evidence.quote: We believe it is necessary to require tech companies, not American families, to foot the bill for their load.
evidence.what_it_shows: He led Shaheen, Blumenthal, Reed, Markey and Whitehouse in asking the grid operator how it will protect residential ratepayers, citing a 13% rise in residential prices in 2025.

evidence.title: Press release: Welch, McCormick introduce bipartisan REWIRE Act to modernize America's electric grid and cut red tape
evidence.quote: We’re up against the clock when it comes to meeting America’s growing energy needs.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pairs ratepayer protection with faster grid buildout: the bill creates a NEPA categorical exclusion for reconductoring and other upgrades in existing rights-of-way to meet demand growth.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4727, Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a federal study of AI's energy, water and pollution footprint and a reporting system.

evidence.title: VTDigger: Vermont plugs into the data center conversation
evidence.what_it_shows: Vermont press reported Welch urging ISO-NE to require data centers to pay for their own electricity and grid upgrades as the state debated its own data center rules.

evidence.title: Seven Democratic senators' letter to FERC Chair Laura Swett urging action to stop data-center-driven rate hikes
evidence.what_it_shows: Senators urged FERC to reject transmission filings that spread data-center costs across regions, investigate cost allocation and PJM practices, resist queue-jumping for large fossil generators, standardize load forecasting, and prioritize residential ratepayers in the DOE-requested large-load interconnection rulemaking.

evidence.title: Six New England senators' letter to ISO New England CEO Vamsi Chadalavada on protecting ratepayers from data center growth
evidence.what_it_shows: Senators asked the New England grid operator how it will keep tech companies, not families, paying for data center load, citing a 13% rise in residential prices in 2025 and PJM's capacity price spike as a warning.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Welch backs specific guardrails rather than a pause: product liability for AI harms (AI LEAD Act), transparency about training data (his TRAIN Act), age checks for companion chatbots (GUARD Act), a right to control AI copies of one's voice and face (NO FAKES), and letters pressing Meta, Character.AI and others on children's safety. He also fought letting AI decide Medicare prior authorizations.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.2455, TRAIN Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Lets copyright holders subpoena AI training records to learn whether their work trained a model.

evidence.title: Press release: Welch leads bipartisan bill to protect musicians, artists, and creators from unauthorized AI training
evidence.quote: As AI evolves and gets more embedded into our daily lives, we need to set a higher standard for transparency.
evidence.what_it_shows: His own framing of the TRAIN Act, introduced with Blackburn, Schiff and Hawley.

evidence.title: Press release: Welch and Blackburn host 20+ music artists on Capitol Hill to discuss protecting creators from AI harm
evidence.quote: The TRAIN Act is an incredibly important, bipartisan bill to stand up to AI and give power back to creators.
evidence.what_it_shows: He continues to push the TRAIN Act and NO FAKES Act as creator protections against generative AI.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.2937, AI LEAD Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would let people harmed by an AI system sue the developer under product liability rules.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3062, GUARD Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require chatbot companies to verify ages and keep minors away from AI companions.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4591, NO FAKES Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Gives people a legal right to stop unauthorized AI replicas of their voice or likeness.

evidence.title: Press release (Sen. Padilla): Padilla, Welch probe AI chatbot apps on safeguards for children
evidence.quote: policymakers, parents, and their kids deserve to know what your companies are doing to protect users from these known risks
evidence.what_it_shows: He and Padilla wrote to Character.AI, Chai and Replika about self-harm risks and how their models handle mental health conversations.

evidence.title: Bipartisan letter of 10 senators to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on AI chatbots and children (reposted on Welch's site)
evidence.quote: While AIs have many uses, the wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined Hawley, Schatz and others demanding Meta explain chatbot policies that allowed romantic conversations with children and asking it to ban targeted ads to minors.

evidence.title: Press release: Welch joins bicameral bill to protect Medicare benefits from Trump administration's AI experiment
evidence.quote: Their newest plan to let AI take over important Medicare prior authorization decisions will be a disaster for providers and make it harder for seniors to get the care they need
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposes letting AI systems approve or deny medical care in traditional Medicare.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1633, TEST AI Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports government testbeds to check whether AI systems are safe and trustworthy.

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on AI chatbot policies permitting 'romantic or sensual' conversations with children
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators demanded details on how Meta's chatbot safety policies for minors were developed, asked for more visible disclosures and a ban on targeted ads to under-18 users, writing that 'the wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.'

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: Welch is an antitrust hawk on Big Tech. He cosponsors bills to sunset Section 230, toughen merger law, break up Google's control of online advertising, and pass the Kids Online Safety Act and COPPA 2.0. He demanded ByteDance shut down its Seedance video model over copyright theft and wants courts to scrutinize weak antitrust settlements.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3546, Sunset Section 230 Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would end the liability shield for online platforms to force Congress to write new rules.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.130, Competition and Antitrust Law Enforcement Reform Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Would make it harder for dominant companies to merge and shift the burden of proof onto the biggest deals.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1060, AMERICA Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would stop giant ad-tech firms like Google from controlling every side of the digital ad market.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1748, Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Imposes a duty of care and safety design rules on platforms used by minors.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.836, Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Updates children's privacy law to require consent for data collection and ban targeted ads to kids and teens.

evidence.title: Press release: After weak Live Nation-Ticketmaster antitrust deal, Welch joins bicameral bill on antitrust settlements
evidence.quote: Any backdoor corporate settlement needs to face real scrutiny before it’s allowed to move forward. We need stronger antitrust laws that protect hardworking families.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants courts to review antitrust settlements, including at the FTC, and calls for stronger antitrust law overall.

evidence.title: Press release: Welch, Blackburn urge ByteDance to immediately shut down Seedance 2.0 AI video model
evidence.quote: Seedance 2.0 poses a direct threat to the American intellectual property system and, more broadly, to the constitutional rights and economic livelihoods of our creative community.
evidence.what_it_shows: He and Blackburn accused ByteDance of industrial-scale copyright infringement and deepfake abuse and demanded the model be shut down.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.278, Kids Off Social Media Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would bar children under 13 from social media and limit algorithmic feeds for teens.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.1671 (118th), Digital Platform Commission Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported creating a new federal agency to police large online platforms.

evidence.title: Schatz-led bipartisan letter of 10 senators to Zuckerberg on safeguards for children using Meta AI chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators told Meta they were 'alarmed' by its chatbot policies, asked how its minor-safety rules were developed, and demanded Meta ban targeted ads to under-18s, improve disclosures and add mental-health referrals.

evidence.title: Padilla and Welch letters to CEOs of Character.AI, Chai and Luka (Replika) on companion-chatbot safety for children
evidence.what_it_shows: Two senators asked three AI companion companies how they train models to handle self-harm and mental-health conversations and what safety measures they use, citing the Florida teen's suicide linked to Character.AI.

evidence.title: Blackburn and Welch roundtable statement with artists supporting the NO FAKES Act and TRAIN Act
evidence.what_it_shows: During the Recording Academy's advocacy day, the two senators said the NO FAKES Act would protect creators from deepfakes and the TRAIN Act would let them find out when their copyrighted works train AI models, urging Congress to pass both.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Welch opposes Washington overriding state AI laws. He joined the States' Right to Regulate AI Act to block Trump's executive order, saying the order ties states' hands and threatens consumer safety, while also calling for federal rules to be built on top of state protections.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.3557, States' Right to Regulate AI Act
evidence.what_it_shows: The bill preserves state authority over AI and would bar implementation of the preemption executive order.

evidence.title: Press release: Welch joins legislation to block Trump's illegal executive order undermining AI state safeguards
evidence.quote: At a moment when we should be putting every effort into finding ways to make AI safer, this executive order threatens consumer rights and safety by tying states’ hands
evidence.what_it_shows: His own words opposing the Dec 11 2025 executive order; he says Congress must reverse it and then write federal policies that protect people.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on Senate roll call 363, Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted with the 99-1 majority to remove the state AI-law moratorium; nearly every senator did, so this alone is weak evidence. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Welch has not spoken publicly on Nvidia's H20 or H200 sales. evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.686 (118th), RESTRICT Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported letting the government review and block technology from adversary countries such as China.

members.signature: Judiciary Democrat who partners with Republicans on AI creator protections (his TRAIN Act, NO FAKES), fights federal preemption of state AI laws, and leads New England senators pressing grid operators to make data centers pay their own way.

quote.text: We cannot force everyday Americans to subsidize profits of the multi-billion dollar AI industry.
