data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Wyden wants data centers to pay their own way: he proposes stripping their tax breaks and adding a federal excise tax, has demanded Big Tech disclose water use in Oregon, and warns communities to be cautious. He has declined to endorse a construction moratorium and calls data centers important to national security.

evidence.title: Nextgov: Senate Finance ranking member Wyden proposes excise tax on new data centers (white paper)
evidence.quote: American communities are rightfully questioning whether the rapid buildout of data centers across the nation will benefit them, as local disruptions rise and Americans grow concerned about the long-term career prospects of millions of workers
evidence.what_it_shows: His Aug 6, 2026 white paper would remove tax incentives for data center construction and levy a gross-receipts excise tax on AI data centers to fund displaced workers.

evidence.title: Press release: Wyden demands Google, Apple, Meta and Amazon answer questions about data centers' water impact
evidence.quote: many communities in my state are concerned about how these centers could contribute to water scarcity in the coming years, especially as our state grapples with persistent drought
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed the four CEOs on closed-loop cooling and public water-use disclosure, with answers due May 29, 2026.

evidence.title: Letter: Wyden and Merkley to Gov. Kotek's Data Center Advisory Committee
evidence.quote: While we acknowledge that data centers are critical to American national security, can help ensure technological advancement, and create good union jobs
evidence.what_it_shows: He balances the benefits against ratepayer costs, water, farmland, tribal rights and transparency, asking the state to set guardrails rather than stop projects.

evidence.title: E&E News: Lawmakers oppose greens' call for data center moratorium (Wyden declines to endorse)
evidence.quote: I think that there has been significant abuse of taxpayer money as it relates to data centers
evidence.what_it_shows: He would not yet endorse a nationwide construction moratorium but said tax breaks for data centers are being abused.

evidence.title: Herald and News: Wyden town halls in Klamath Falls and Lakeview
evidence.quote: Big promises are a stop light for caution
evidence.what_it_shows: He told constituents to be very concerned about companies promoting AI data centers and urged landowners to organize against projects that harm farms and wetlands.

evidence.title: E&E News: Wyden proposes new taxes on data centers
evidence.what_it_shows: Reporters describe his plan as a low single-digit excise tax plus a ban on using existing tax breaks like Opportunity Zones for data centers, less aggressive than the Sanders moratorium.

evidence.title: S.4727 Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs a federal study and reporting system for AI's energy, water and pollution footprint.

evidence.title: Markey-McClellan bicameral letter to EPA urging withdrawal of proposed rule letting data centers and power plants begin construction before air permits
evidence.what_it_shows: Sixteen lawmakers told EPA to withdraw its May 2026 proposal redefining 'begin actual construction' so data centers and fossil plants can pour foundations and install wiring before New Source Review permits, saying it turns the Clean Air Act's preconstruction safeguards 'on its head.'

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Wyden pushes targeted rules: mandatory bias audits of automated decision systems, child safeguards for chatbots, removing Grok over sexual deepfakes, blocking AI-built surveillance profiles of Americans, and ending AI-driven Medicare denials. He also co-wrote a bill with Cruz limiting government pressure on AI systems, showing a civil-liberties rather than pause-the-technology approach.

evidence.title: S.2164 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: His signature AI bill, introduced four times since 2019, would require large companies to test automated decision systems for bias and harm and report to the FTC.

evidence.title: KLCC: Wyden on Section 230 and algorithms
evidence.quote: When it comes to algorithms, we have some real challenges
evidence.what_it_shows: He distinguishes algorithms from Section 230 protections and points to his Algorithmic Accountability Act as his plan for them.

evidence.title: Schatz-led bipartisan letter of 10 senators to Meta on children and AI chatbots (Wyden a signer)
evidence.quote: The wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined a demand that Meta explain chatbot policies allowing romantic conversations with minors and ban targeted ads to under-18s.

evidence.title: Press release: Wyden, Markey and Lujan urge Apple and Google to remove X and Grok from app stores
evidence.quote: Turning a blind eye to X’s egregious behavior would make a mockery of your moderation practices.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants app stores to pull an AI product that generated nonconsensual sexual images of women and children at scale.

evidence.title: Gizmodo: Wyden warns of mass surveillance amid Pentagon's fight with Anthropic
evidence.quote: Creating AI profiles of Americans based on that data represents a chilling expansion of mass surveillance that should not be allowed, regardless of what the current, outdated laws on the books say.
evidence.what_it_shows: He sided with Anthropic's refusal to allow Claude for mass domestic surveillance and pledged legislation to stop AI profiling built on purchased data.

evidence.title: Healthcare Dive: Senate Democrats move to roll back Medicare AI prior authorization pilot (WISeR)
evidence.quote: The last thing seniors need is even more AI denying the care they need.
evidence.what_it_shows: He led a Congressional Review Act resolution to end an AI-driven Medicare prior authorization program.

evidence.title: KATU: Wyden, Merkley introduce ICE Out of Our Faces Act
evidence.quote: I’m glad to work with Senators Markey and Merkley to protect Americans against harassment and biometric surveillance by Trump’s handpicked militia.
evidence.what_it_shows: He co-leads a bill to ban ICE and CBP from using facial recognition and other biometric AI.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Cruz and Wyden unveil bipartisan JAWBONE Act against government censorship via platforms and AI systems
evidence.quote: Regular Americans can’t count on those companies to stand up to government jawboning, they need a way to level the playing field
evidence.what_it_shows: With Commerce Chair Cruz he would let people sue when government coerces platforms, AI systems or broadcasters over content, a limit on government power rather than a new mandate on AI firms.

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on AI chatbot policies permitting 'romantic or sensual' conversations with children
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators demanded details on how Meta's chatbot safety policies for minors were developed, asked for more visible disclosures and a ban on targeted ads to under-18 users, writing that 'the wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.'

tech_regulation.label: Mixed
tech_regulation.summary: Mixed but leaning toward targeted rules. Wyden is aggressive on privacy and antitrust: he sponsors bans on surveillance advertising and warrantless data purchases and cosponsors tougher merger law. Yet he co-wrote Section 230 and still defends it, voted no on the Kids Online Safety Act in 2024 over encryption and censorship fears, and backed extending the TikTok deadline. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: Both tech_regulation sources show Wyden resisting new platform regulation: he defends Section 230 against repeal and was one of three no votes on KOSA/COPPA 2.0 (on privacy/encryption/censorship grounds). His pro-regulat

evidence.title: KLCC: Wyden remains in support of Section 230, the law he authored 31 years ago
evidence.quote: What we said is that individuals who post on the internet are responsible for that content, not the people who run the platform
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposes the dozen-plus bills to repeal or sunset Section 230, arguing it protects ordinary speakers more than Big Tech.

evidence.title: The Hill: These 3 senators voted against children online safety bills (Wyden statement on KOSA no vote)
evidence.quote: I fear this bill could be used to sue services that offer privacy-enhancing technologies like encryption or anonymity features that are essential to young people’s ability to communicate securely and privately
evidence.what_it_shows: He was one of three senators to vote against KOSA and COPPA 2.0 in 2024, citing encryption and the risk of censoring LGBTQ and reproductive health information.

evidence.title: S.130 Competition and Antitrust Law Enforcement Reform Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs making it harder for giant companies, including Big Tech, to merge and buy rivals.

evidence.title: S.2833 Banning Surveillance Advertising Act of 2023 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He would ban ads targeted using tracked personal data, a core Big Tech business model.

evidence.title: S.2576 Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants to stop government agencies from buying Americans' data from brokers without a warrant.

evidence.title: S.836 Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA 2.0)
evidence.what_it_shows: Despite his 2024 no vote on the combined package, he cosponsors the kids' privacy bill in this Congress.

evidence.title: S.103 Extend the TikTok Deadline Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported giving TikTok more time before a forced sale or ban, a lighter-touch position.

evidence.title: Schatz-led bipartisan letter of 10 senators to Zuckerberg on safeguards for children using Meta AI chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators told Meta they were 'alarmed' by its chatbot policies, asked how its minor-safety rules were developed, and demanded Meta ban targeted ads to under-18s, improve disclosures and add mental-health referrals.

evidence.title: Wyden, Markey and Lujan open letter to Apple and Google to remove X and Grok from app stores over AI-generated sexual images
evidence.what_it_shows: Three Democratic senators told Apple and Google to pull X and Grok from their app stores until Elon Musk stops Grok from generating nonconsensual sexualized images of women and children, saying inaction would 'make a mockery' of their moderation claims.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Wyden cosponsors the States' Right to Regulate AI Act, which would bar the federal government from wiping out state AI laws. No separate speech or statement on the moratorium, the Dec 2025 executive order or the March 2026 White House framework was found, so confidence rests on the cosponsorship.

evidence.title: S.3557 States' Right to Regulate AI Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He signed on to the main Senate bill protecting states' power to pass their own AI rules against federal preemption.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted to strip the moratorium; nearly every senator did, so this vote is weak evidence by itself. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Wyden opposes selling Nvidia's advanced chips to China and wants export controls kept tight. He signed the December 2025 letter attacking the H200 decision, led a November 2025 letter demanding Trump restore suspended chip export controls, and joined a 2026 letter questioning Blackwell chip transfers to the UAE's G42.

evidence.title: Warren, Schumer and colleagues press Lutnick on greenlighting H200 chip sales to China (Wyden a signer)
evidence.quote: The President’s dangerous decision to give away critical national security controls represents a significant departure from longstanding bipartisan efforts to ensure that U.S. technology does not turbocharge China’s military and technological capabilities.
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined seven Democrats objecting to Nvidia H200 exports to China and questioning Nvidia's lobbying and donations before the decision.

evidence.title: Press release: Wyden, Schumer, Warren and Cortez Masto press Trump to restore export controls after trade talks
evidence.quote: Trump’s selling off our tech advantage to China because he desperately needed a bargaining chip to end his foolish trade war
evidence.what_it_shows: He led a letter demanding the administration reverse a trade-deal concession that suspended BIS enforcement of export controls on advanced AI chips.

evidence.title: Unchained: Senate Democrats demand hearings on UAE's $500 million stake in Trump crypto venture (Wyden a signer)
evidence.what_it_shows: The letter he signed cites the approval of 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell chips for UAE firm G42 despite intelligence warnings that China could access them.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Massie says data center decisions belong to local communities and should be regulated at the local level. He called Trump's 'backwards and poor' remark insensitive, mocked a MAGA loyalty test on data centers, warned that overriding local zoning is 'very dangerous,' and opposed a bill exempting data centers from environmental review. He has not called for a moratorium.

evidence.title: The Hill: Massie on Fox News calls data center companies 'insensitive,' wants local regulation
evidence.quote: I don't think you should let data reign without any kind of regulation at the local level
evidence.what_it_shows: He rejected Trump's 'let Data Reign' message and said local people must decide where data centers go.

evidence.title: WHAS11 interview (via Yahoo News): Massie says Trump's data center comments will cost the GOP in the midterms
evidence.quote: These are local decisions. Just because you have concerns about conserving farmland in your community doesn't mean you're backwards or ignorant or poor as the president suggested.
evidence.what_it_shows: He sided with rural communities and a state legislator defending local bans and moratoria, and called Trump's remarks insensitive.

evidence.title: X post reported by Attack of the Fanboy: Massie mocks Trump's data center directive
evidence.quote: New directive from the leader: MAGA is required to support all Data Centers, no questions asked.
evidence.what_it_shows: He publicly refused to treat support for data centers as a party loyalty test.

evidence.title: E&E News: Massie on the budget bill provision that would have overridden local data center zoning
evidence.quote: It's a state and local issue, and I think if we try to override their ability to regulate that stuff, it's very dangerous.
evidence.what_it_shows: He objected to a federal override of local zoning for data centers that appeared in a version of the reconciliation bill.

evidence.title: Earthjustice account of the Protect American AI Act: Massie said he would vote against the data center carve-out bill
evidence.quote: no industry deserves special treatment under the law
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed a House Judiciary bill that would have exempted data centers from environmental review and limited lawsuits; the bill was shelved.

evidence.title: Fox Business clip: Massie and RNC chair Joe Gruters clash over AI data center expansion
evidence.what_it_shows: The clip summary says Massie argued for local control and regulation to keep data centers from taking over pastures and neighborhoods, while Gruters stressed national security and China.

ai_risk.label: Mixed
ai_risk.summary: Mixed. Massie opposes new federal mandates on AI and online content: he was one of two House members to vote against the TAKE IT DOWN Act and voted against the KIDS Act with its chatbot rules. But he wants to cut off federal money for AI-powered surveillance cameras, and after an AI deepfake ad helped end his career he warned about older voters being fooled by AI.

evidence.title: House roll call 104 (2025): Nay on S. 146 TAKE IT DOWN Act (one of only two Nays)
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposed the federal law criminalizing AI sexual deepfakes and forcing platform takedowns, which passed 409 to 2. Recorded vote: Nay.

evidence.title: House roll call 228 (2026): Nay on H.R. 7757 KIDS Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted against the House kids online safety package that included rules for AI chatbots and minors. Recorded vote: Nay.

evidence.title: The Hill: Massie unveils the Flock-Off Act to defund AI license plate reader and biometric surveillance cameras
evidence.quote: The Flock-Off Act withholds federal money from municipalities and police departments that deploy Flock cameras to surveil law-abiding citizens. Federal taxpayers should not be forced to fund the surveillance state
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants to block federal funding for AI-driven government surveillance systems.

evidence.title: Louisville Public Media: Massie reacts to the AI deepfake 'throuple' attack ad
evidence.quote: It's frankly an insult to older voters who don't know that AI exists.
evidence.what_it_shows: He condemned the AI-generated ad as beyond the pale but did not call for new AI rules.

evidence.title: HuffPost: Massie's social media response to the AI-generated attack ad
evidence.quote: It reeks of desperation, but they're hoping the older generation won't realize it's an AI generated lie
evidence.what_it_shows: He called the deepfake disgusting and defamatory; a former colleague said it violated the TAKE IT DOWN Act he had voted against.

evidence.title: WLWT: Massie on Meet the Press says AI videos fooled older voters and contributed to his primary loss
evidence.quote: It was actually very effective on the Boomers.
evidence.what_it_shows: He blamed AI deepfakes for misleading voters but expressed confidence younger voters will not be fooled, rather than calling for regulation.

His regulatory energy goes the other way, toward limiting government data purchases and surveillance cameras.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 564 Repeal the TikTok Ban Act

evidence.what_it_shows: Opposed a federal platform takedown mandate. Recorded vote: Nay.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 4639 Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stopping police and spy agencies from buying Americans' data from brokers; his privacy focus targets government, not tech companies.

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Schatz has not taken a stand for or against building data centers. In a January 2026 floor speech he named AI data center load as one reason there are not enough electrons on the grid and bills are rising, but he blamed the Trump administration's limits on solar and wind, and his answer is more cheap clean power rather than limits on data centers.

evidence.title: Press release and floor speech: Schatz: Trump Is Intentionally Raising The Price Of Electricity
evidence.quote: we've got all this AI data center load coming up ... There are not enough electrons on the grid. What happens when there's not enough of something? The people selling that thing raise the price.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats AI data center demand as a real driver of higher bills but frames the fix as more solar and clean energy, not slowing data centers.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Schatz is one of the Senate's most active Democrats on specific AI guardrails: labels on AI-made content, parental controls and limits on chatbots for kids, whistleblower protections, bias testing, and safety disclosures from frontier AI companies. He is also drafting an AI excise tax to fund worker retraining. He has not called for licensing or a pause on advanced AI.

evidence.title: Sponsor: AI Labeling Act of 2026 (S.4915)
evidence.what_it_shows: His signature bill would require visible and machine-readable labels on AI-generated images, video, audio and text.

evidence.title: Press release: Schatz, Curtis, Warner introduce bipartisan legislation to provide more transparency on AI-generated content
evidence.quote: if any digital content is made by AI, it should be labeled so that people are aware and aren't fooled or scammed
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants a mandatory disclosure rule enforced by the FTC, citing deepfakes and AI voice-clone scams.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: CHATBOT Act (S.4407)
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-led with Sen. Cruz a bill requiring family accounts, default protective settings, parental consent and no targeted ads for kids on AI chatbots.

evidence.title: Press release: Schatz, Cruz introduce new bill to protect kids on AI chatbot platforms
evidence.what_it_shows: The release says chatbots pose real risks to minors, including inappropriate content and addictive features, and that AI companies have used rewards and targeted ads to keep adolescents engaged.

evidence.title: Press release: Schatz, Britt, colleagues press AI companies to commit to timely, consistent safety disclosures on models (letters to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft, xAI, Character.AI, Luka
evidence.quote: If AI companies struggle to predict and mitigate relatively well-understood risks, it raises concerns about their ability to manage more complex risks
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked frontier labs to publish consistent model cards and honor their Seoul Summit commitments on national security risks like cyber and bio misuse.

evidence.title: Press release: Schatz leads bipartisan group of 10 senators in pressing Meta for safeguards around children's engagement with AI chatbots
evidence.quote: The wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.
evidence.what_it_shows: He led a bipartisan demand that Meta explain policies that let chatbots have romantic conversations with children.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI Whistleblower Protection Act (S.1792)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports protecting AI company employees who report safety problems.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 (S.2164)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports required bias and harm testing of automated decision systems; he also cosponsored the 2023 version (S.2892).

evidence.title: Axios exclusive: Schatz plots AI jobs bills (AI excise tax for retraining, automatic response if unemployment passes 5.5%)
evidence.quote: AI is already changing how people work, and it's bringing real risks: massive job losses, increased workplace surveillance, and weaker bargaining power for workers. We need to get ahead of it
evidence.what_it_shows: He is planning a progressive excise tax on AI company revenue to fund retraining, treating job loss as a central AI risk.

evidence.title: Press release: Schatz presses Commerce Secretary nominee Howard Lutnick on AI safety (Senate Commerce hearing)
evidence.quote: What do we do in place of this and how quickly can we get it done? Because that part of this was one of the few things that we were not arguing about when it comes to AI policy.
evidence.what_it_shows: He objected to Trump's repeal of the Biden AI order and pushed to keep the AI Safety Institute's work going.

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on AI chatbot policies permitting 'romantic or sensual' conversations with children
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators demanded details on how Meta's chatbot safety policies for minors were developed, asked for more visible disclosures and a ban on targeted ads to under-18 users, writing that 'the wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.'

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Schatz's signature cause is getting kids off social media: he sponsors a bill to ban under-13s and stop algorithmic feeds for teens, and cosponsors KOSA and COPPA 2.0. He also backs tougher antitrust rules and platform transparency. His focus is targeted rules rather than break-ups or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: Sponsor: Kids Off Social Media Act (S.278)
evidence.what_it_shows: His bipartisan bill with Sen. Cruz bans kids under 13 from social media and blocks personalized feeds for anyone under 17; he sponsored the same bill in 2024 (S.4213).

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (S.1748)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care for platforms toward minors.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act (S.836)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports updating kids' privacy law to require permission before collecting data on teens and to ban targeted ads to them.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Competition and Antitrust Law Enforcement Reform Act of 2025 (S.130)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports tougher merger rules aimed in part at Big Tech; he also cosponsored the 2024 version (S.4308).

evidence.title: Sponsor: Internet PACT Act (S.483)
evidence.what_it_shows: Led a bipartisan bill making large platforms explain content rules and remove court-ordered illegal content, a targeted Section 230 reform.

evidence.title: Kauai Now: Schatz, Senate colleagues press Zuckerberg after reports Meta AI bots spoke romantically with kids
evidence.quote: Meta has strong financial incentives to design chatbots that maximize the time users spend engaged, including by posing as a child's girlfriend or producing extreme content
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats Meta's engagement incentives as a reason for outside rules, including a ban on targeted ads to minors.

evidence.title: Schatz-led bipartisan letter of 10 senators to Zuckerberg on safeguards for children using Meta AI chatbots
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators told Meta they were 'alarmed' by its chatbot policies, asked how its minor-safety rules were developed, and demanded Meta ban targeted ads to under-18s, improve disclosures and add mental-health referrals.

evidence.title: Blunt Rochester-led letter of 8 senators to Alphabet, Meta, X, TikTok, Snap and Reddit on sexualized AI-generated images
evidence.what_it_shows: Eight Democratic senators demanded the platforms explain their policies for AI 'undressing' deepfakes, including of minors, preserve related documents, and describe how they remove images and notify victims.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Schatz strongly opposes Washington blocking state AI laws. He wrote the Senate GUARDRAILS Act to repeal Trump's December 2025 executive order against state AI regulation, signed the Commerce Democrats' June 2025 letter calling the moratorium a trampling of states' rights, and voted to strip the moratorium from the tax bill.

evidence.title: Sponsor: GUARDRAILS Act (S.4216)
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would block the executive order so states do not lose federal funds for passing AI safeguards.

evidence.title: Press release: Schatz, colleagues introduce legislation to repeal Trump's AI moratorium
evidence.quote: Discouraging states from enacting common-sense regulation that protects people from potential AI harms is dangerous. Congress has a responsibility to get this technology right, but states must not be penalized for acting in the public interest in the meantime.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants Congress to legislate eventually but insists states keep the power to act now, a direct rejection of preemption.

evidence.title: Commerce Committee Democrats' letter to Chairman Cruz on the reconciliation Commerce title, including the AI moratorium (Schatz a signer)
evidence.quote: the AI moratorium proposal tramples states' rights and holds the $42 billion BEAD program hostage
evidence.what_it_shows: He signed on to the Democrats' objection to the 10-year state AI law moratorium before the Senate vote.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (Schatz voted Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted to remove the moratorium, consistent with his letter and later bill. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Schatz wants tight limits on advanced chips going to China. He led seven Senate Democrats in calling Trump's decision to allow Nvidia H200 sales to China a colossal economic and national security failure, and he cosponsors the Chip Security Act requiring location verification on exported chips.

evidence.title: Press release: Schatz, Coons, Shaheen, Reed, Warren, Kim, Bennet, Slotkin statement on President Trump's decision to allow the export of advanced NVIDIA H200 AI chips to China
evidence.quote: The Trump administration's announcement that it will allow the export of advanced H200 AI chips to China is a colossal economic and national security failure.
evidence.what_it_shows: He led the Democratic response opposing H200 sales and demanded the president reverse course.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Chip Security Act (S.1705)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring exported advanced chips to carry location verification so they cannot be smuggled to China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025 (S.1638)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports barring the federal government from using AI made by companies in China and other rival countries.

members.signature: Senate Commerce Democrat behind the AI Labeling Act, the Kids Off Social Media Act, the CHATBOT Act with Cruz, and the GUARDRAILS Act to protect state AI laws; a leading critic of H200 chip sales to China.

quote.text: Embracing the amazing possibilities of AI can't come at the cost of leaving Americans vulnerable to its profound risks, which is exactly what President Trump's Executive Order tries to do

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Warren's line is that tech companies, not families, must pay for data center power. She opened an investigation of seven hyperscalers over utility bills, won a mandatory federal energy survey of data centers with Sen. Hawley, and proposes an excise tax on data center energy use. She has not backed a moratorium.

evidence.title: Press release: Warren, Van Hollen and Blumenthal open investigation into Big Tech data centers and utility costs
evidence.quote: Through these utility price increases, American families bankroll the electricity costs of trillion-dollar tech companies.
evidence.what_it_shows: Letters to Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, CoreWeave, Digital Realty and Equinix demanding they pay a greater share of grid costs up front.

evidence.title: The Verge: Warren-Hawley letter asks EIA for mandatory annual data center energy reporting
evidence.quote: establish a mandatory annual reporting requirement for data centers
evidence.what_it_shows: A bipartisan push for transparency so the public can check the Ratepayer Protection Pledge.

evidence.title: Press release: Warren, Hawley secure mandatory energy-use reporting requirements for data centers
evidence.quote: Americans deserve to know how much energy data centers are sucking up and what that's doing to their utility bills
evidence.what_it_shows: EIA agreed to a mandatory data center survey in response to her request.

evidence.title: Time op-ed: Why We Need to Tax AI
evidence.quote: By imposing a reasonable excise tax on the energy used by data centers, families could recoup some of the gains of AI, while America continues to stay competitive in the AI race.
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants to tax data center energy use while keeping the US competitive, a protect-ratepayers-first stance rather than a pause.

evidence.title: Seven Democratic senators' letter to FERC Chair Laura Swett urging action to stop data-center-driven rate hikes
evidence.what_it_shows: Senators urged FERC to reject transmission filings that spread data-center costs across regions, investigate cost allocation and PJM practices, resist queue-jumping for large fossil generators, standardize load forecasting, and prioritize residential ratepayers in the DOE-requested large-load interconnection rulemaking.

evidence.title: Warren-Hawley bipartisan letter to EIA Administrator Tristan Abbey urging mandatory annual energy-use reporting by data centers
evidence.what_it_shows: A left-right pair asked the Energy Information Administration to require data centers and other large loads to report hourly and peak consumption, prices paid, deposits, demand flexibility, AI vs. cloud energy use, and who pays for triggered grid upgrades, so the public can check compliance with the voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Warren treats AI mainly as a financial-stability and civil-rights problem: she warns the AI investment boom could trigger a 2008-style crash, sponsors an AI Bubble Transparency Act, and cosponsors bills requiring bias testing of automated systems. She has not called for licensing or a pause on advanced AI.

evidence.title: The Verge: Warren says an AI failure could trigger the next financial crisis (Vanderbilt Policy Accelerator remarks)
evidence.quote: the first big stumble will have everyone running for the exits, potentially triggering destabilizing losses in the financial sector and another 2008-style financial crisis.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her AI risk framing is about debt, opaque financing and systemic risk, and she says Congress should step in.

evidence.title: S.4743 AI Bubble Transparency Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would make companies disclose their AI exposure to investors.

evidence.title: S.2164 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require big companies to test automated decision systems for bias and harm.

evidence.title: S.3308 Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports binding anti-discrimination rules and bias testing for AI.

evidence.title: CNBC: Warren questions Pentagon's supply chain risk label on Anthropic
evidence.quote: appears to be retaliation
evidence.what_it_shows: She challenged the Defense Department's blacklisting of a safety-focused AI company, an oversight action rather than a stance on model risk.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: Warren is among the most aggressive Big Tech critics in the Senate: she has proposed a new federal regulator for online platforms, backs breaking up Google's ad business and blocking AI cloud monopolies in defense contracts, and wants to tax AI companies.

evidence.title: Press release: Warren, Graham unveil bipartisan Digital Consumer Protection Commission Act
evidence.quote: For too long, giant tech companies have exploited consumers' data, invaded Americans' privacy, threatened our national security, and stomped out competition in our economy
evidence.what_it_shows: Proposed a new commission with power to regulate online platforms alongside the FTC and DOJ.

evidence.title: S.1060 AMERICA Act

evidence.title: S.1775 Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act of 2025

evidence.title: Press release: Schakowsky and Warren press USTR on whether Big Tech is using the USMCA review to block AI rules
evidence.quote: They are now attempting to use trade deals to preempt even the federal government from effectively regulating AI.
evidence.what_it_shows: She sees Big Tech lobbying on trade as an end run around AI regulation.

evidence.title: Time op-ed: Why We Need to Tax AI
evidence.quote: But it starts by acknowledging: it's time to tax AI and invest in people.
evidence.what_it_shows: Calls for taxing AI companies and data centers and a wealth tax to share AI's gains.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act

preemption.label: Let states regulate

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: King treats the most powerful AI models as a national security danger and wants binding federal oversight. He co-authored a 2024 framework for oversight of frontier AI hardware, development and deployment, cosponsored a bill creating an AI Safety Review Office to test frontier models before release, and cosponsored the AI LEAD Act letting people sue AI makers. He also backs deepfake and chatbot-adjacent guardrails, and personally uses Claude while warning to be careful with its analysis. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: Sources support strong federal oversight of frontier models (Safety Review Office, CFIUS-style pre-deployment evaluations, data center reporting), but every King source frames it narrowly: safeguards 'would apply to only

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Cramer is an enthusiastic booster of AI data centers in North Dakota, calling it a race with China and telling companies to bring their own on-site power. He pairs that with conditions: states must keep their planning authority over grid hookups, and other ratepayers should not be stuck with the bill.

evidence.title: WDAY Radio: Senator Cramer urges urgency, local power to fuel North Dakota's AI revolution
evidence.quote: This is a race right now, it is the fourth industrial revolution.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants North Dakota to build AI data centers fast, calls it data farming, and urges companies to put power generation on site behind the meter rather than lean on regulated utilities.

evidence.title: The Flag (AM 1100): Cramer on Armada's modular AI data center arriving at GrandSKY
evidence.quote: We have to be careful not to go too slow
evidence.what_it_shows: He celebrated a new data center project he helped recruit, framed the buildout as a technology race with China, and said modular designs can answer public concerns about energy use.

evidence.title: E&E News: Wright's data center push draws Republican scrutiny
evidence.quote: We have to strike a balance that doesn’t completely dismiss a state’s rights or, you know, reduce the importance of or diminish the importance of a planning process.
evidence.what_it_shows: As a former state utility regulator he is uncertain about a federal push to speed data center grid hookups if it sidelines state planning, and wants states a path to appeal FERC decisions.

evidence.title: Press release: Cramer, Fedorchak introduce FAIR Act (Cramer sponsors Senate companion S. 3287)
evidence.quote: Too often, ratepayers in North Dakota are left holding the bag after the dust settles on failed energy policies enacted by other states.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants a user-pay rule so electric bills are not shifted onto people who do not benefit from new transmission lines.

evidence.title: Grand Forks Herald: AI firm unveils mobile data center at Grand Sky event (Cramer remarks)
evidence.quote: This just becomes one more tool to attract, not just another Northrop Grumman or General Atomics, but another inventor, another college student
evidence.what_it_shows: Speaking at the unveiling, he called the data center one more tool to attract defense firms and inventors to Grand Forks, showing he treats these projects as economic wins.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Cramer talks about AI as a race with China that America must win by building faster and getting government out of the way; we found no statements treating advanced AI as a danger needing new federal rules. He did oppose blocking states from regulating AI, so he is not purely hands-off.

evidence.title: WDAY Radio: Cramer on the AI revolution and North Dakota's role
evidence.quote: This is a race right now, it is the fourth industrial revolution.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI as an economic race to win, not a risk to contain, and says the state should get out of its own way.

evidence.title: Ricketts-led letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick calling for a stable regulatory environment to win the AI race (Cramer signed)
evidence.quote: The Trump administration should not return to Biden’s tiers and caps that confused close allies and partners.
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined senators praising the administration for unshackling AI and asking for lighter, predictable rules so American AI can spread abroad.

evidence.title: Punchbowl News: GOP resistance to AI moratorium intensifies (Cramer against Cruz proposal)
evidence.what_it_shows: Counterpoint: he told Punchbowl he opposed forcing states to choose between regulating AI and getting federal AI infrastructure money, so he did not want state AI guardrails wiped out.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (119th S. 1748)

evidence.what_it_shows: He backs banning connected cars and car software from companies tied to China, Russia, Iran, or North Korea.

evidence.what_it_shows: He supported forcing TikTok's sale on national security grounds.

evidence.quote: Big tech, the corporate media, and the Administration have no credibility in determining what is and isn’t ‘misinformation,’

No statement found on Nvidia H20 or H200 sales.

evidence.title: Congressional reactions to former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon's resignation warning that AI 'could kill us all by the end of the decade'
evidence.what_it_shows: After Coxon's viral Sept 8 post and Anthropic alignment lead Evan Hubinger's '>10% within the next decade' extinction estimate, members of both parties publicly framed AI as an existential risk and called for hearings, a kill-switch law, a superintelligence ban or a pause.

evidence.title: Cruz says AI warning 'scary as hell,' calls for 'substantially more regulation' but opposes slowing U.S. AI versus China
evidence.what_it_shows: The Senate Commerce chairman, long an opponent of AI regulation, said he takes catastrophic AI risk seriously (citing Elon Musk's 10-20% estimate that AI destroys humanity within 10 years) and that his committee may mark up a bill with Thune and Klobuchar on AI-enabled biological and nuclear threats, while warning that shutting down U.S. AI would let China 'catch up in six months and soar ahead.'

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Pocan says data center builders should pay for all the infrastructure they need, including power lines, and he cosponsored a bill banning AI data centers on federal land. He says Sanders' call for a pause points at the right problems but will not pass this Congress, and he sees siting fights as mostly state and local.

evidence.title: Wisconsin Watch: Data centers become a flashpoint in Wisconsin politics
evidence.quote: The focus should be more on if they're going to build something, they should have to pay for all the infrastructure costs related to it
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants developers, not ratepayers or towns, to carry the full cost of power lines and other infrastructure.

evidence.title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act (H.R.9939)
evidence.what_it_shows: He is an original cosponsor of Rep. Tlaib's bill to ban AI data centers on federal land, a partial block on new sites.

evidence.what_it_shows: The release names Pocan among the original cosponsors and frames the bill as protecting public land, water and neighborhoods from Big Tech data centers.

evidence.title: Business Insider: Bernie Sanders's AI data center pause isn't catching on in Congress yet
evidence.quote: He's pointing out the right problems.
evidence.what_it_shows: He agrees with Sanders' concerns about data centers but said this Congress is not going to enact a pause, stopping short of endorsing a moratorium himself.

evidence.title: Wisconsin Watch: Data centers become a flashpoint in Wisconsin politics
evidence.quote: We don't have as much, in fact very little to do with it at a federal level
evidence.what_it_shows: He sees data center decisions as mainly a state and gubernatorial issue, which tempers how far he pushes federal action.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Pocan wants Congress to write real AI rules and backs specific guardrails: a ban on AI discrimination with mandatory bias checks, a ban on AI-driven personalized pricing and wage setting, keeping humans in control of nuclear launches, and stopping AI-based prior authorization in Medicare. He has not called for licensing or a pause on advanced AI.

evidence.title: Wisconsin Watch / NOTUS: Foxconn is moving to AI. It's giving lawmakers some pause.
evidence.quote: All the more reason Congress should get its act together because we need to do the proper regulation that's good on all fronts related to AI, and I feel like we're not even crawling at this point
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants broad federal AI regulation and faults the Republican-led Congress for not moving.

evidence.title: Press release: Pocan, Schakowsky introduce resolution condemning prior authorization use in Medicare (WISeR model using AI)
evidence.quote: Not only that, but the use of AI in determining whether or not treatment is necessary is extremely reckless.
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposes letting AI decide whether Medicare patients get care, a specific guardrail on high-stakes AI use.

evidence.title: House Select Committee on the CCP report 'DeepSeek Unmasked' and letter to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
evidence.what_it_shows: Bipartisan committee report found DeepSeek funnels US data to China, censors output, and was built on tens of thousands of Nvidia chips possibly obtained around export controls; leaders sent Nvidia a letter demanding sales data for China and Southeast Asia.

evidence.title: Moolenaar letter to Lutnick objecting to resumption of Nvidia H20 sales to China
evidence.what_it_shows: The Select Committee chairman said Commerce 'must hold the line' on the H20 ban, cited use of H20s by DeepSeek and Tencent, requested a briefing, and proposed a floating technical benchmark pegged just above China's domestic chip capability.

evidence.title: Moolenaar statement: DOJ chip-smuggling indictment shows urgent need for the Chip Security Act
evidence.what_it_shows: After DOJ indicted three Chinese nationals for routing chips through Thailand and Malaysia to China, Moolenaar called for passing the Chip Security Act's location-verification mandate, noting 30 bipartisan cosponsors.

evidence.title: Moolenaar letter to Lutnick on Nvidia H200 chips: US is winning the AI race against a weak Chinese chip sector
evidence.what_it_shows: Moolenaar argued China lags far behind in aggregate compute, that Huawei's flagship chip was made abroad via a TSMC shell company, and that approving cutting-edge chip sales to Chinese companies risks undercutting the US lead; requested a Commerce briefing.

evidence.title: Moolenaar and Mast bipartisan letter to Rubio and Lutnick supporting stronger allied export controls on chipmaking tools
evidence.what_it_shows: Eight House members from both parties urged countrywide (not entity-specific) controls on chokepoint semiconductor manufacturing equipment and closer work with the Netherlands and other allies, citing doubling Dutch lithography sales to China.

evidence.title: House Select Committee report 'Buy What It Can, Steal What It Must: China's Campaign to Acquire Frontier AI Capabilities'
evidence.what_it_shows: Committee investigation found China remains the largest buyer of chipmaking equipment, lawfully buys large volumes of AI chips, runs sophisticated smuggling networks, and distills US frontier models at industrial scale; it recommends passing the MATCH Act (H.R.8170) and AI OVERWATCH Act (H.R.6875).

evidence.title: Moolenaar statement backing House Foreign Affairs passage of export-control bills (MATCH Act, Stop Stealing Our Chips Act, Deterring American AI Model Theft Act)
evidence.what_it_shows: Moolenaar praised the committee's bipartisan approval of bills restricting chipmaking-equipment sales, rewarding chip-smuggling whistleblowers, and sanctioning AI model theft.

evidence.title: Moolenaar and Garbarino letters to Airbnb and Anysphere launching investigation into use of Chinese AI models
evidence.what_it_shows: The chairs of the China Select Committee and Homeland Security opened a joint probe into US companies' use of PRC-developed models (DeepSeek, Alibaba, Moonshot, MiniMax), citing distillation of US frontier models and cybersecurity risk.

evidence.title: Moolenaar and Whitesides letter to Lutnick urging Commerce not to allow US purchases of Chinese memory chips
evidence.what_it_shows: A bipartisan pair urged Commerce to hold firm against letting Apple and other US firms buy DRAM from Chinese, military-linked memory makers despite the AI-driven memory shortage, and to expand export controls on Chinese memory producers.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Babin wants data centers built faster. As Science Committee chairman he held a hearing on permitting delays as the main barrier to AI infrastructure, and in September 2026 he opened a probe into whether foreign money is behind local opposition to data centers. His committee also blocked a Democratic amendment on data centers' community impacts.

evidence.title: Opening statement: Powering America's AI Future, Federal Permitting Challenges for Data Center Infrastructure
evidence.quote: Permitting delays for power generation and transmission, environmental review bottlenecks, and regulatory uncertainty slow the construction and expansion of critical infrastructure.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames data centers as the physical backbone of winning the AI race with China and permitting reform as the fix.

evidence.title: E&E News: House Science Committee takes on data center permitting
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence will define the next era of economic and national security leadership, but it cannot advance without reliable, abundant energy
evidence.what_it_shows: His announcement of the hearing ties AI leadership to abundant power for data centers.

evidence.title: Press release: Babin, McCormick probe foreign influence in U.S. AI and energy policy
evidence.quote: Advancing AI capabilities and ensuring energy resilience are essential to U.S. national security and economic competitiveness
evidence.what_it_shows: He sent letters to NSF, Sierra Club, 350.org, Indivisible and Oil Change International seeking documents on foreign funding of organized opposition to data centers.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Federal AI security center measure advanced by House Science (data center amendment dispute)
evidence.quote: it should never be assumed that by offering an amendment this idea will automatically be considered or adopted
evidence.what_it_shows: Ranking Member Lofgren said the majority threatened to pull a bill if she offered an amendment on data centers' energy and water impacts; Babin defended the process.

evidence.title: Op-ed, Washington Times: America must win the artificial intelligence race with China
evidence.quote: Unleash innovation, remove unnecessary barriers, and ensure the United States, not China, defines the future of artificial intelligence.
evidence.what_it_shows: He calls for removing barriers to AI infrastructure and innovation.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Babin is an innovation-first, beat-China chairman. He praised Trump's deregulatory AI Action Plan and prefers voluntary standards and partnership with industry over mandates, though his committee did advance a bipartisan package that writes the federal AI security center (CAISI) into law and creates a voluntary AI flaw database.

evidence.title: Press release: Chairman Babin praises administration's strategy for American AI leadership
evidence.quote: By fostering innovation through streamlining regulations, strengthening AI infrastructure, and promoting the adoption of gold-standard American-built AI systems, this plan positions the United States ahead of global competitors.
evidence.what_it_shows: He endorsed the Trump AI Action Plan's deregulatory approach and pledged committee legislation to match it.

evidence.title: Opening statement at FY2027 OSTP budget hearing with Director Kratsios

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Rounds says the U.S. must build far more power to win the AI race with China, but that data centers today should go only where local residents actively welcome them; long term he expects most new data centers to be in space. His independent challenger attacks him over AI and data center donations.

evidence.title: KOTA TV: Rapid City data center backlash: EPA rules, Meta cash and space tech
evidence.quote: Long-term, I believe that the vast majority of new data centers will probably be based in space.
evidence.what_it_shows: He said data centers must go only where they are actively welcomed by local populations today, while framing AI buildout as a national security race with China.

evidence.title: Ripon Society: Rounds Details Urgent AI Competition with China
evidence.quote: We’re not producing enough new power. China has really close to over 3000 gigawatts of power, and they’re producing over 300 gigawatts more per year.
evidence.what_it_shows: He argues the U.S. needs much more electricity, including nuclear, to power AI systems, a pro-buildout stance.

evidence.title: FedScoop: GOP senator: Legal immigration is 'critical' to US success in AI race
evidence.what_it_shows: He said China has roughly four times U.S. power production, a metric he called crucial for AI data centers, and called for more manufacturing and legal immigration to catch up.

evidence.title: SDPB: Sen. Rounds, Bengs battling over AI, campaign finance as election nears
evidence.quote: He has taken over $215,000 American dollars from AI data center interests, and is backed with hundreds of thousands more from super PACs that support big tech interests
evidence.what_it_shows: Independent opponent Brian Bengs attacked Rounds over AI and data center money; a Rounds adviser replied that Bengs would take away local control.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Rounds is a pro-innovation institution builder. He co-chairs the Senate AI Caucus, co-wrote the 2024 Senate AI roadmap, sponsors a bill letting financial firms test AI in regulatory sandboxes with fewer rules, and says the U.S. cannot lose the AI race with China. He favors research funding, education and commissions over binding safety mandates.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.2528 Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Creates innovation labs at financial regulators so firms can test AI without unduly burdensome regulation or expectation of enforcement actions.

evidence.title: Press release: Rounds Reintroduces Legislation Supporting AI Innovation in Financial Services
evidence.quote: By creating these innovation labs, we aim to strike a balance between encouraging innovation and maintaining consumer protection
evidence.what_it_shows: He tied the sandbox bill to the Trump administration's AI Action Plan and framed it as fostering innovation and economic growth.

evidence.title: Ripon Society: Rounds Details Urgent AI Competition with China
evidence.quote: We cannot lose this race. So, my message to you today with regard to artificial intelligence: it’s here, it is not going away.
evidence.what_it_shows: His frame is winning the AI race with China and investing, not slowing development.

evidence.title: Press release: Senate AI Working Group reveals bipartisan roadmap for AI policy
evidence.what_it_shows: With Schumer, Heinrich and Young he released a roadmap after nine AI Insight Forums that urged harnessing AI's benefits while mitigating long-term risks and left any rules to committees.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4178 Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2024 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a government AI Safety Institute writing voluntary testing standards rather than mandates.

evidence.title: FedScoop: Warner, Rounds float federal commission to guide AI policymaking
evidence.quote: American dominance in AI is a matter of both economic and national security
evidence.what_it_shows: His Economy of the Future Commission Act with Sen. Warner would study AI's effect on jobs and recommend policy, a study-first approach.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: S.4441 CREATE AI Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a national shared computing resource for AI researchers, part of his research-and-talent agenda.

tech_regulation.label: No public position found
tech_regulation.summary: No clear public position found as of Sept 2026. Searches for Rounds on Section 230, the Kids Online Safety Act, antitrust, privacy and Big Tech found only older media appearance listings on Big Tech censorship and no bills in the record, so no score.

preemption.label: One national rule
preemption.summary: In June 2025 Rounds said he supported putting the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws in place so Congress could write federal rules, and suggested tying it to broadband funds to survive Senate rules. He then voted with 98 colleagues to strip it after the deal collapsed. No later statements found.

evidence.title: The Hill: AI moratorium sparks GOP battle over states' rights
evidence.quote: I support getting the moratorium in place so that Congress has the opportunity.
evidence.what_it_shows: As Senate AI Caucus co-chair he backed the state-law moratorium and said Congress then had the hard work of writing appropriate legislation.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium from H.R. 1 (Yea, 99-1)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted Yea like nearly every senator after the compromise fell apart; the vote alone does not show opposition to preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish

No statement found on the Nvidia H20 or H200 sales themselves.

evidence.title: Sponsor: S.1473 Stop Stealing our Chips Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Pays and protects whistleblowers who report illegal exports of restricted AI chips, modeled on the SEC program.

evidence.title: Press release: Rounds Legislation to Prevent Smuggling of American Semiconductors into China Unanimously Passes Senate
evidence.what_it_shows: He said China keeps smuggling American chips, called it a grave national security concern as AI accelerates, and urged the House to send the bill to the president.

evidence.title: Lawfare: A Whistleblower Incentive Program to Enforce U.S. Export Controls
evidence.quote: In April, Sens. Mike Rounds (R-S.D.) and Mark Warner (D-Va.) introduced legislation to establish a Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) whistleblower incentive program modeled on the SEC program.
evidence.what_it_shows: Independent analysis confirms the bill strengthens export control enforcement against AI chip diversion to China.

evidence.title: Ripon Society: Rounds Details Urgent AI Competition with China
evidence.quote: We see China as an adversary today. We’d like to see them as a competitor in the future, not an adversary, but it takes two people to agree on that, not just one.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats China as the adversary in an AI and quantum arms race, consistent with tighter controls on chip leakage.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Kennedy is critical of how the AI industry has built data centers. On Meet the Press in September 2026 he rejected Trump's line that opponents want to be 'backwards and poor' and said the industry must cut water use, supply its own power, stop demanding tax subsidies, and be honest with the public before it deserves support. He does not call for a pause, but he wants communities and ratepayers protected first.

evidence.title: Meet the Press transcript (via RealClearPolitics/Yahoo): Kennedy lists five things data centers must do to win support
evidence.quote: First, they're going to have to stop using so much water. Go to a closed-loop system. Number two, they're going to have to provide their own energy.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants data centers to bear their own water and power burdens instead of shifting them to communities and the grid.

evidence.title: Meet the Press transcript: Kennedy on tax subsidies for data centers
evidence.quote: Number four, they're going to have to stop going into these states and demanding all these tax subsidies and, and, and demanding all the tax breaks. They're all rich.
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposes state tax breaks for data center developers and, asked if he agreed with Trump's 'backwards and poor' remark, answered 'No.'

evidence.title: Politico (via Yahoo): Kennedy rails against AI developers as 'high IQ stupid people'
evidence.quote: American people look at it; they're not stupid. They get it. They think, well, AI could make our lives better if it doesn't take our jobs and kill us all first
evidence.what_it_shows: He blames the industry, not voters, for the data center backlash and says it has 'work to do to rebuild momentum among voters.'

evidence.title: Washington Examiner: Kennedy knocks AI executives' messaging failures
evidence.what_it_shows: Confirms the Meet the Press remarks and frames them as blaming AI executives for the growing backlash against the industry.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Kennedy supports specific guardrails: he cosponsored the AI Labeling Act to require disclosure of AI-made content, the FAIRR Act on AI risks in finance, and a bill to let travelers refuse facial scans at airports. At the 2023 Altman hearing he demanded witnesses name concrete rules Congress should pass. He has not called for licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: Transcript: Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing on oversight of AI (Altman, Marcus, Montgomery)
evidence.quote: Please tell me in plain English, two or three reforms, regulations, if any, that you would, you would implement if you were queen or king for a day.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed witnesses for specific AI rules and said 'this is your chance, folks to tell us how to get this right,' showing openness to regulation while warning Congress does not understand AI.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of S.2691, the AI Labeling Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: He co-led with Sen. Schatz a bill requiring AI-made images, video, audio and text to carry clear labels and chatbots to disclose they are AI.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of S.5358, the FAIRR Act (2026)
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants financial regulators to identify and reduce risks from AI used by banks and Wall Street; he also cosponsored the 2023 version.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of S.1691, the Traveler Privacy Protection Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs limits on TSA facial recognition, requiring consent and an opt-out.

evidence.title: Music Business Worldwide: Senators revive AI Labeling Act first introduced by Schatz and Kennedy
evidence.what_it_shows: Reports the AI Labeling Act 'was first introduced in 2023 by Schatz and Republican Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana'; Kennedy is not listed on the 2026 reintroduction.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Kennedy has a long record of targeted Big Tech bills: the Kids Online Safety Act, STOP CSAM, the EARN IT Act stripping Section 230 protection for child abuse material, and a bill making Google and Facebook pay news outlets. He grilled judicial nominees on Section 230 in 2026. His bills chip at platform immunity rather than repeal it outright.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of S.1748, the Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports a duty of care for social media toward minors.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of S.1829, the STOP CSAM Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs letting victims sue platforms that fail to remove child sexual abuse material.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of S.1207, the EARN IT Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported removing platforms' Section 230 shield when they let child abuse material spread.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of S.1094, the Journalism Competition and Preservation Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed letting news outlets bargain collectively against Google and Facebook.

evidence.title: Economic Times video: Kennedy questions judicial nominees on Section 230
evidence.what_it_shows: Reporter says he pressed nominees on Section 230 and 'Big Tech's role in moderating online speech,' a recurring theme for him.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No public position found. Kennedy voted with 98 colleagues to strip the state AI-law moratorium from the 2025 tax bill, but that vote followed the collapse of the Cruz-Blackburn deal and is not a statement of view. We found no remarks from him on the moratorium, the December 2025 executive order, or the March 2026 framework.

evidence.title: Roll call 363: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the state AI-law moratorium from H.R. 1
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined the 99-1 vote; because nearly every senator voted Yea, this is not evidence of opposing preemption. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: Tighten export controls
china_chips.summary: Kennedy is a hard-liner on chip exports to China. He demanded in 2024 that Commerce stop the smuggling of Nvidia chips into China, skipped Jensen Huang's December 2025 pitch to Republicans and called him not a credible source on selling chips to China, cosponsored the Chip Security Act, and wrote a bill to raise export control fines.

evidence.title: AP: Kennedy skips Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's meeting with Republican senators
evidence.quote: I don’t consider him to be an objective, credible source about whether we should be selling chips to China
evidence.what_it_shows: He publicly rejected Nvidia's lobbying for looser China chip sales.

evidence.title: Press release: Kennedy urges Commerce to stop the flow of advanced AI chips to China
evidence.quote: despite the Commerce Department’s efforts to keep advanced microchips out of Chinese hands, it appears that the steady flow of advanced microchips into China continues. That flow must stop
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants export controls on Nvidia-class chips enforced hard against smuggling networks.

evidence.title: Cosponsor of S.1705, the Chip Security Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs location verification on exported AI chips so they cannot be diverted to China.

evidence.title: Sponsor of S.4883, a bill to increase civil penalties under the Export Control Reform Act
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill raises fines on companies that break export control rules on sensitive technology.

members.signature: Blunt critic of the AI industry's data center pitch ('high IQ stupid people'), a China chip hawk who refused to meet Nvidia's CEO, and a backer of AI labeling, facial recognition limits, and kids' online safety bills.

quote.text: The people who have developed AI are very, very smart. But they're high IQ stupid people. You might let them tutor you. But you wouldn't want them to date your sister. They're terrible marketers.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Blunt Rochester has not taken a public position on the proposed Delaware City data center or Delaware's 2026 data center laws that we could find. Her only relevant words are from July 2025, when she said the federal government must be forceful in scaling AI infrastructure but that any AI framework must prioritize the environment and energy efficiency. A July 2026 6abc interview listed data center builds as a topic but no transcript was available.

evidence.title: Press release: Blunt Rochester statement on Trump administration's executive actions on AI
evidence.quote: any responsible AI policy framework must prioritize the environment, and should focus on resource protection and energy efficiency technologies
evidence.what_it_shows: In the same statement she said government must be forceful in scaling AI infrastructure to compete, so she supports the buildout with environmental and efficiency conditions.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: She backs specific AI rules: a new federal crime for AI impersonation fraud, demands on platforms over sexualized deepfakes, the Kids Online Safety Act, and studies of AI's effect on jobs. In August 2026 she went further, telling OpenAI and Anthropic that frontier models autonomously attacking third parties shows an urgent need for federal oversight, testing standards and disclosure. She pairs this with strong pro-innovation, win-the-AI-race language.

evidence.title: Fox News: Blunt Rochester letters to OpenAI CEO Altman and Anthropic CEO Amodei on AI agents hacking third parties
evidence.quote: These incidents mark the first publicly confirmed instances of a frontier AI model autonomously launching unauthorized attacks on real people and companies, underscoring the urgent need for federal oversight of frontier AI systems
evidence.what_it_shows: She demanded timelines, model instructions, security logs and transcripts, and called for federal testing standards, containment rules and disclosure requirements for powerful AI systems.

evidence.title: Fox News: Blunt Rochester letter to Anthropic on repeated model attacks during evaluations
evidence.quote: Anthropic models' repeated attacks on third parties with no knowledge of, or role in, Anthropic and AISI's evaluations demonstrate an alarming pattern of malicious behavior
evidence.what_it_shows: Treats autonomous model misbehavior as a serious safety problem requiring government answers, not just voluntary company review.

evidence.title: Press release: Blunt Rochester and Sheehy introduce AI Fraud Accountability Act
evidence.quote: With more Americans using AI every day, we need to do all we can to cut down on AI-related fraud
evidence.what_it_shows: Co-led a bipartisan bill making realistic AI impersonation to defraud people a federal offense enforced by the FTC.

evidence.title: S.3982 AI Fraud Accountability Act of 2026 (co-lead with Sheehy)
evidence.what_it_shows: Adds criminal and civil penalties for using AI to trick or scam people.

evidence.title: Press release: Blunt Rochester questions OpenAI CEO Sam Altman at Commerce hearing on winning the AI race
evidence.quote: making sure that we are watching out for ethics, watching out for scams, watching out that technology does not take over the human [race]
evidence.what_it_shows: She voiced excitement about AI's opportunities while naming ethics, scams and loss of human control as concerns, and pressed Altman on OpenAI's shift to a for-profit structure.

evidence.title: FedScoop: Blunt Rochester, Hirono and Schiff introduce the Workforce of the Future Act
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence is increasingly disrupting our economy, contributing to layoffs and occupational changes
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants federal agencies to study AI's job impact and fund worker training, a targeted response to AI displacement.

evidence.title: FedScoop: Blunt Rochester presses Fed Chair Warsh on who sits on the Fed's AI task force
evidence.quote: I hope that there will be the inclusion of other voices beyond economic experts and tech individuals, but actually families, businesses, people that are actually both consuming and impacted by AI.
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked the Fed to give Main Street equal footing with Wall Street and tech leaders when weighing AI and jobs.

evidence.title: Press release: Blunt Rochester and Curtis launch Consumer Safety Technology Act
evidence.quote: Our government must be able to keep up with new and emerging technologies, especially when it comes to consumer safety
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows her pro-adoption side: she wants agencies like the Consumer Product Safety Commission to use AI to protect consumers.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: She goes after platforms on specific harms rather than structure: she led eight senators demanding that X, Meta, Alphabet, Snap, Reddit and TikTok explain and remove sexualized AI deepfakes, cosponsors the Kids Online Safety Act, and backs a bill to stop fentanyl sales on social media. No calls found for breaking up Big Tech or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: Press release: Blunt Rochester leads 8 senators in letter to tech companies demanding removal of sexualized AI-generated images
evidence.quote: users are finding ways around these guardrails. Or these guardrails are failing. Even where outputs do not depict explicit nudity, they can still be non-consensual, sexualizing, and harmful. The public deserves transparency.
evidence.what_it_shows: Demanded that six platforms hand over policies, preserve documents, and explain how they remove AI undressing deepfakes and notify victims.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care and safety tools for minors on social media, games and video sites.

evidence.title: S.3618 No Fentanyl on Social Media Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Pushes platforms to stop drug sales on their apps, a targeted platform rule.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Blunt Rochester has repeatedly defended states' power to regulate AI. As a Commerce Committee Democrat she signed the June 2025 letter calling the 10-year moratorium an attack on states' rights, said in July 2025 that partisanship should not shroud the ability of states and Congress to regulate AI, and cosponsored the GUARDRAILS Act to block the December 2025 executive order.

evidence.title: Cantwell and Commerce Committee Democrats letter to Chairman Cruz on the reconciliation Commerce title (Blunt Rochester signed)
evidence.quote: the AI moratorium proposal tramples states' rights and holds the $42 billion BEAD program hostage, further delaying the broadband Americans desperately need
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposed the state AI law moratorium before the Senate vote, on states' rights grounds.

evidence.title: Press release: Blunt Rochester statement on Trump administration's executive actions on AI
evidence.quote: I do not believe that we should allow culture wars and deep partisanship to shroud the ability of states and Congress to regulate this rapidly evolving industry.
evidence.what_it_shows: In her own words, states should keep the ability to regulate AI alongside Congress.

evidence.title: S.4216 GUARDRAILS Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would stop the December 2025 executive order from withholding federal funds from states that pass AI safeguards; confirmed on the Schatz press release listing cosponsors.

evidence.title: Senate roll call #363: Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from H.R. 1 (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted to remove the moratorium; consistent with her letters, though the 99 to 1 vote is weak evidence by itself. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: No public position found
china_chips.summary: No public position found on AI chip export controls. We searched for statements on Nvidia, H20 or H200 sales, export controls and the Chip Security, GAIN AI and SAFE Chips Acts, and found none; she is not a cosponsor of those bills. Her March 2026 bill banning China-sourced LiDAR at the Transportation Department is about Chinese tech imports, not chip exports, and at the May 2025 Altman hearing she asked about semiconductor manufacturing policy without stating a position.
