data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Johnson frames data centers as essential to beating China in AI, opposes a federal moratorium, and wants faster permitting and more gas, nuclear and coal power to run them. Under pressure from vulnerable Republicans, his office scheduled a September 2026 House vote on a bipartisan bill to keep data center power costs off household bills.

evidence.title: Michigan Advance (via Livingston Post): Johnson rejects a data center moratorium while campaigning in Lansing
evidence.quote: We're in a race with China on that AI race, and if they're able to leapfrog us in that race, it's a very dangerous thing for everybody around the country,
evidence.what_it_shows: He called a broad moratorium on data centers 'kind of a dangerous prospect right now' while saying companies should work with local officials and take community concerns into account.

evidence.title: KTIV interview in Sioux City: Johnson on data centers and AI
evidence.quote: Data centers are directly related to that. We have to fuel AI because we have to keep our edge.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pushed back on community opposition to data centers and said China is spreading misinformation to turn communities against them.

evidence.title: Speech: Speaker Johnson at the Hill and Valley Forum, 'America Will Win the AI Race'
evidence.quote: We all know the amount of energy required to power all these data centers and meet our national demands is truly enormous.
evidence.what_it_shows: He called for more natural gas, oil, nuclear and coal, streamlined permitting, and asked tech companies to build data centers and chips on American soil.

evidence.title: Benzinga (via TradingView): Speaker's office confirms House vote on the Ratepayer Protection Act
evidence.quote: The bill will be on the floor of the House next week,
evidence.what_it_shows: His spokesperson Taylor Haulsee confirmed a floor vote on a bipartisan bill asking state regulators to make data centers cover costs of new power they need, a modest ratepayer step after months of pressure.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Johnson's stated approach is to 'simplify and streamline where we can, regulate only where we must' so America wins the AI race with China. He created a bipartisan House AI task force in 2024 to weigh guardrails and says a national framework should protect kids, but as of Sept 2026 he had not answered House Democrats' call to cancel recess and pass safeguards against catastrophic AI risks.

evidence.title: Speech: Speaker Johnson at the Hill and Valley Forum, 'America Will Win the AI Race'
evidence.quote: this is our commitment in a simple summary: simplify and streamline where we can, regulate only where we must, and pave the way for American dominance.
evidence.what_it_shows: His governing philosophy for AI is light-touch: speed, streamlining, and minimal new rules, with government urged to resist 'the siren song of control'.

evidence.title: Press release: House launches Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence
evidence.quote: to explore how Congress can ensure America continues to lead the world in AI innovation while considering guardrails that may be appropriate to safeguard the nation against current and emerging threats.
evidence.what_it_shows: With Leader Jeffries he created a 24-member task force whose December 2024 report weighed both innovation and guardrails.

evidence.title: Nola.com: Louisiana waits to see how Trump, Congress will regulate AI (Johnson's office on the Kill Switch bill)
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked whether he would back a bipartisan bill letting DHS order shutdown of dangerous AI systems, his spokesperson did not answer and pointed to his 'regulate only where we must' remarks.

evidence.title: CNN: House Democrats urge Speaker Johnson to cancel recess to pass AI safeguards, citing 'catastrophic' risk
evidence.what_it_shows: Reps. Liccardo, Whitesides, Trahan and Lieu asked him to keep the House in session for AI safeguards against cyber and bioweapon risks; no response from him was reported.

tech_regulation.label: Mixed
tech_regulation.summary: Mixed. In Dec 2024 Johnson stalled the Senate-passed Kids Online Safety Act over free speech and censorship worries, then in June 2026 the House passed a narrower KIDS Act that he praised as holding Big Tech accountable. He also backed a bill barring officials from pressuring platforms to remove posts.

evidence.title: Fox News: Speaker Johnson says 'still some concern' about the Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.quote: There's still some concern about the free speech components of that, and whether it might lead to further censorship by the government of valid, you know, conservative voices, for example.
evidence.what_it_shows: He declined to bring the Senate's 91-3 KOSA to a House vote in 2024, citing censorship fears and FTC power.

evidence.title: Roll Call: House online safety bills take narrower approach than Senate
evidence.quote: I've talked to the leaders, the authors of the previous bill, about concerns that were expressed and that they work to address that. So I hope and assume that they have.
evidence.what_it_shows: He signaled openness to a House kids' safety package once his earlier objections to KOSA were addressed.

evidence.title: Press release: House passes KIDS Act to protect children, teens online
evidence.quote: This legislation represents an important step forward in Congress' effort to protect children online and hold big tech accountable, while also empowering parents and protecting free speech,
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed the narrower House kids' online safety bill (H.R. 7757) and framed it as accountability for Big Tech balanced with free speech.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Free Speech Protection Act (H.R. 4791)
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported barring government officials from pressuring platforms to take down posts, an anti-censorship rather than anti-Big-Tech measure.

preemption.label: One national rule
preemption.summary: Johnson wants one national AI framework that 'avoids a patchwork of state regulations' and, with other House GOP leaders, pledged to enact the White House framework that calls for preempting state AI laws. Eighty-one House Democrats wrote to him in Nov 2025 opposing any revival of the state-law moratorium in the defense bill.

evidence.title: Joint statement: Johnson, Scalise, Guthrie, Jordan, Babin pledge to implement the national AI framework
evidence.quote: Today, the Trump Administration took a critical step in releasing a framework that gives Congress a roadmap to pursue legislation that provides innovators with much-needed certainty, while protecting consumers and prioritizing kids' online safety.
evidence.what_it_shows: House GOP leadership endorsed the White House framework, which calls for blocking state AI laws that impose 'undue burdens' in favor of a single national standard.

evidence.title: Speech: Speaker Johnson at the Hill and Valley Forum
evidence.quote: The first thing is we have to deliver a single national framework that protects children, safeguards communities, supports creators, and avoids a patchwork of state regulations.
evidence.what_it_shows: He listed replacing state-by-state AI rules with one federal framework as Congress's first AI job.

evidence.title: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats to Speaker Johnson and other leaders opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and by executive order
evidence.quote: Congress should not freeze state and local AI safeguards, least of all when there are no meaningful federal protections in place.
evidence.what_it_shows: He was the lead recipient of the Democratic letter fighting the push to put a state AI law moratorium into the defense bill; the moratorium was left out of the final NDAA.

evidence.title: Johnson, Scalise, Guthrie, Jordan, Babin joint statement pledging to implement the White House National AI Framework
evidence.what_it_shows: House Republican leaders and three committee chairs said the Trump framework, which calls for preempting state AI laws, 'gives Congress a roadmap' and that House Republicans 'look forward to working across the aisle to enact a national framework.'

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Johnson calls China an adversary that steals intellectual property and says the American AI stack should reach allies while staying out of adversaries' hands, but he has taken no public stand found on Nvidia H20 or H200 sales or on specific export control bills. He voted against the 2022 CHIPS Act and briefly floated repealing it in 2024.

evidence.title: CNBC Squawk Box: Johnson says China is straining U.S. relations with Nvidia chip ban

evidence.what_it_shows: He called China an 'adversary' after Beijing told firms to stop buying Nvidia chips, hawkish rhetoric without a stated position on US export limits.

evidence.title: Speech: Speaker Johnson at the Hill and Valley Forum
evidence.quote: And we know it's possible to expand the American AI stack to friends and allies, while also ensuring it stays out of the hands of America's adversaries and rivals.
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs exporting American AI to allies while keeping it from China, the administration's framing that supports both sales abroad and controls on adversaries.

evidence.title: Bloomberg via SCMP: Johnson floats, then walks back, repeal of the CHIPS and Science Act
evidence.quote: I expect that we probably will, but we haven't developed that part of the agenda yet.
evidence.what_it_shows: He had voted against the chip-factory subsidy law and suggested repeal before saying it was 'not on the agenda for repeal'.

members.signature: Speaker who pledged to 'regulate only where we must' on AI, wants one national framework over state laws, and calls a data center moratorium 'a dangerous prospect'.

quote.text: America will win the AI race. We will win it if two things happen, if government resists the siren song of control and if industry steps up as our patriotic partner.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails

evidence.what_it_shows: A long record of asking antitrust enforcers to check Google, Apple and Amazon's reach.

preemption.label: Let states regulate

At a September 2025 hearing he said opposition to an AI moratorium is broad and bipartisan and that a moratorium would wipe out state laws without putting a national law in their place. In June 2026 he said preemption backers had caved to billionaires who own the AI models, and that states should be allowed to experiment.

evidence.title: Judiciary Democrats: At hearing on federal preemption of state AI laws, subcommittee Democrats underscore need for guardrails

evidence.what_it_shows: After the White House framework, he attacked broad preemption of state law and tort claims with no federal regulation in return.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: In his 2026 governor and Senate campaigns Norman said he opposes any subsidies for data centers, wants them to pay their own way, and says water, the power grid and ratepayers come first with local communities getting the final say. He attacked Darline Graham for backing data centers more unconditionally. He did vote for the SPEED Act permitting bill.

evidence.title: WYFF: Norman on data centers after the Aug 17, 2026 Senate runoff forum
evidence.quote: I am not for any subsidies for data centers, let them pay their own way if they are a fit, but I feel bad for the homes being around data centers when they had no idea it was being built
evidence.what_it_shows: His own words: no subsidies, pay your own way, sympathy for neighbors, protect water and electricity.

evidence.title: FOX Carolina candidate profile quoting Norman at the Apr 21, 2026 SCGOP gubernatorial debate
evidence.quote: We must always protect our water for our farmers... we should always protect ratepayers. But the final say should come to the people. People in local communities should have the final say of who they want their neighbors to be.
evidence.what_it_shows: Puts ratepayers, water and local consent ahead of economic development incentives for data centers.

evidence.title: NBC News: Aug 18, 2026 Senate runoff debate exchange on data centers
evidence.quote: Norman charged that Graham had previously supported data centers more unconditionally.
evidence.what_it_shows: Reporter's account: he used data centers as an attack line against his opponent for being too pro-development.

evidence.title: Roll call 356: voted Yea on H.R. 4776, the SPEED Act (permitting reform)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported a permitting reform bill that speeds energy and infrastructure projects, a pro-build vote that sits alongside his protective statements. Recorded vote: Yea.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: At the Aug 2026 Senate runoff debate Norman said he supports regulating AI where possible to keep it from hurting children and Americans, while admitting broad rules would be hard to write, like regulating the internet. No bills or detailed proposals found.

evidence.title: South Carolina Public Radio: Graham and Norman Senate runoff debate coverage
evidence.quote: You try to regulate what you can and find out what you can so that it's used in a good way instead of hurting American children and Americans in general
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports some AI rules focused on protecting people, especially children, but is skeptical that sweeping regulation is workable.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules

evidence.quote: This clean, abundant resource has the potential to help meet the United States’ power demand, which is increasing at a historic rate due in part to AI and other technological advancements.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats AI-driven demand as a reason to cut federal red tape and build more generation, with lower consumer prices as the stated goal.

evidence.title: Op-ed: Geothermal, the energy powerhouse Idaho already understands
evidence.quote: Ensuring America is ready to meet these growing needs through various power sources, such as geothermal, is essential to keeping prices low for consumers and strengthening our energy independence.
evidence.what_it_shows: He links rising electricity demand driven in part by AI to the need for new supply and permitting reform, while naming consumer prices as the concern.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Mixed. He cheers AI as a field where America must lead and praised the 2025 House package that promoted AI, but he presses hard on specific harms: kids forming attachments to chatbots, AI-faked sexual images, AI-enabled bioweapons and terrorism. No support found for broad AI licensing or safety mandates.

evidence.title: E&C Oversight hearing on AI chatbots: Fulcher questions on kids and chatbots
evidence.quote: Kids are wired to form attachments with things that act friendly. What we don’t want happening is a chatbot taking the role of teaching a child right and wrong.
evidence.what_it_shows: He worries children will treat chatbots as parental authorities and, per the hearing transcript, that customizable chatbots can validate abusers and pull struggling users away from human relationships.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.633 TAKE IT DOWN Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports criminalizing AI-faked sexual images and forcing fast takedowns, a targeted AI harm rule now law.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R.6499 Assessing Safety Tools for Parents and Minors Act
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill orders a study of parental control tools; it was part of the 18-bill kids' online safety package the E&C subcommittee advanced in December 2025.

evidence.title: E&C Oversight hearing on AI and biotechnology: Fulcher on stopping AI-enabled bio threats
evidence.quote: can you say what specific parts of that order are actually going to stop these threats, or have the best chance of stopping these threats?
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked whether the May 2025 executive order's gene synthesis screening provisions would stop AI-enabled biological threats and what more Congress should do.

evidence.title: Fulcher video: 'Are we at that point?' Fulcher questions if terrorists can use AI to carry out attacks
evidence.what_it_shows: Video-only post of his hearing questions on whether terrorists can already use AI to carry out attacks; shows attention to catastrophic misuse, direction on rules unclear.

evidence.title: Press release: Fulcher on Energy and Commerce passage of reconciliation text
evidence.quote: This legislation takes important steps to strengthen America’s leadership on the world stage by supporting rapid technological advancements in Artificial Intelligence
evidence.what_it_shows: He framed AI as a race for American leadership and praised the committee text that promoted AI adoption, a pro-innovation counterweight to his harm-focused questioning.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.6734 Auto Data Privacy and Autonomy Act

preemption.summary: Leans toward one national approach: his office touted the 2025 Energy and Commerce budget text for guarding against a patchwork of state AI laws, and he voted for the House bill that carried the 10-year state-law moratorium. ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Trahan wants binding federal rules on the most powerful AI models now: mandatory incident reporting, independent audits and a government pause button for models posing catastrophic risk. After the Sept 2026 Anthropic researcher warnings she said Congress must listen and act, while insisting her framework does not smother innovation.

evidence.title: WBUR interview: Trahan calls for legal guardrails after whistleblower warns AI could kill us all
evidence.quote: I think that when the people building this technology are the ones sounding the alarm, we must listen. Today, the only thing we have in place is the honor system.
evidence.what_it_shows: She takes catastrophic-risk warnings seriously and describes the FRONTIER Act's mandated transparency, incident reporting, independent verification and a government pause button.

evidence.title: CNBC: AI regulation calls grow after researcher's extinction warning
evidence.quote: It's past time for Congress to get off the sidelines and act
evidence.what_it_shows: She says bipartisan support for AI regulation has reached a tipping point.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Joyce pushes hard to build data centers, framing the buildout as a race with China and asking the FBI to investigate whether foreign adversaries are behind local opposition. At the same time he cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act to keep big users' grid costs off household electric bills. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: The only data-center evidence is a letter he co-signed calling the Sanders moratorium bill 'disastrous', casting local/state pauses as possibly foreign-directed, and asking the FBI to investigate opponents of buildout. T

evidence.title: Letter: Chairmen Guthrie, Joyce and Latta ask PCAST and FBI Director Patel to investigate foreign efforts to block U.S. data center buildout
evidence.quote: The U.S. is in a global race for technological superiority that has significantly raised the stakes for economic and national security if our nation falls behind.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats data-center construction as critical national infrastructure and calls the Sanders data-center moratorium bill disastrous, a strongly pro-buildout stance.

evidence.title: Data Center Dynamics: Trio of Republicans call for FBI investigation into data center opposition
evidence.quote: foreign influence campaigns… have engaged in a coordinated effort to slow US growth in AI development and the building of infrastructure supporting AI data centers
evidence.what_it_shows: Trade press coverage of the same letter shows Joyce casting grassroots data-center opposition as possibly foreign-directed rather than a legitimate local concern.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs a bill to stop regular customers' electric bills from rising to pay for power that large new users like data centers need, a condition on the buildout.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on SPEED Act permitting reform (House roll call 356)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted to speed federal permitting for energy and infrastructure projects, consistent with a build-faster approach to the power needed for AI. Recorded vote: Yea.

ai_risk.label: Mixed
ai_risk.summary: Mixed. As Oversight chairman Joyce held hearings warning that AI chatbots can harm vulnerable users and that AI-designed biology is outrunning existing safeguards, and said current oversight must be re-examined. But he also frames AI as a race with China, promotes AI medical devices, and was endorsed by the industry-funded Leading the Future super PAC.

evidence.title: Opening statement: O&I hearing on the risks and benefits of AI chatbots
evidence.quote: It is important that we consider the implications of these technologies as we balance the benefits of AI innovation with protecting the most vulnerable among us.
evidence.what_it_shows: He convened a hearing on chatbot harms to children and people with mental illness and welcomed the FTC inquiry, a guardrail-minded but balanced posture.

evidence.title: Opening statement: O&I hearing on biosecurity at the intersection of AI and biology
evidence.quote: the federal government must continue to carefully assess whether our current safeguards and reporting systems are adequate in an era of rapidly advancing AI technology.
evidence.what_it_shows: He said AI tools that can help design dangerous pathogens introduce profound new risks and that existing oversight frameworks may not cover them.

evidence.title: Letter: Guthrie, Joyce and Latta request investigation of efforts to slow American AI progress
evidence.quote: The U.S. is in a global race for technological superiority that has significantly raised the stakes for economic and national security if our nation falls behind.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI primarily as a competition with China and treats efforts to slow AI development as a threat, a light-touch signal.

evidence.what_it_shows: He is an enthusiast for deploying AI in medicine and wants Medicare to pay for AI-enabled devices faster.

evidence.quote: part of a broader ecosystem of current members who have engaged with the industry
evidence.what_it_shows: The $100 million-plus AI industry super PAC named Joyce a champion, meaning the industry views him as an ally on a national framework with basic rather than strict rules.

Critics on the left call his privacy bill too friendly to industry, and he has also pressed platforms over alleged censorship of conservatives.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: Steil, whose district includes Microsoft's Mount Pleasant campus, praised Microsoft's January 2026 pledge to cover its own energy, water and infrastructure costs so families are not stuck with the bill, and reportedly said it could set a national standard. He did not respond to Wisconsin Watch's December 2025 request for comment, and the WTMJ story could not be opened, so this rests on thin evidence.

evidence.title: WTMJ: Steil: Don't stick families with AI costs
evidence.what_it_shows: Headline seen in Google News results; the page returned 403 and no archive copy exists. A first-pass summary says he attended Microsoft's Washington announcement of its community-first plan shifting costs onto the company and said it could set a national standard.

evidence.title: Microsoft On the Issues: Building Community-First AI Infrastructure (the plan Steil praised)
evidence.what_it_shows: Microsoft's pledge to pay full electricity costs for data centers, back Wisconsin's very-large-customer rate class, and use closed-loop cooling; it is the plan Steil endorsed rather than any limit on building.

evidence.title: Wisconsin Watch / NOTUS: Foxconn is moving to AI. It's giving lawmakers some pause.
evidence.what_it_shows: A spokesperson for Steil, whose district includes Racine County, did not return a request for comment on Foxconn's AI data center plans and their energy use.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Steil chairs the House Financial Services subcommittee on AI and digital assets and frames AI in finance as an innovation opportunity needing rules of the road. He cosponsored a bill letting banks test AI with some rules turned off, and has not backed AI safety mandates.

evidence.title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act (H.R.4801)
evidence.what_it_shows: He cosponsored a bill creating regulatory sandboxes so financial firms can try AI projects with some normal rules suspended.

evidence.title: Press release: Steil named chairman of the Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence
evidence.quote: Innovation in the financial services sector provides an exciting opportunity for consumers and entrepreneurs, as technologies like financial apps, digital assets, and machine learning revolutionize our economy
evidence.what_it_shows: His framing on taking the AI gavel is pro-innovation, promising rules of the road rather than new restrictions.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Steil supports targeted online safety measures: he introduced a bill to build a federal strategy on social media's harm to children's mental health, led a 2022 letter to ban TikTok from Wisconsin state devices, and voted for the 2024 TikTok divestiture law.

evidence.title: Press release: Steil introduces nonpartisan bill to protect kids' mental health online (Protecting Young Minds Online Act, with Rep. Balint)
evidence.quote: Social media and emerging technologies can have a harmful impact on children, driving depression, anxiety, and in worst cases, self-harm and suicide
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants the federal government to develop a strategy on how social media and new technologies affect kids' mental health.

evidence.title: Press release: Steil, delegation call for Evers to ban TikTok from state government devices
evidence.quote: TikTok presents clear national security risks. To protect Wisconsin's government data and our personal data, we should not be using TikTok on government devices.
evidence.what_it_shows: He led Wisconsin Republicans in urging a state-device TikTok ban on data security grounds.

evidence.title: House roll call 86 (2024): H.R. 7521, Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (TikTok divestiture)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted Yea to force TikTok's sale or ban, a targeted restriction on a foreign-controlled app. Recorded vote: Yea.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: Steil voted for the House budget bill that carried a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws, but that vote was on the whole package and no statement from him on preempting state AI laws was found. Because the only evidence is a vote on a sweeping budget bill, no position is shown.

evidence.title: House roll call 145: passage of H.R. 1 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act) including the 10-year moratorium on state and local AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted Yea on the bill containing the moratorium; a vote on a large reconciliation bill is weak evidence of his view on preemption itself. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: No public position found
china_chips.summary: No public position found on AI chip export controls as of Sept 2026. Searches for Steil with Nvidia, export controls and chips found only his 2022 push for domestic semiconductor manufacturing and faster fab permitting, which is about building chips at home, not restricting sales abroad.

evidence.quote: At the top of the list of what needs to be produced in the United States is semiconductor chips.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants more domestic chip production for supply chain and defense reasons; the column takes no position on export controls to China.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Hawley is the Missouri delegation's loudest critic of data center power costs. He says data centers are fine if they create jobs, but wants a binding law forcing them to pay for their own electricity and water, and he sponsors the GRID Act to keep them off the regular grid.

evidence.title: Press release: Hawley and Blumenthal introduce the GRID Act (S.3852) to stop data centers from raising consumer electricity bills
evidence.quote: American families should not have to shoulder the burden of the rising electricity costs produced by data centers in Missouri and across the country. This is unacceptable
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill would bar consumer rate increases tied to data centers, give households grid priority, and require new data centers to use off-grid power.

evidence.title: St. Louis Public Radio interview: Hawley says ratepayers should not subsidize data centers
evidence.quote: If data centers are going to come into the state, fine. If they're going to create jobs? Hey, wonderful. But if they're going to suck up a bunch of electricity, they need to pay for that.
evidence.what_it_shows: He does not oppose data centers outright but conditions them on paying their own way, putting him at odds with Gov. Kehoe and Rep. Jason Smith.

evidence.title: Letter to Ameren CEO demanding answers on rate hikes, shut-offs and data center deals
evidence.quote: I am concerned Ameren is seeking dramatic rate increases in order to supply massive data centers and industrial users.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed Missouri's largest utility on whether residential customers are cross-subsidizing data center contracts.

evidence.title: Warren-Hawley letter to the Energy Information Administration seeking mandatory data center energy reporting
evidence.quote: Comprehensive information regarding the operations of data centers and other large loads is essential for accurate grid planning and will support policymaking to prevent large companies from increasing electricity costs for American families
evidence.what_it_shows: A left-right push for mandatory disclosure so the public can check whether data centers pay their share.

evidence.title: Missourinet: Hawley wants Trump's ratepayer protection pledge written into law
evidence.quote: I think we ought to say in the law that the data centers have to pay for their own electricity, the data centers have to pay for their own water supply.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats the White House's voluntary pledge as insufficient and wants binding law covering both power and water.

evidence.title: Free Press op-ed: AI Will Control Us If We Do Not Control It (cites the Festus, Mo. data center fight)
evidence.quote: The companies building these facilities can afford to supply their own power, protect residential rates, and safeguard local water. We must hold them to that with binding legal requirements, not hollow promises.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames data centers as a cost shifted onto working families and demands legally binding conditions.

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Hawley wants binding rules now. He sponsors mandatory federal safety testing of the most powerful AI models, product liability for AI harms, a ban on AI companions for minors, and AI layoff reporting, and in Sept. 2026 he opened a Senate probe of OpenAI citing existential risk.

evidence.title: Press release: Hawley and Blumenthal introduce the Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act (S.2938)
evidence.quote: This bipartisan legislation would guarantee common-sense testing and oversight of the most advanced AI systems, so Congress and the American people can be better informed about potential risks
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill would make advanced AI systems go through a mandatory Energy Department evaluation program before release.

evidence.title: Press release and letter: Chairman Hawley launches investigation into OpenAI for the Hugging Face hack and existential risk of AI products
evidence.quote: My investigation will probe this AI hacking incident, along with growing allegations of the existential risk of new AI products.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats frontier AI as a potential existential danger and is using subcommittee oversight powers on a leading lab.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Hawley reacts to Trump executive order setting voluntary cyber reviews of advanced AI
evidence.quote: I would go farther. I think we ought to enact my legislation that I have with Senator [Richard] Blumenthal that would make that sort of reporting and monitoring mandatory
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed the order but said voluntary review is not enough and mandatory testing should be law.

evidence.title: Axios AI+DC Summit: Hawley pushes ban on AI chatbots for minors (GUARD Act, S.3062)
evidence.quote: The first thing we need to do is we need to pass legislation that would prevent AI chatbots from targeting minor children
evidence.what_it_shows: His GUARD Act, which the Judiciary Committee later passed 22-0, would ban AI companions for minors and add criminal penalties for chatbots that sexualize children.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI LEAD Act (S.2937), product liability for AI systems
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs letting people hurt by AI sue the developer like any other defective product.

evidence.title: Sponsor: AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act (S.3108)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require companies to report AI-driven layoffs to the government.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI Whistleblower Protection Act (S.1792)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports legal protection for AI company employees who report safety problems.

evidence.title: Blumenthal-Hawley Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act (licensing regime, liability, transparency)
evidence.quote: Congress must act on AI regulation, and these principles should form the backbone
evidence.what_it_shows: As far back as 2023 he proposed licensing sophisticated general-purpose models through an independent oversight body.

evidence.title: Press release: Hawley warns 'AI threatens the working man' at NatCon 5
evidence.quote: millions of Americans out of work. That's not any conspiracy theory, by the way. That's what the tech titans openly tell us.
evidence.what_it_shows: He casts AI as a threat to jobs and liberty and says protecting children should be the lodestar for guardrails.

evidence.title: Washington Examiner: Public First Action launches $15 million project featuring Hawley among pro-guardrail Republicans
evidence.what_it_shows: An AI safety group is spending to promote him, along with Sens. Cotton and Moody and Rep. Donalds, as Republicans who back AI guardrails.

evidence.title: Hawley op-ed, 'AI Will Control Us If We Do Not Control It' (The Free Press)
evidence.what_it_shows: Hawley argued the federal government must set binding rules on AI jobs impacts, data centers and child safety, that AI 'is a question of self-government' that 'cannot be left to' Silicon Valley, and that the final stake is 'the conquest of some men by other men.'

evidence.title: Hawley, Blumenthal and Padilla remarks at Senate Judiciary markup of the GUARD Act (22-0 vote)
evidence.what_it_shows: At the unanimous committee vote to ban AI companions for minors, Hawley said a beneficial AI age 'is a choice, not an inevitability,' Blumenthal predicted tech companies would fight the bill 'with armies of lawyers and lobbyists,' and Padilla said he would keep refining one section.

evidence.title: Hawley document-request letters to Character.AI, Google, Meta, OpenAI and Snap on AI chatbot policies after Judiciary subcommittee hearing
evidence.what_it_shows: Following his Sept 16, 2025 hearing with parents of children who died after chatbot interactions, Hawley demanded all communications about the companies' AI chatbot policies.

evidence.title: Bipartisan senators' letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on AI chatbot policies permitting 'romantic or sensual' conversations with children
evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators demanded details on how Meta's chatbot safety policies for minors were developed, asked for more visible disclosures and a ban on targeted ads to under-18 users, writing that 'the wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.'

evidence.title: Hawley letter to Mark Zuckerberg launching Judiciary subcommittee investigation into Meta AI chatbots and children
evidence.what_it_shows: Hawley demanded Meta preserve and produce all versions of its 'GenAI: Content Risk Standards' by Sept 19, 2025, after reports its rules allowed chatbots to have 'romantic' and 'sensual' exchanges with children.

evidence.what_it_shows: Ten senators told Meta they were 'alarmed' by its chatbot policies, asked how its minor-safety rules were developed, and demanded Meta ban targeted ads to under-18s, improve disclosures and add mental-health referrals.

evidence.title: Hawley document requests to Character.AI, Google, Meta, OpenAI and Snap on AI chatbot policies after Judiciary subcommittee hearing
evidence.what_it_shows: Following testimony from parents whose children died after chatbot interactions, Hawley demanded five companies turn over all communications about their chatbot policies by Oct 17, 2025, writing 'children are dead. Families are broken.'

evidence.what_it_shows: The subcommittee chair and Judiciary ranking member told Roblox it 'appears to prioritize revenue and engagement metrics over the safety and well-being of our children,' cited 65,381 suspected exploitation reports in 2025, and directed it to preserve all child-safety records.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Hawley opposed the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws in the 2025 budget bill, said he would offer an amendment to strip it, and cheered when a preemption provision was dropped from the NDAA, calling it a terrible provision that should stay out.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Bentz says Oregon will run short of power as data centers and electrification grow, and his answer is to build faster: permitting reform, more transmission, nuclear power and, in his words at an AI hearing, waiving environmental rules. He voted for the SPEED Act. He has not proposed conditions on data centers themselves.

evidence.title: Bend Bulletin: Bentz warns of future power shortfall in Oregon, calls for changes to energy policy
evidence.quote: I asked them directly if they have enough power to meet demand around here. And the answer was no.
evidence.what_it_shows: He cites Prineville data centers among the drivers of a looming shortage and wants Oregon to lift its nuclear restrictions and speed transmission.

evidence.title: Bend Bulletin: Bentz on permitting reform
evidence.quote: If we don’t streamline permitting, we’re not going to build what we need in time.
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs federal permitting changes to speed power lines and generation to meet data center-driven demand.

evidence.title: House roll call 356: passage of H.R. 4776 SPEED Act (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted for the NEPA permitting overhaul meant to accelerate energy and infrastructure projects. Recorded vote: Yea.

evidence.title: KOBI-TV: Congressman Bentz urges passage of SPEED Act in light of energy shortfalls
evidence.quote: We need about as much power in the future as we have today and we need it really soon, so that means we have to about double the amount we have in the Northwest
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants the Senate to pass permitting reform, citing a 9-gigawatt Northwest shortfall and maxed-out transmission.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: House Energy and Commerce hearing on AI's role in energy and climate (Bentz remarks)
evidence.quote: We need to waive environmental rules, we need to push things aside. We need to create exemptions. We need to get past this haystack of obstacles that we created for ourselves to protect things.
evidence.what_it_shows: He argued for clearing environmental and permitting obstacles to build AI energy infrastructure quickly.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: Bentz frames AI as an existential race the United States must win against China and wants obstacles cleared, not new mandates. At a May 2025 hearing he called consumer protection serious but steered toward how AI is funded, and he has not backed AI safety rules.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: House Energy and Commerce hearing on AI's role in energy and climate (Bentz on winning the race)
evidence.quote: Why It's absolutely essential that we win this race to a goal that's not as clear as I would like.
evidence.what_it_shows: He called AI competition with China an existential issue and asked witnesses to make the public case for it.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: House subcommittee hearing on AI Regulation and the Future of US Leadership (Bentz remarks)
evidence.quote: the question about consumer protection is interesting and serious and I'm happy for our discussion of it
evidence.what_it_shows: At the hearing that launched Republicans' national AI framework push, he focused on how the trillions invested in AI get funded and whether smaller players can compete, not on new rules.

tech_regulation.label: Mixed
tech_regulation.summary: Mixed. Bentz sponsors a bipartisan bill ordering an FTC study of social media's effects on kids and joined the 2021 GOP task force on reining in Big Tech, but he stresses caution about government action and in 2021 amended a House antitrust bill to make it friendlier to innovation.

evidence.title: H.R.6290 Safe Social Media Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He sponsors a bill directing the FTC to study social media use among people under 17.

evidence.title: Press release: Bentz's Safe Social Media Act passes Energy and Commerce subcommittee
evidence.quote: This Act will require a study that will gather the data necessary to learn how and what social media is impacting our children. My bill is a necessary step toward real accountability.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants data on harms to kids first, calling the study a step toward accountability rather than proposing mandates.

evidence.title: Press release: Bentz appointed to GOP Task Force on Big Tech Censorship and Data
evidence.quote: we must make sure government actions are carefully considered as we weigh many subjects, including: free speech, innovation, data privacy, national security, and the welfare of consumers
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined a Republican effort to rein in Big Tech but urged caution, and his amendment to a 2021 antitrust bill made it more supportive of innovation.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No public position found. I searched for Bentz statements on the state AI law moratorium, the Dec 2025 executive order, the March 2026 White House framework and Energy and Commerce's federal framework work, and found none, even though he sits on the committee drafting it.

data_centers.label: No public position found
data_centers.summary: No statement on data centers found as of Sept 2026, even though Wisconsin's boom is a top issue and he sat next to a data center bill author on PBS Wisconsin. He has voted for permitting reform and grid reliability bills that tech companies favored, but never tied them to data centers himself.

evidence.title: Press release: Fitzgerald votes to pass the SPEED Act (NEPA permitting reform) and the Power Plant Reliability Act
evidence.quote: The SPEED Act reforms NEPA by setting clear timelines, limiting frivolous litigation, and cutting through the bureaucratic obstacles liberals have imposed to stop growth.
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs faster permitting and keeping power plants open, bills that AI infrastructure builders supported, but his statement does not mention data centers.

evidence.title: Roll call 145: Yea on H.R. 1, whose 10-year state AI moratorium critics said would have blocked local rules on data centers
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted for the House budget bill containing the moratorium; the Center for American Progress Action argues that language would have curtailed local control over data centers. Recorded vote: Yea.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: At a Sept 2025 Judiciary AI hearing he asked how adopting European-style AI regulation would affect the U.S. AI industry, a question framed to highlight the costs of heavy rules. No other AI safety statements found.

evidence.title: R Street review of Adam Thierer's Sept 2025 testimony before the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Courts, Intellectual Property, AI and the Internet
evidence.what_it_shows: Fitzgerald, a subcommittee member, asked how embracing European-style regulation would affect U.S. AI development, which the pro-innovation witness used to argue Europe's rules stifle AI; the framing leans light touch.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Fitzgerald chairs the House antitrust subcommittee and says his priority is holding Big Tech accountable for censorship. He backed TikTok divestiture, a child online safety bill and a Section 230 court brief, but he also attacks aggressive antitrust enforcement as anti-business, so his record is mixed.

evidence.title: Press release: Fitzgerald statement on being named Antitrust Subcommittee Chairman
evidence.quote: hold Big Tech accountable for censorship, reverse the Biden Administration’s anti-business agenda, and fight the federal bureaucracy
evidence.what_it_shows: His stated agenda targets platforms over content moderation while opposing broader regulatory activism, a conservative version of reining in Big Tech.

evidence.title: Heritage Foundation amicus brief in Gonzalez v. Google filed on behalf of 17 lawmakers including Fitzgerald
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined a brief asking the Supreme Court to narrow Section 230's liability shield for tech platforms.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 7521 (118th), Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (TikTok divestiture)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed forcing TikTok's sale or ban, a major intervention against a tech platform.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 5182 (118th), Child Online Safety Modernization Act of 2023
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stronger reporting duties on online companies for child abuse material.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 4791 (118th), Free Speech Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs barring government officials from pressuring platforms to remove posts, part of his censorship focus.

evidence.title: Press release: Fitzgerald letter to FTC Chair Lina Khan demanding neutrality in antitrust enforcement
evidence.what_it_shows: He criticized the Biden-era FTC's aggressive antitrust posture as politicized, the light-touch side of his record.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: Fitzgerald voted for the House budget bill that included a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws. He has not made a direct statement on preempting state AI rules that we could find. Because the only evidence is a vote on a sweeping budget bill, no position is shown.

evidence.title: Roll call 145: Yea on H.R. 1, including the 10-year moratorium on enforcing state and local AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: He supported the bill carrying the moratorium; because it was a sweeping budget package, this is weak evidence of a considered preemption stance. Recorded vote: Yea.

china_chips.label: No public position found
china_chips.summary: No position found on AI chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China as of Sept 2026. He is hawkish on Chinese tech in other ways, leading a bill to deny U.S. patents to blacklisted Chinese firms, and he voted against the 2022 CHIPS Act subsidies.

evidence.title: Press release: Fitzgerald, Moolenaar and Issa introduce the Prohibiting Adversarial Patents Act and Foreign Adversary Patent Disclosure Act
evidence.quote: The Chinese Communist Party has spent years exploiting the American economy to advance its own technological and military ambitions
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows a hawkish posture on Chinese technology firms like Huawei, though the bills concern patents, not chip exports.

evidence.title: Press release: Fitzgerald issues statement on voting NO on the CHIPS bill
evidence.quote: Despite my support of domestic manufacturing in critical technologies like semiconductors, this legislation potentially creates as many problems as it hopes to fix
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed the $280 billion chip subsidy package as bloated and lacking guardrails against China benefiting, a fiscal objection rather than an export-control position.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Letlow has championed Meta's Hyperion data center in her district since its 2024 launch, calling the $50 billion expansion 'transformative' and 'responsible growth' and praising Meta's promise to cover energy and water costs so ratepayers are protected. Reporting in Aug 2026 showed she signed a Meta NDA in June 2024, before the project was public, and later bought Meta and Nvidia stock that she disclosed late.

evidence.title: Press release: Letlow statement on Meta expansion in Northeast Louisiana
evidence.quote: I'm thrilled that Meta is committing to cover the full cost, protecting ratepayers while supporting our local businesses, education, and infrastructure. After years of our children moving away, responsible growth is on the horizon
evidence.what_it_shows: She celebrates the project and treats Meta's voluntary pledge to pay for energy, water and infrastructure as sufficient ratepayer protection, without asking for new conditions.

evidence.title: WWNO/Gulf States Newsroom: Letlow's remarks at Meta's Dec 2024 launch event
evidence.quote: I was so excited about it, I even skipped a vote in Washington. Don't tell anybody, please.
evidence.what_it_shows: She skipped a House vote to attend the public launch of the Richland Parish data center and cheered it on.

evidence.title: KNOE: Letlow addresses budget bill and Meta data center at Monroe luncheon
evidence.quote: I was just doing some TV interviews the other day and said $12 billion, but I was talking to Scott and he said, 'Julia, it's going to far surpass that.'
evidence.what_it_shows: She touted the project's growing size as a win for her district and did not raise power, water or cost concerns.

evidence.title: WWNO investigation: Letlow signed a Meta NDA on June 29, 2024, then bought Meta and Nvidia stock disclosed late
evidence.quote: She didn't disclose those trades for more than a year, well past the 45-day deadline required under the STOCK Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Her financial ties to the project's builder and chip supplier drew scrutiny; this is context on her boosterism, not a policy statement.

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Carter takes a balanced line. He signed a March 2026 New Democrat letter calling data center growth 'vital for America's economy' while asking the Energy Department for a national plan on grid reliability, consumer costs, and water. At the July 2026 markup he spoke for the Ratepayer Protection Act, stressing it does not dictate outcomes to Louisiana. We found no comment from him on Meta's Richland Parish project.

evidence.quote: Rapidly increasing demand for data centers, driven by cloud computing and AI, is vital for America's economy and competitiveness. However, this expansion strains electricity grids, land, water, and community infrastructure
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants managed growth: a DOE plan on electricity demand, consumer costs, water efficiency and geographic spread, not a pause.

evidence.quote: This bill doesn’t force state regulators to adopt any specific rate structure. It sets a federal standard for state utility commissions to consider, then use their own judgement to decide whether and how to apply it.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions

ai_risk.label: Light touch

evidence.quote: That's the kind of innovation and competition that's going to make us win this really important AI race with China.
evidence.what_it_shows: His framing is innovation and beating China; the only federal role he described was keeping Big Tech from blocking smaller innovators.

evidence.title: Press release: Schmitt amendment to cut NTIA funding for 'algorithmic justice' work
evidence.quote: This amendment would stop the NTIA's woke transfer, cutting the Biden NTIA's ability to fund an Orwellian "algorithmic justice" bureaucracy.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treated federal work on algorithmic bias as a bureaucracy to defund, a light-touch signal.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act (S.1290)
evidence.what_it_shows: His AI bills focus on workforce mapping, not risk controls.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Mixed but leaning toward targeted rules: he wants Section 230 protection pulled from platforms that act as publishers or take down speech at government request, cosponsors ad-tech antitrust and a bill to break Big Tech's hold on Pentagon AI contracts, and hopes for bipartisan kids' online safety action. He also raised free speech concerns about the NO FAKES Act.

evidence.title: Press release: Schmitt questions witnesses on screentime and social media algorithms at Senate Commerce hearing
evidence.quote: they should lose that Section 230 protection. There's not really been a hammer behind that.
evidence.what_it_shows: He said platforms that act as publishers should lose Section 230 immunity and voiced hope for bipartisan agreement on protecting kids online.

evidence.title: Sponsor: COLLUDE Act (S.69)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would strip a platform's liability shield when it removes political speech at the government's request; his Big Tech focus is censorship.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AMERICA Act (S.1060), digital advertising antitrust
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs breaking up conflicts of interest in Google-style ad markets.

evidence.title: Press release: Schmitt reintroduces Protecting AI and Cloud Competition in Defense Act with Sen. Warren (S.1775)
evidence.quote: I am proud to be leading this bill that promotes competition, as well as encourages innovation so the U.S. can continue to lead A.I.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants to stop the Pentagon from handing AI and cloud contracts to a few giants without competition.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: Senate Commerce hearing on 30 years of Section 230
evidence.quote: And the government can't outsource that censorship to private actors either, can it?
evidence.what_it_shows: His questioning centered on government jawboning of platforms rather than platform accountability for harms.

evidence.title: Roll Call: AI deepfakes (NO FAKES Act) bill advanced by Senate Judiciary Committee; Schmitt among senators voicing free speech concerns

evidence.title: Startland News: Schmitt agrees consistent federal oversight is key at KC Tech Council AI roundtable
evidence.quote: It's probably important for the federal government to come in and preempt this
evidence.what_it_shows: He explicitly endorsed federal preemption of a state-by-state patchwork, adding that Kansas and Missouri having different AI rules is not going to work.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Chip Security Act (S.1705)

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 (S.4429)

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Moylan backs targeted transparency rules rather than broad AI limits. He co-led a bipartisan bill making companies report AI-driven layoffs and cosponsored bills requiring labels and standards for AI-made images, video and audio. He has not spoken about advanced AI as a major danger or called for licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs, Horsford, Moylan introduce the AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act
evidence.quote: As these technologies continue to evolve, Congress must ensure we have transparent and reliable data to better understand how AI is impacting workers, industries, and local economies, including communities like Guam.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he wants Congress to require data on how AI is hitting workers, a targeted transparency rule rather than a broad AI limit.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.9352 AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Makes large companies and federal agencies report AI-related layoffs to the Labor Department; he is one of the three original leads.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.8479 Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Requires AI-made pictures, video and audio to be labeled so people know they are not real; a targeted guardrail on deepfakes.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.8893 Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act (119th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Has the government set standards for telling when content was made by AI; a second version of the same labeling idea.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.7766 Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed AI content labeling in the prior Congress too, so this is a repeated position, not a one-off.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.5077 CREATE AI Act of 2023 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported a national shared computing resource for AI research; shows he is not anti-AI, he pairs guardrails with support for building the technology.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Thin record. He cosponsored a 2023 bill making online companies report child abuse material more fully, but no statements were found on Section 230, antitrust, kids online safety, or privacy law. The score rests on that single cosponsorship.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R.5182 Child Online Safety Modernization Act of 2023 (118th)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs making online platforms report child abuse material more fully and keep the evidence longer; a targeted rule on tech companies.

preemption.label: No public position found
preemption.summary: No public position found on whether states should be allowed to write their own AI laws. As a non-voting delegate he had no vote on the Senate roll call. Searches for his views on the H.R.1 moratorium, the Dec 2025 executive order, the Mar 2026 White House framework, and the GUARDRAILS Act turned up nothing; his July 2025 review of H.R.1 for Guam covered SNAP, Medicaid and tipped income and did not mention the AI provision.

evidence.title: Guam Daily Post: Delegate says little impact on Guam from new federal budget (H.R.1)
evidence.what_it_shows: His detailed review of the reconciliation bill's effects on Guam did not mention the AI moratorium fight, so he took no public side on preemption.

data_centers.label: Build faster
data_centers.summary: Burlison is Missouri's most vocal data center champion. He wrote that Missouri must lead the data center revolution, calls water worries overblown, says opposition is stoked by China or solar and wind interests, and held Oversight hearings promoting AI infrastructure. He allows that projects deserve oversight and local review of measurable impacts, but opposes blanket opposition and moratoriums.

evidence.title: Op-ed (St. Louis Post-Dispatch, posted on his site): Missouri Must Lead America's Data Center Revolution
evidence.quote: Projects like these deserve oversight, but blanket opposition only slows us down. Missouri can pursue this responsibly while creating high-paying jobs, strengthening schools, and attracting new investment across the state.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants Missouri to build data centers aggressively, criticizes local moratoriums and argues state law already protects ratepayers.

evidence.title: Missourinet: Burlison says data centers are a national security issue
evidence.what_it_shows: He said the only groups with reason to demonize data centers are the solar and wind industry or foreign actors, that data centers pay for infrastructure and cut peak demand, and that you do not want your data housed in China (page blocked; quotes seen only via a summary).

evidence.title: Newstalk KZRG: Burlison blames China for hate against data centers
evidence.quote: From what I understand, most of them use less water than a car wash
evidence.what_it_shows: He dismisses water-use concerns and warns that foreign actors including China shape online opposition.

evidence.title: Missouri Times: Burlison post blaming China for anti-data-center content
evidence.quote: They know the future runs on AI and data centers, and they want the edge.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames anti-data-center sentiment as something China wants Missourians to feel.

evidence.title: Newstalk KZRG: Burlison defends AI, says data centers deserve a fair look
evidence.quote: Whether it’s a data center or any other business, I think we should approach them all the same way
evidence.what_it_shows: He accepts local review of power, water and traffic impacts but rejects fear-based restrictions on data centers as central planning.

evidence.title: Oversight subcommittee release: Burlison opening statement at hearing on the economics of AI, data centers and power consumption
evidence.quote: This rapid growth is astounding and has concerning implications for both current and future power generation.
evidence.what_it_shows: He acknowledges data center power demand is a real planning problem while praising the Stargate buildout and Trump's AI dominance order.

evidence.title: Oversight release: Burlison remarks at roundtable on economic competition with China
evidence.quote: As part of undermining American AI development, China is funding nonprofits in the U.S. and spreading propaganda to impede data center construction and energy projects.
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats obstacles to data center construction as part of China's strategy against American AI.

evidence.title: Press release: Burlison reintroduces Reliable Grid Act to limit EPA rules that reduce dispatchable power
evidence.quote: My Reliable Grid Act puts an end to this madness and stops future radical EPA tyrants from destroying our energy infrastructure
evidence.what_it_shows: His grid bill is a supply-side answer (keep fossil plants running) that supporters explicitly tie to new demand from data centers and AI.

ai_risk.label: Hands off
ai_risk.summary: Burlison argues regulation makes American AI slower, not safer, praised Trump for revoking Biden's AI order, and was one of only two House members to vote against the Take It Down Act on AI deepfake porn. He does support limits on government AI surveillance (the Flock-Off Act) and once said Congress should fight potential AI abuse, but his overall stance is hands off.

evidence.title: Oversight release: Burlison opening statement at roundtable on AI and American power
evidence.quote: Government-mandated red tape and free-speech constraints do not make AI safer, they just make American companies slower while our adversaries sprint ahead unchecked.
evidence.what_it_shows: He explicitly opposes AI regulation and praised the revocation of Biden's AI executive order.

evidence.title: Oversight release: Burlison remarks on regulating AI into mediocrity
evidence.quote: It requires leaders who are willing to fight for American competitiveness rather than regulate it into mediocrity.
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames AI policy as a race with China in which regulation is the enemy.

evidence.title: Newsweek: Burlison one of two Republicans voting against the Take It Down Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted no on the 409-2 bill criminalizing nonconsensual AI deepfake sexual images, the only bipartisan AI guardrail to become law in 2025.

evidence.title: Press release: Chairman Burlison announces hearing on America's AI leadership
evidence.quote: This subcommittee is committed to analyzing how Congress can assist the Trump Administration’s ongoing efforts to unleash AI responsibly while also examining pro-market solutions that foster new innovation.
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants Congress to help the administration reduce barriers to AI, with pro-market rather than regulatory answers.

evidence.title: Press release: Burlison attends first meeting of the bipartisan AI Task Force
evidence.quote: Congress should work to ensure our country's continued leadership in AI, while also fighting against potential abuse
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier, more balanced framing that paired AI leadership with fighting abuse.

evidence.title: Carter County Times: Massie and Burlison introduce the Flock-Off Act to defund AI surveillance cameras
evidence.quote: The federal government should not use taxpayer dollars to build a surveillance state that tracks law-abiding Americans.
evidence.what_it_shows: Contrasting evidence: he wants to cut federal funds for AI-augmented license plate readers and biometric cameras on Fourth Amendment grounds.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 9497 AI Advancement and Reliability Act of 2024
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a neutral bill creating a NIST center to study AI reliability and trustworthiness.

evidence.title: Oversight hearing wrap-up on harmful deepfakes: Burlison asks about detection technology
evidence.quote: Can we talk about the technology that is possibly available to recognize or identify AI and how that might be applied in a commercial setting?
evidence.what_it_shows: His interest in deepfakes centered on commercial detection tools rather than new rules.

tech_regulation.label: Mixed
tech_regulation.summary: Mixed, libertarian pattern. He sponsors the Auto Data Privacy and Autonomy Act to give drivers control of car data, co-leads the Flock-Off Act against surveillance cameras and opposes FISA surveillance, yet he voted against the Take It Down Act and calls Biden-era AI rules free-speech constraints.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 6734 Auto Data Privacy and Autonomy Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require written consent before automakers access or sell vehicle data and bar transfers to foreign adversaries.

evidence.title: Press release: Burlison and Lee reintroduce vehicle data privacy bill
evidence.quote: Auto manufacturers have quietly turned cars into data-harvesting machines
evidence.what_it_shows: He is willing to impose privacy mandates on companies when the issue is personal data ownership.

evidence.title: Newstalk KZRG: Burlison targets Big Brother surveillance with federal funding threat
evidence.quote: This is not just people that have got a warrant or criminals. This is all of us,
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants to withhold federal grants from communities using AI-powered license plate readers, a restriction on surveillance tech.

evidence.title: Newsweek: Burlison one of two House votes against the Take It Down Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed a platform takedown mandate for nonconsensual intimate images that nearly every other member supported.

preemption.label: Mixed or conditional
preemption.summary: Signed a letter: House Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence final report (118th Congress) - Federal Preemption of State Law chapter.

evidence.title: House Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence final report (118th Congress) - Federal Preemption of State Law chapter
evidence.what_it_shows: The 24-member bipartisan task force found that preempting state AI laws 'is complex,' has 'benefits and drawbacks,' can be done via floors or ceilings, and must use precise definitions; its only preemption recommendation was that Congress commission a study of existing federal and state AI regulations. It did not endorse a moratorium.

china_chips.label: Leans sell more
china_chips.summary: Burlison praised the administration for clearing the way for trusted allies to access American AI technology as part of an American AI export stack, a lean toward exporting more. He has not taken a position found on Nvidia chip sales to China or the Chip Security Act.

evidence.title: Oversight release: Burlison opening statement at AI and American power roundtable
evidence.quote: The Administration is also clearing the way for trusted allies to access American AI technology and incorporate their technologies into the American AI export stack, a key advantage we must sustain over our adversaries.
evidence.what_it_shows: He endorses promoting exports of the American AI stack to allies; he says nothing about controls on sales to China.

pacs.agenda: Elect 'pro-innovation, pro-AI' candidates of both parties; push a single national AI framework / federal preemption over state AI laws; oppose candidates who back state AI-safety statutes (chief targe
pacs.detail: Endorsed by LTF May 8, 2026; Think Big IEs $292,419 (May 8-11). Her spokesman said she 'did not seek out the endorsement'; she then backtracked, saying 'I refuse to ignore industry and deny workers a seat at the table.'

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Hoyle cosponsors a bill to keep the cost of data center power lines and plants off family electric bills and voted against the SPEED Act permitting bill. I found no speeches or statements of her own about data centers.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6529 Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined a bill meant to stop household electric bills from rising to pay for grid upgrades that AI data centers need.

evidence.title: Roll call 356: Nay on H.R. 4776 SPEED Act (permitting reform)
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted against a permitting-reform bill whose backers said it would speed energy and data center construction; a general environmental-review vote, so weak evidence on its own. Recorded vote: Nay.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Hoyle says AI must be regulated so it does not hurt workers or people, and she cosponsors bills on AI pricing, AI election deepfakes, and keeping humans in control of nuclear launches. But after the pro-industry super PAC Leading the Future endorsed her she shifted to praising a common sense federal framework and industry cooperation, so her stance is targeted guardrails with a mixed recent tone.

evidence.title: Transformer: Hoyle's first response to the Leading the Future endorsement
evidence.quote: AI must be regulated so that it does not harm labor or people
evidence.what_it_shows: Her initial statement distanced her from the anti-regulation super PAC and put worker protection first.

evidence.title: Transformer: Hoyle's revised statement after Leading the Future was asked for comment
evidence.quote: Workers and consumers need to be protected and we need to have a broad federal framework based on common sense.
evidence.what_it_shows: Within days she softened, saying she wants industry at the table and a federal framework; this is the main contradictory signal.

evidence.title: Leading the Future endorsement and Think Big spending for Hoyle
evidence.quote: $292,419 of publicly disclosed spending by Think Big, a super PAC affiliated with and funded by Leading the Future, on ads supporting Hoyle
evidence.what_it_shows: The AI industry super PAC endorsed her on May 8, 2026 (first reported by Axios) and its affiliate spent on her primary; she said she did not seek it but ultimately accepted it.

evidence.title: Yahoo News / NBC: AI industry super PAC ads in 2026 primaries
evidence.quote: "Standing up to big pharma, fighting for local jobs, Val Hoyle doesn't back down," says an ad backing the Oregon Democratic representative
evidence.what_it_shows: National coverage listed her among candidates boosted by AI-industry-funded super PAC ads ahead of her primary.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 4640 Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs banning companies from using AI and personal data to charge people different prices or pay workers different wages.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 5272 Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports banning AI-made fake audio or video of candidates meant to trick voters.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 2894 Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for a hard rule that a human, not an AI, must decide any nuclear launch.

tech_regulation.label: Targeted rules
tech_regulation.summary: Hoyle wants targeted rules on tech companies, especially privacy standards that apply to every platform and a ban on AI-driven surveillance pricing. She voted against forcing the sale of TikTok, saying singling out one company was the wrong approach.

evidence.title: Press release: Hoyle's statement on voting against the bill forcing the sale of TikTok
evidence.quote: This is not just a TikTok problem, it's a problem with social media and tech companies across-the-board.
evidence.what_it_shows: She opposed a company-specific ban and called instead for the same data privacy and user engagement standards for all social media platforms.

evidence.title: NW Labor Press: grocery union campaign against surveillance pricing
evidence.quote: Representative Val Hoyle (D-Oregon) is a lead sponsor on a House version.
evidence.what_it_shows: Labor press identifies her as a House lead on banning personalized pricing based on consumer data, in line with her H.R. 4640 cosponsorship.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 8622 Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She supported outlawing landlords' use of shared pricing algorithms to push up rents.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Hoyle has strongly opposed federal preemption of state AI laws, signing the November 2025 letter against the NDAA moratorium and calling the White House effort outrageous and a Big Tech backroom deal. Her later acceptance of an endorsement from Leading the Future, which opposes state AI regulation, and her call for a broad federal framework muddy the picture but do not endorse preemption.

evidence.title: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and a preemption executive order
evidence.quote: Congress should not freeze state and local AI safeguards, least of all when there are no meaningful federal protections in place.
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed a letter telling congressional leaders not to revive the moratorium or use an executive order to override state AI laws.

evidence.title: Transformer: Hoyle's past comments on the NDAA preemption push
evidence.quote: “outrageous,” a “Big Tech backroom deal,” and “government overreach.”
evidence.what_it_shows: Transformer reports she used these words for the White House effort to preempt state AI laws through the defense bill.

evidence.title: Leading the Future endorsement of Hoyle and her acceptance
evidence.quote: Leading the Future endorsed me because they are working to build a broader coalition around AI regulation and I don’t believe we can put our heads in the sand and ignore the industry.
evidence.what_it_shows: Contradictory signal: the PAC says it opposes state AI regulation and backs the White House framework, and she chose to accept its support.

china_chips.label: No public position found
china_chips.summary: No public position found on chip export controls as of Sept 2026. She voted against forcing TikTok's sale by its Chinese owner and welcomed CHIPS Act investment in Oregon, but neither addresses selling AI chips to China.
