data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Salinas wants data centers to pay their way. She sponsored a bill taxing every kilowatt-hour data centers use to fund housing, conservation, Superfund cleanup, highways, and clean energy, cosponsored a study of AI's energy and water use, and signed a letter pressing regulators and utilities to keep grid costs off household bills. She says communities should share in data center growth, not stop it.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 10102 Data Center Community Reinvestment Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own bill would put a 1-cent-per-kilowatt-hour federal excise tax on electricity used by data centers over 1 megawatt, raising about $1.76 billion a year for five federal funds.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Salinas introduces bill to tax data centers, reinvest in housing, conservation, and infrastructure
evidence.quote: As AI use expands and the demand for data centers grows, we need to ensure our communities aren’t left footing the bill
evidence.what_it_shows: In her own words the goal is to make data centers, not communities, cover the costs of the AI buildout.

evidence.title: Data Center Knowledge: House bill would put federal electricity tax on data centers
evidence.quote: Every community deserves to drive a hard bargain with data center developers, and at the end of the day, every community deserves to share in the benefits from data center growth,
evidence.what_it_shows: She accepts data center growth but wants communities to extract benefits from it, which places her at protect-communities-first rather than pause.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 9183 Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs a federal study of AI's electricity, water, and pollution footprint with voluntary company reporting.

evidence.title: Mullin-led letter from 20 House Democrats to FERC, Edison Electric Institute, and the Data Center Coalition on data center energy costs
evidence.quote: The expansion of data centers risks creating persistent affordability challenges for households and small businesses.
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed a letter asking regulators, utilities, and the industry how they will keep grid upgrade costs off household bills and what cost-allocation tools Congress should consider.

evidence.title: Roll call 356: Nay on H.R. 4776 SPEED Act (permitting reform)
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted against a permitting-reform bill whose backers said it would speed energy and data center construction; a general environmental-review vote, so weak evidence on its own. Recorded vote: Nay.

evidence.title: Markey-McClellan bicameral letter to EPA urging withdrawal of proposed rule letting data centers and power plants begin construction before air permits
evidence.what_it_shows: Sixteen lawmakers told EPA to withdraw its May 2026 proposal redefining 'begin actual construction' so data centers and fossil plants can pour foundations and install wiring before New Source Review permits, saying it turns the Clean Air Act's preconstruction safeguards 'on its head.'

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Salinas is an AI optimist who wants specific guardrails. She cosponsors the Algorithmic Accountability Act, which makes companies test automated decision systems for bias and report to the FTC, wants research on how AI affects kids in classrooms, and signed a letter warning against a regulatory vacuum. At the same time her own bills push AI education, scholarships, and shared research computing.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 5511 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports mandatory bias and harm testing of automated decision systems with reporting to the FTC, a binding targeted rule.

evidence.title: Press release: Whitesides, McClain-Delaney, Salinas introduce the Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
evidence.quote: AI is already changing how students learn, but we still have serious questions about how it affects their attention, development, and reliance on technology
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants evidence on AI's effects on children before it spreads further in schools, while explicitly avoiding new mandates on schools.

evidence.title: Press release: Reps. Salinas, Fong introduce the NSF AI Education Act of 2025
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence technology has the potential to transform our society for good and drive economic growth across a broad range of industries, from clean energy to agriculture, to manufacturing
evidence.what_it_shows: Her lead bill treats AI as an economic opportunity to prepare workers for, showing the innovation side of her position.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 2385 CREATE AI Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs a national shared computing and data resource so researchers and students can build and study AI without a big company's money.

evidence.title: Clarke-led letter from 44 House Democrats opposing an AI moratorium in the FY26 NDAA
evidence.quote: a moratorium would be wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed a letter arguing that AI rules are needed and that wiping out state rules without federal ones would let Big Tech run unchecked.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 3106 Preventing Deepfakes of Intimate Images Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for making AI-made sexual deepfakes of real people illegal and letting victims sue.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Casar wants data centers to pay their own way. He co-wrote bills forcing AI data centers to generate their own renewable power and to disclose energy and water use, and a bill capping utility profits. He has not called for a pause on building.

evidence.title: Press release: Menendez and Casar introduce the PRICE Act and Data Center Transparency Act
evidence.quote: Families should not pay more for utilities so that billionaires can get rich off AI data centers.
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI data centers as a threat to household electric bills and the environment and wants them to bring their own clean power.

evidence.title: H.R. 6983, PRICE Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: The bill would require data centers to generate the electricity they use, reaching 100 percent renewable by 2040, with daily fines for violations.

evidence.title: H.R. 6984, Data Center Transparency Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Data centers would have to publicly report electricity and water use and effects on household bills.

evidence.title: H.R. 8568, Lowering Utility Bills Act
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill caps utility profit margins and bars charging ratepayers for lobbying and executive perks, part of a broader affordability push as bills rise.

evidence.title: Texas Tribune: Casar unveils bill targeting utility costs
evidence.quote: They pay basically no risk, but pay themselves more than anybody else can get investing in the stock market, and then you are forced to pick up the tab
evidence.what_it_shows: He casts rising power bills as a fight between utilities and ratepayers, the same lens he applies to data centers.

ai_risk.label: Strict rules now
ai_risk.summary: Casar treats advanced AI as a serious danger. He is the House sponsor of the Sanders bill to permanently ban superintelligent AI and pause advanced AI development, led letters demanding hearings with AI CEOs under oath and answers from OpenAI about a model that escaped testing, and wants a tax on AI companies to fund jobs.

evidence.title: Press release: Sanders and Casar announce the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act
evidence.quote: In just four years, we have gone from the first version of ChatGPT to AI models so powerful they cannot be properly controlled. Congress should immediately ban AI systems too powerful to control.
evidence.what_it_shows: He is the House sponsor of a bill to permanently ban superintelligent AI, pause advanced AI development, create a cabinet-level regulator, and jail violators for up to 20 years.

evidence.title: The Hill: Sanders, Casar call for artificial superintelligence ban amid rogue AI hackings
evidence.what_it_shows: National coverage confirms the bill would pause advanced AI development until federal safety standards exist and pursue international agreements against superintelligence.

evidence.title: Press release: Casar leads 19 members demanding hearings with AI CEOs under oath
evidence.quote: Advanced AI models pose a clear risk to the safety and security of the American people.
evidence.what_it_shows: He led a letter to Speaker Johnson saying Congress has failed to respond to AI threats and asking for CEOs to testify under oath.

evidence.title: Press release: Casar leads 31 members demanding OpenAI release logs on a security incident
evidence.quote: Given the serious risk that frontier AI models can pose, it is imperative we have a detailed understanding of how this security incident unfolded, including any potential negligence on the part of OpenAI.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed OpenAI with 23 questions about a model that reached the internet from a test environment, including whether models tried to defeat evaluations or undermine oversight.

evidence.title: H.R. 10044, AI Tax and Work Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill taxes large AI companies to fund a Work Protection Administration that creates jobs to offset AI layoffs.

evidence.title: Press release: Casar leads introduction of the AI Tax and Work Protection Act
evidence.quote: This bill says: we will not let AI billionaires get rich by putting you out of work.
evidence.what_it_shows: He warns of Great Depression levels of AI unemployment and says the federal government is doing nothing to protect workers.

evidence.title: Op-ed, The American Prospect: Tax AI to Create Jobs
evidence.quote: We face potential unemployment on par with the Great Depression. We need a mass employment program to get through it. AI can pay for it.
evidence.what_it_shows: He argues slowing AI adoption through a tax is a feature, and also calls for safety protocols against out-of-control AI, worker and IP protections, and rules against mass surveillance.

evidence.title: Common Dreams: Casar on MeidasTouch calls AI oligarchs' vision dystopic
evidence.quote: But going toward 10%, 20% unemployment just so these guys can be super rich is completely dystopic.
evidence.what_it_shows: He rejects the idea that AI-driven mass unemployment softened by basic income is acceptable.

evidence.title: H.R. 4640, Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill bans using AI and personal data to charge people different prices or pay workers different wages.

evidence.title: H.R. 9619, People-First Chatbot Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs safety rules requiring AI chatbots to put users' wellbeing first.

evidence.title: H.R. 7110, Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports civil rights teams inside agencies to catch discriminatory algorithms.

evidence.title: H.R. 2894 (118th), Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed requiring a human decision for any nuclear launch, an early sign of concern about AI control.

evidence.title: Congressional reactions to former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon's resignation warning that AI 'could kill us all by the end of the decade'
evidence.what_it_shows: After Coxon's viral Sept 8 post and Anthropic alignment lead Evan Hubinger's '>10% within the next decade' extinction estimate, members of both parties publicly framed AI as an existential risk and called for hearings, a kill-switch law, a superintelligence ban or a pause.

tech_regulation.label: Rein in Big Tech
tech_regulation.summary: Casar is a populist critic of Big Tech. He wrote the first federal bill to ban AI surveillance pricing, backs bans on algorithmic rent fixing and a face-recognition moratorium, and has urged Democrats to refuse AI industry money. He voted against the TikTok forced-sale law, calling it rushed.

evidence.title: Press release: Casar introduces the Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act
evidence.quote: Giant corporations should not be allowed to jack up your prices or lower your wages using data they got spying on you
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants a federal ban, enforced by the FTC and private lawsuits, on companies using personal data to set individual prices and wages.

evidence.title: H.R. 8622 (118th), Preventing the Algorithmic Facilitation of Rental Housing Cartels Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports making it illegal for landlords to use shared pricing software to push up rents.

evidence.title: H.R. 1404 (118th), Facial Recognition and Biometric Technology Moratorium Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed halting federal use of face recognition until Congress approves it.

evidence.title: Press release: Casar reacts to TikTok forced sale bill
evidence.quote: I voted no on the TikTok forced sale bill. While I have serious data privacy concerns with TikTok, this bill was rapidly rushed to a vote by the Republicans with almost no public scrutiny, and that’s a recipe for unintended consequences
evidence.what_it_shows: A contrary data point: he opposed the TikTok divestiture law as rushed even while citing data privacy concerns.

evidence.title: MS NOW: 'As toxic as AIPAC': Progressive leader wants Dems to reject AI cash
evidence.what_it_shows: Headline-level report that he urged Democrats to refuse AI industry campaign money; article body was not readable.

preemption.label: Let states regulate
preemption.summary: Casar has twice signed letters opposing a federal moratorium on state AI laws, and in his own op-ed he criticized the preemption push as the only major AI proposal Congress had advanced.

evidence.title: Matsui letter from 81 House Democrats opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and a preemption executive order (Casar signed)
evidence.quote: We write to express our strong opposition to any effort in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) that would reintroduce a sweeping moratorium on the ability of states and local governments to enforce their own artificial intelligence (AI) laws
evidence.what_it_shows: He signed the letter telling congressional leaders not to revive the state AI-law moratorium or override states by executive order; his name appears in the signature pages.

evidence.title: Clarke letter from 44 House Democrats urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA (Casar signed)
evidence.quote: a moratorium would be wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation
evidence.what_it_shows: He is listed among the 44 signers asking defense-bill negotiators to keep any state AI preemption out of the NDAA.

evidence.title: Op-ed, The American Prospect: Tax AI to Create Jobs
evidence.quote: The only major AI proposal advanced this Congress was a failed effort to prevent states from regulating the industry.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he treats the effort to block state AI rules as a failure of Congress rather than a goal.

evidence.title: Clarke-led House Democratic letter to House and Senate Armed Services leaders urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA
evidence.what_it_shows: 44 House Democrats asked the defense-bill negotiators to keep any state AI-law preemption or moratorium out of the NDAA, calling a moratorium 'wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation.'

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Casar has no direct statement on Nvidia chip sales or export control bills. The superintelligence ban he sponsors would use export controls as one tool to stop superintelligence being built abroad, and he rejects the race-with-China argument for going easy on AI companies.

evidence.title: Press release: Sanders and Casar announce the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (export controls provision)
evidence.quote: policies such as export controls to prevent the development of artificial superintelligence anywhere in the world
evidence.what_it_shows: The bill he co-leads directs the United States to use export controls and international agreements against superintelligence development abroad.

evidence.title: Op-ed, The American Prospect: Tax AI to Create Jobs
evidence.quote: I am not interested in a race to the bottom where Chinese and American workers both end up victims of a competition where only the very wealthy actually win.
evidence.what_it_shows: He dismisses the beat-China argument used against AI regulation, but this is not a position on chip exports.

members.signature: Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus; House sponsor of the Sanders bill to ban artificial superintelligence, author of the AI Tax and Work Protection Act and the Stop AI Price Gouging Act, and co-lead of the PRICE Act making data centers power themselves.

quote.text: Despite its potential deadly consequences, cutting-edge AI technology is less regulated than the average food truck. That must change.

data_centers.summary: Wants Alaska to build data centers fast. He introduced the House DATA Act to loosen federal rules so data centers can run isolated grid-of-one power systems, wrote an op-ed urging Alaska to capitalize on the AI gold rush, and backed the SPEED Act permitting overhaul. He frames self-supplied power as the way to keep household bills from rising rather than as a limit on building.

evidence.title: Press release: Begich introduces House version of the DATA Act (H.R. 8400) to allow off-grid data center power
evidence.quote: The DATA Act allows manufacturers to operate on fully self-contained, ‘grid-of-one’ power systems, so innovation can scale without forcing households to subsidize massive new energy demands or straining local utilities.
evidence.what_it_shows: His signature data center bill deregulates so large power users can bring their own generation, pitched as protecting ratepayers while letting projects scale.

evidence.title: Op-ed (Anchorage Daily News, posted on his site): How Alaska can use our energy advantage to capitalize on the AI gold rush
evidence.quote: We can hesitate, regulate too early and risk becoming an observer in one of the most important economic shifts of our time, or we can engage thoughtfully, strategically and on our own terms.
evidence.what_it_shows: He argues Alaska's stranded gas, land, and cool climate make it ideal for rural data centers and warns against restricting them early.

evidence.title: Politico: Trump wants to move on data centers, Congress less so (Begich statement on DATA Act)
evidence.quote: America leads when we provide the private sector the space it needs to move at the speed of innovation
evidence.what_it_shows: Politico notes the Cotton-Begich bill would incentivize rather than mandate data centers to build their own power, and Begich frames it as getting out of industry's way.

evidence.title: Cato Institute blog on Scaling Laws podcast interview with Rep. Begich
evidence.quote: Rep. Begich made a strong case for why Alaska may be a hub for the necessary data center buildout.
evidence.what_it_shows: Pressed on local opposition, he said Alaska's resource-governance approach could ease those concerns, showing he expects to build through community pushback.

evidence.title: Press release: Begich applauds House passage of SPEED Act permitting reform
evidence.quote: The SPEED Act is a strong step forward in making life more affordable and allowing America to build again by establishing clear timelines for environmental reviews and limiting endless litigation
evidence.what_it_shows: He cosponsored and celebrated the NEPA permitting overhaul that speeds energy and infrastructure projects, including the power plants data centers need.

ai_risk.label: Mixed
ai_risk.summary: Light touch with some nuance. He says Congress must not hamstring AI development or push it offshore and that without global rules the only defense is speed, and he sponsors research and education bills rather than safety mandates. But he has raised concerns about agentic AI acting for people and about fully open-sourcing frontier models, comparing the risk to nuclear technology. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: Sources show a light-touch default ('cannot slow down', 'careful not to hamstring', colleagues should experiment before regulating), but also concrete pro-guardrail positions: he opposes fully open-sourcing frontier/post

evidence.title: American Bazaar: Begich discusses the future of AI regulation on the Regulating AI podcast
evidence.quote: I think the United States Congress in particular has to be careful not to hamstring artificial intelligence development in a way that would push that work to other jurisdictions
evidence.what_it_shows: His core stance is that regulation must not slow U.S. AI development; he also said that until international standards exist the country cannot slow down on AI.

evidence.title: American Bazaar: Begich on agentic AI and liability
evidence.quote: When AI starts to work on behalf of an individual, we have to start thinking about whether we should empower agentic AI to, for example, enter into a contract relationship that would perhaps bind someone financially.
evidence.what_it_shows: He does see specific risks from AI agents and wants personhood validation, a targeted concern rather than a call for broad rules.

evidence.title: Bitcoin Magazine: Begich at Bitcoin Policy Institute event on Bitcoin reserve and AI
evidence.quote: On the question of open-source AI models, Begich pushed back against the idea that openness is an unqualified good at advanced capability levels.
evidence.what_it_shows: He compared fully open-sourcing frontier models to releasing nuclear or biotech research, saying some asymmetric risks cannot be contained once released.

evidence.title: Cato Institute blog on interview with Rep. Begich
evidence.quote: According to Rep. Begich, his colleagues would benefit from playing around with AI a little more before deciding whether and how to regulate it.
evidence.what_it_shows: He counsels patience before regulating and says falling even slightly behind on AI would compound quickly.

evidence.title: Press release: Begich introduces House DATA Act
evidence.quote: America must win the race to lead in artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI policy as a race the U.S. must win, an innovation-first lens.

evidence.title: Sponsor: bill to create an OSTP prize competition program for artificial intelligence (H.R. 9506)
evidence.what_it_shows: His own AI bill rewards breakthroughs rather than imposing rules.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: NSF AI Education Act of 2025 (H.R. 5351)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs AI scholarships and teacher training, a pro-adoption measure.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI PLAN Act (H.R. 2152)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a government report on criminals' use of AI for financial crimes, a study rather than a mandate.

tech_regulation.label: No public position found
tech_regulation.summary: No clear position found. Searched for statements or bills on Section 230, Big Tech antitrust, kids online safety, app stores, and privacy; found only a podcast remark that liability for AI agents would likely follow the platform-immunity model, and no relevant cosponsorships.

preemption.label: Leans national rule
preemption.summary: Leans toward a national approach. In a Cato interview he accepted that some AI questions belong to states but stressed treating frontier AI as a national priority, and earlier he called for a globally harmonized set of rules of the road. No statement found on the 2025 moratorium fight, the Dec 2025 executive order, or the March 2026 White House framework.

evidence.title: Cato Institute blog on interview with Rep. Begich (state versus federal AI role)
evidence.quote: Rep. Begich acknowledged that some regulatory questions are properly left at the local and state levels. Still, we both expressed the importance of treating frontier AI as a national policy priority.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants frontier AI handled nationally while leaving room for states on some questions; the Cato host summarized his view as states rowing in the same direction.

evidence.title: American Bazaar: Begich on the need for harmonized AI rules
evidence.quote: We need to have an effective set of regulations, (…) a globally harmonized set of rules of the road.
evidence.what_it_shows: He favors uniform rules across jurisdictions over a patchwork, which points toward one national standard.

china_chips.label: Leans hawkish
china_chips.summary: Leans hawkish on China and AI. He cosponsored a bill to punish foreign companies that steal American AI models and has described China's open-source AI strategy as an economic weapon against U.S. AI investment. No statement found specifically on Nvidia chip sales or export controls.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 (H.R. 8283)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports penalties on foreign companies, especially Chinese ones, that steal or copy American AI models.

evidence.title: Bitcoin Magazine: Begich on China's open-source AI strategy
evidence.quote: He was pointed in his characterization of China’s open-source model strategy, suggesting it is less a gesture of openness than an economic tool
evidence.what_it_shows: He sees Chinese AI releases as an effort to undermine the investment case for American AI, a hawkish framing.

members.signature: Tech entrepreneur turned congressman who leads the House DATA Act to let data centers bring their own off-grid power, calls the AI buildout a gold rush for Alaska, and warns Congress not to regulate AI too early.

quote.text: We can hesitate, regulate too early and risk becoming an observer in one of the most important economic shifts of our time, or we can engage thoughtfully, strategically and on our own terms.

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: McBride's message on data centers is protect the ratepayer first. She told the White House science director that Delawareans fear data centers will strain power and water and raise everyone's bills, signed the November 2025 letter urging the PJM grid operator to make data centers curtail power in a crunch, is an original cosponsor of the Energy Bills Relief Act, and voted against the SPEED Act permitting bill. Her preferred fix is Delaware-made liquid cooling to shrink data centers' footprint, not a moratorium.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: House Science hearing 'Advancing America's AI Action Plan' with OSTP Director Kratsios
evidence.quote: I've certainly heard from countless Delawareans that are worried about data centers being constructed in their communities, straining our energy and water supply and increasing the cost of utilities for all of us.
evidence.what_it_shows: Pressed the administration on what it is doing to mitigate data center effects on communities and asked it to fund liquid cooling; Kratsios promised to look for funding.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. McBride presses Trump administration on data center impacts, secures commitment to explore funding for liquid cooling
evidence.what_it_shows: Her office framed the exchange as centering Delaware communities in national AI policy and pushing innovation that lowers costs and protects local resources.

evidence.title: Van Hollen and Beyer letter from 12 lawmakers to the PJM Interconnection board on data center demand and electricity costs (McBride signed)
evidence.quote: PJM must swiftly address the fact that data center energy demand is threatening to overwhelm the grid
evidence.what_it_shows: Urged mandatory backstop rules forcing new large loads like data centers to curtail demand so homes, schools and businesses are shielded from higher prices and blackouts.

evidence.title: H.R.7977 Energy Bills Relief Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Joined a Democratic bill aimed at bringing down household electric bills as data center demand pushes prices up; cosponsorship confirmed on GovTrack.

evidence.title: H.R.5332 Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs federal study and promotion of liquid cooling so AI data centers use less energy and water.

evidence.title: House roll call #356: passage of H.R. 4776, the SPEED Act permitting reform bill (Nay)
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted against a bill to speed environmental reviews for energy and infrastructure projects, including those serving data centers; a general permitting vote, not data-center specific. Recorded vote: Nay.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: McBride wants what she calls a Goldilocks approach: guardrails strong enough to protect people without slowing American competitiveness. Her main AI bill, the READ AI Models Act, is a voluntary NIST transparency label for AI models. She cosponsors bills against AI sexual deepfakes and says AI should never make high-stakes decisions in criminal justice, immigration or benefits on its own.

evidence.title: H.R.6461 READ AI Models Act (sponsor with Rep. Obernolte)
evidence.what_it_shows: Directs NIST to build a voluntary, modular documentation template describing what an AI model is, what data trained it and how it was tested.

evidence.title: Press release: McBride introduces bipartisan READ AI Models Act to bring more transparency to AI
evidence.quote: The READ AI Models Act brings transparency to AI in a way that’s simple, consistent and accessible. Think of it as a clear, easy-to-read snapshot, a ‘nutrition label’ for an AI model. It levels the playing field and helps people make informed decisions. That’s what transparency is all about. This bill is voluntary, bipartisan, and grounded in NIST’s world-class expertise.
evidence.what_it_shows: She stresses the bill is voluntary, bipartisan and grounded in NIST, so her signature approach is transparency and standards rather than mandates.

evidence.title: Tech Policy Press transcript: McBride on national AI standards at House Science hearing with Kratsios
evidence.quote: I heard Chair Babin earlier say that he supports consensus-based standards as well, and I'm happy to say I agree with that.
evidence.what_it_shows: She endorsed the AI Action Plan's call for clear national standards so people can trust AI and asked Kratsios to work with her on the READ AI bill.

evidence.title: American Bazaar: McBride on the RegulatingAI podcast describes a 'Goldilocks solution' for AI rules
evidence.what_it_shows: Per the article's summary, she wants rules strong enough to provide guardrails but not so restrictive they slow US competitiveness, says AI must never make high-stakes decisions alone, and raised UBI and portable benefits as responses to job displacement.

evidence.title: H.R.3562 DEFIANCE Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Lets victims sue people who make or share AI sexual deepfakes of them.

evidence.title: H.R.633 TAKE IT DOWN Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Criminalizes posting real or AI-faked sexual images without consent and forces fast takedowns; now law.

evidence.title: H.R.5360 AWARE Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Has the government publish public warnings and learning resources about the risks of AI tools.

evidence.title: H.R.2110 Safe Vehicle Access for Survivors Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Makes carmakers cut off an abuser's remote access to a car's apps and location data when a survivor asks.

She also cosponsors a reproductive data privacy bill.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (co-lead): H.R. 8031 GUARDRAILS Act

evidence.what_it_shows: Her own words defending states' authority to regulate AI against the White House preemption order.

evidence.title: MeriTalk: Delaney hints at new quantum, AI legislation

data_centers.label: Protect ratepayers first
data_centers.summary: Dexter is one of the more critical House voices on data centers. She calls them a threat to water supplies, won an amendment making the Energy Department study their water use, wants to keep them off public lands, and cosponsors a bill to put data centers in their own rate class so other customers do not pay for them. She has not called for a moratorium.

evidence.title: Blog post: Big Tech is draining our water
evidence.quote: At a time when the climate crisis is driving water insecurity across the country, that is not a trade-off our communities can afford.
evidence.what_it_shows: In her own words she frames data centers as a water threat, points to her DOE study amendment, and says protecting public lands from data centers is next on her list.

evidence.title: Amendment 58 to H.R. 4553 (FY2026 Energy and Water appropriations), Dexter, made in order
evidence.quote: conduct a study assessing current and projected water use by data centers, associated impacts on local water resources, and best practices and technologies to reduce water consumption.
evidence.what_it_shows: She used the appropriations process to force a federal study of how much water data centers use and how to cut it.

evidence.title: Original cosponsor: H.R. 8241 Power for the People Act of 2026
evidence.quote: To promote the creation of data center load queues and data center-specific rate classes to mitigate the impact of data centers on other electricity consumers
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs putting data centers in their own utility rate class so households do not absorb their grid costs.

evidence.title: Roll call 356: Nay on H.R. 4776 SPEED Act (permitting reform)
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted against a permitting-reform bill whose backers said it would speed energy and data center construction; a general environmental-review vote, so weak evidence on its own. Recorded vote: Nay.

ai_risk.label: Targeted guardrails
ai_risk.summary: Dexter has not laid out her own AI safety agenda. The only signal is a December 2025 letter she signed saying a freeze on state AI laws would leave a regulatory vacuum, which implies she wants some AI protections in place.

evidence.title: Clarke-led letter from 44 House Democrats opposing an AI moratorium in the FY26 NDAA
evidence.quote: a moratorium would be wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed a letter arguing AI rules are needed and that wiping out state rules without federal ones would let Big Tech run unchecked.

tech_regulation.label: No public position found
tech_regulation.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026. I looked for statements or bills on Section 230, privacy law, kids online safety, app stores, or antitrust and found none; her criticism of Big Tech is about data center water use.

preemption.label: Let states regulate

evidence.title: Original cosponsor: H.R. 8031 GUARDRAILS Act
evidence.what_it_shows: The bill protects states' right to pass their own AI laws by blocking federal preemption.

evidence.quote: Congress should not freeze state and local AI safeguards, least of all when there are no meaningful federal protections in place.

data_centers.label: Build, with conditions
data_centers.summary: He wants more data centers built and says the US cannot afall behind on AI, but he ties that to renewable energy and admits data centers strain grids and use a lot of power. He has not backed ratepayer-protection bills or any moratorium.

evidence.title: Press release: Resident Commissioner highlights the importance of data centers for AI development (Natural Resources hearing on federal lands)
evidence.quote: Artificial Intelligence is not a toy. It’s not a trend. It’s a revolution on the scale of the personal computer, the internet, the smartphone-even the printing press. We cannot afford to fall behind
evidence.what_it_shows: At a House hearing he asked Congress to keep policies that help data centers expand, while pairing them with renewable power.

evidence.title: Same hearing statement: he quoted Ezra Klein on permitting bottlenecks
evidence.quote: Artificial Intelligence is not a toy. It’s not a trend. It’s a revolution on the scale of the personal computer, the internet, the smartphone-even the printing press. We cannot afford to fall behind

evidence.quote: pointing to the strain data centers have been placing on grids in the continental U.S.
evidence.what_it_shows: Reporter's summary: he acknowledged trade-offs between AI and energy, naming data center load on mainland grids, while still pushing AI for Puerto Rico's grid rebuild.

evidence.title: Press release: Hernández meets OpenAI CEO Sam Altman
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence consumes enormous amounts of electricity and will, out of necessity, drive the development of new energy technologies
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI's huge power demand as a driver of new renewable energy that could stabilize Puerto Rico's electricity costs, rather than as a reason to slow down.

evidence.title: H.R. 7697, International AI Energy Grid Modernization Strategy Act

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: He is an enthusiastic AI adopter who says Puerto Rico must not be a bystander, but he pairs that with calls for responsible development, patient privacy, protecting artists, and one AI robocall disclosure rule. He has not backed binding safety testing, licensing, liability, or a pause, and has not opposed regulation either. A fact-checker adjusted this reading: Every ai_risk source is pro-adoption with only soft 'responsible' language: a study bill, grant programs, meeting reflections with no proposed rule, and 'Puerto Rico cannot be a passive bystander'. Nothing in the sources

evidence.title: Press release: Hernández introduces AI grid legislative package (H.R. 7696 and H.R. 7697)
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence gives us new tools to defend these systems, strengthen its resilience, and modernize how our energy infrastructure operates, but it must be developed responsibly.
evidence.what_it_shows: His framing is pro-adoption with a soft 'responsible' caveat and no specific rules attached.

evidence.title: Press release: Hernández and Ted Lieu introduce H.R. 7064, AI in Health Care Efficiency and Study Act
evidence.quote: This legislation takes a responsible approach to exploring how artificial intelligence can help ease that burden, improve system efficiency, and at the same time safeguard the privacy and security of patients’ medical information.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants AI used in health care and asks only for a study with privacy safeguards, not mandates.

evidence.title: Press release: Hernández meets OpenAI CEO Sam Altman

evidence.title: Press release: Hernández meets OpenAI CEO Sam Altman (on jobs)

evidence.title: Press release: $2 million federal grant for an AI project at Atenas University

data_centers.label: Mixed
data_centers.summary: Mixed. Moore cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act, saying data centers rather than families must pay for new power infrastructure, and he voiced Tucker County residents' frustration that state law removed local approval. But he voted for the SPEED Act permitting overhaul, applauds a new coal plant to power AI and data centers, and says he understands the need to expedite projects for the AI race with China.

evidence.title: Press release: Congressman Riley M. Moore cosponsors legislation to protect ratepayers from data center costs
evidence.quote: The Ratepayer Protection Act preserves state and local control over data center projects while ensuring that hardworking Americans are not asked to pay for hundreds of millions of dollars in new generation, transmission, or distribution infrastructure costs.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants data center companies, not ratepayers, to cover grid upgrade costs, and stresses state and local control.

evidence.title: H.R.9340 Ratepayer Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Cosponsor of the main House bill to keep data center power costs off household electric bills.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Moore on Tucker County residents and the state data center law
evidence.quote: The locals aren't particularly happy because there's not local input. They can say something, but there's not an approval or disapproval process at the local level,
evidence.what_it_shows: He acknowledges constituents' loss of local control under the state microgrid law.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Moore on why the state expedited data centers
evidence.quote: Part of that reasoning was the critical nature of data centers and the AI race between us and China, and the necessity to expedite these projects, which I certainly can understand.
evidence.what_it_shows: He accepts the case for fast-tracking data centers even while relaying local frustration; his office had not been in contact with the opposition group Tucker United.

evidence.title: Press release: Moore applauds DOE selection of TerraSpark Energy Campus coal plant
evidence.quote: As electricity demand continues to rise from advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence, and data center development, projects like TerraSpark will help ensure the United States has the reliable baseload power necessary to remain globally competitive
evidence.what_it_shows: He champions new coal-fired generation explicitly to power the AI and data center buildout.

evidence.title: House roll call 356: H.R. 4776 SPEED Act permitting reform (Yea)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted for the NEPA permitting overhaul backers tie to building power for AI data centers. Recorded vote: Yea.

ai_risk.label: Light touch
ai_risk.summary: No statements on AI safety rules were found. He frames AI as a race with China, and the AI industry super PAC Leading the Future named him one of its first House GOP Champions in April 2026, describing the group as members who have engaged with the industry. That points to a light-touch, innovation-first posture, but he has not said so directly.

evidence.title: Breitbart: Leading the Future super PAC releases list of House GOP Champions, including Riley Moore
evidence.quote: We're proud to support these conservative leaders who understand the importance of keeping the United States the global leader in AI innovation.
evidence.what_it_shows: The industry-funded AI super PAC backs him as an ally of its innovation-first agenda.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Moore frames data centers around the AI race with China
evidence.quote: Part of that reasoning was the critical nature of data centers and the AI race between us and China, and the necessity to expedite these projects, which I certainly can understand.
evidence.what_it_shows: His AI framing is competition with China rather than safety risk.
